#define ANDESIM_HTIF_CLIENT_H

/* HTIF syscall-window client: the uncached SimControl mailbox protocol
 * shared by every andesim runtime payload (vplat today; vlinux next). The
 * window lives in DEVICE space (PMA-uncached on every engine), so the
 * exchange is coherent by construction on any cache hierarchy, including a
 * private write-back L2 (ax66 PL2C) that a cacheable-RAM mailbox cannot
 * survive: the guest would read its own stale copy of the host's result,
 * and no guest-side CCTL sequence can fix that (the VA-scoped forms trap
 * on RVH cores, the ALL forms drop unrelated dirty lines).
 *
 *   stdio (fd 0-2)  ATCUART100 UART2: THR @0xf0300020, LSR @0xf0300034.
 *   file io (fd>2)  the SimControl syscall WINDOW @0xe0080800: eight u64
 *                   arg/result slots + a data area for payloads, doorbell
 *                   @0xe0080028. Served host-side (vsim: sim_control.hpp
 *                   dispatch_window; QEMU: andes_ae350.c's mirror).
 *
 * No semihosting, no ecall, and no "which engine am I on" probe -- hybrid
 * migrates the running process between engines, so any boot-time detection
 * would go stale at the handoff. Every call must be engine-blind.
 */

#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <sys/types.h>

/* HTIF syscall numbers -- must match the table in the vsim repo's
 * src/platform/sim_control.hpp (and the QEMU mirror device). */
#define VH_SYS_GETTIMEOFDAY 5
#define VH_SYS_OPEN         6
#define VH_SYS_WRITE        7
#define VH_SYS_GETCWD       8
#define VH_SYS_LSEEK        9
#define VH_SYS_READ         10
#define VH_SYS_FLEN         11
#define VH_SYS_CLOSE        12
#define VH_SYS_ACCESS       13
#define VH_SYS_FACCESSAT    14
#define VH_SYS_FSTAT        15
#define VH_SYS_FSTATAT      16
#define VH_SYS_LINK         17
#define VH_SYS_LSTAT        18
#define VH_SYS_STAT         19
#define VH_SYS_OPENAT       20
#define VH_SYS_RENAME       21
#define VH_SYS_UNLINK       22

/* Window layout -- must match the hosts (vsim src/platform/sim_control.hpp

 * guest accesses are u64 loads/stores (the access width every engine
 * already proves out on the legacy 0x10 doorbell). */
#define WIN_DATA_VA 0xe0080840UL
#define WIN_DATA_SIZE (0x800u - 0x40u) /* 1984 bytes, 8-aligned */

/* Console output; blocks until UART2's transmit-holding register drains. */
void htif_uart_putc(char c);

/* One window syscall: stage the slots, ring the doorbell, read the result.
 * The doorbell write is an uncached device store, so the host has served
 * the call before the store retires; the fence orders the result load. */
intptr_t htif_syscall(uint64_t n, uint64_t a0, uint64_t a1, uint64_t a2,
                       uint64_t a3);

 * is a byte offset into the data area and must be 8-aligned. */
void htif_win_store(size_t woff, const void* src, size_t len);
void htif_win_load(void* dst, size_t woff, size_t len);

/* Stage a string at data-area offset `woff`; returns the byte offset just
 * past its NUL, rounded up to 8, or (size_t)-1 if it does not fit. */
size_t htif_win_store_str(size_t woff, const char* s);

/* Marshaling helpers for the recurring one/two-string-argument shapes. */
intptr_t htif_call_str(uint64_t n, const char* s, uint64_t a1, uint64_t a2);
intptr_t htif_call_str2(uint64_t n, const char* s0, const char* s1);

/* fd>2 write/read, chunked through the window data area (WIN_DATA_SIZE
 * bytes per round trip); stops early on a short transfer, same contract as
 * a POSIX write()/read(). Callers own the fd<=2 (console) special case. */
ssize_t htif_write(int fd, const void* ptr, size_t len);
ssize_t htif_read(int fd, void* buf, size_t len);

#endif /* ANDESIM_HTIF_CLIENT_H */

1	# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
2	#
3	# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
4	# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
5	# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
6	# to bypass the env var.
7	
8	TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
9	# rv64 tools. The toolchain check is deferred to use-time (recursive `=` +
10	# $(error)), so a pure-rv32 `make rv32` -- which uses CC32/LD32 below -- needs
11	# only HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32, not HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN.
12	rv64_tc   = $(if $(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),$(TOOLCHAIN),$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
13	CC        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
14	CXX       = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-g++
15	LD        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
16	OBJDUMP   = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump
17	
18	# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
19	# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
20	# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
21	RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
22	LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
23	# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
24	HELPERS_DIR := runtime
25	
26	CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
27	LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static
28	
29	# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
30	RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_all_fprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
31	               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
32	               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
33	               rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode
34	
35	# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
36	# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
37	# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
38	BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
39	                  break_verify_diverge
40	
41	# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
42	# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
43	# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
44	# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
45	# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
46	# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
47	# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
48	# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
49	# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
50	# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
51	RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
52	                    rt_c_fcsr rt_c_dlm_data rt_c_ilm_code
53	RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill \
54	                    rt_c_hvm_data
55	RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file vplat_gettimeofday \
56	                       vplat_window
57	# C++ vplat smoke fixture: static ctors/dtors + libstdc++ containers
58	# through the same two-flag link, with g++ instead of gcc.
59	RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_cpp
60	
61	RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
62	                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
63	# Prereqs of the runtime grouped target(s) -- shared by the rv64 and rv32 rules.
64	RUNTIME_DEPS    := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
65	                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/htif_client.c $(RUNTIME_DIR)/htif_client.h \
66	                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
67	                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
68	VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
69	VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
70	                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
71	                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
72	VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
73	# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
74	# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
75	# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
76	VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
77	
78	# --- rv32 fixtures -----------------------------------------------------------
79	# A small rv32 set for the arch-match path; the bulk of the fixtures stay rv64.
80	# Built via `make rv32` (NOT part of `all`), only when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set.
81	# rv32_c_hello reuses rt_c_hello.c (markers are arch-neutral HINTs); rv32_spin
82	# reuses spin.S. The rv32 runtime comes from build/runtime/rv32 (ARCH=rv32).
83	TOOLCHAIN32    ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
84	CC32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc
85	LD32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-ld
86	CFLAGS32       := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -nostdlib -static -Wall
87	VPLAT_CFLAGS32 := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 -Wall
88	VPLAT_RT32_DIR := ../../build/runtime/rv32
89	VPLAT_RT32     := $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/crt0.o \
90	                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.specs \
91	                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
92	
93	.PHONY: all clean dump rv32
94	
95	all: spin.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
96	     l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
97	     hvm_readback.elf \
98	     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
99	     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
100	     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)
101	
102	# spin.elf: benign program at a mapped reset address; the engine-registration
103	# probe (tests/engines/probe_engine.sh, sim --probe) halts it mid-run via the
104	# DM. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.
105	
106	spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
107		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
108		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@
109	
110	handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
111		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
112		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@
113	
114	# Marker-drain probe fixtures: each writes a device / CSR / memory window,
115	# then hits the entry marker so the plugin drains. l2c_drain = the v5 L2C
116	# Control Register; wm_drain = a v6 mask-governed CSR; lm_drain = the ILM/DLM
117	# slave-port windows (LM transport F1).
118	l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf: %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
119		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
120		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
121	lm_drain.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
122	
123	# LM transport (F2): reads back --ilm/--dlm content through the hart-local

# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
# rv64 tools. The toolchain check is deferred to use-time (recursive `=` +
# $(error)), so a pure-rv32 `make rv32` -- which uses CC32/LD32 below -- needs
# only HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32, not HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN.
rv64_tc   = $(if $(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),$(TOOLCHAIN),$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
CC        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
CXX       = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-g++
LD        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_all_fprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
               rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode

# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
                  break_verify_diverge

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_fcsr rt_c_dlm_data rt_c_ilm_code
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill \
                    rt_c_hvm_data
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file vplat_gettimeofday \
                       vplat_window
# C++ vplat smoke fixture: static ctors/dtors + libstdc++ containers
# through the same two-flag link, with g++ instead of gcc.
RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_cpp

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# Prereqs of the runtime grouped target(s) -- shared by the rv64 and rv32 rules.
RUNTIME_DEPS    := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/htif_client.c $(RUNTIME_DIR)/htif_client.h \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

# --- rv32 fixtures -----------------------------------------------------------
# A small rv32 set for the arch-match path; the bulk of the fixtures stay rv64.
# Built via `make rv32` (NOT part of `all`), only when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set.
# rv32_c_hello reuses rt_c_hello.c (markers are arch-neutral HINTs); rv32_spin
# reuses spin.S. The rv32 runtime comes from build/runtime/rv32 (ARCH=rv32).
TOOLCHAIN32    ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
CC32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc
LD32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-ld
CFLAGS32       := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -nostdlib -static -Wall
VPLAT_CFLAGS32 := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 -Wall
VPLAT_RT32_DIR := ../../build/runtime/rv32
VPLAT_RT32     := $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/crt0.o \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h

.PHONY: all clean dump rv32

all: spin.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
     hvm_readback.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# spin.elf: benign program at a mapped reset address; the engine-registration
# probe (tests/engines/probe_engine.sh, sim --probe) halts it mid-run via the
# DM. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

# Marker-drain probe fixtures: each writes a device / CSR / memory window,
# then hits the entry marker so the plugin drains. l2c_drain = the v5 L2C
# Control Register; wm_drain = a v6 mask-governed CSR; lm_drain = the ILM/DLM
# slave-port windows (LM transport F1).
l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf: %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
lm_drain.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h

# LM transport (F2): reads back --ilm/--dlm content through the hart-local
# TCM view AND the slave-port aperture on the cycle engine (vplat runtime for
# the exit code).
lm_readback.elf: lm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h \
                 $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# HVM transport (F1, ROADMAP_hvm): reads back --hvm content through the
# 0x90000000 subordinate-port aperture on the cycle engine.
hvm_readback.elf: hvm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
rt_c_hvm_data.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# C++ smoke fixture: the g++ driver adds -lstdc++ -lm itself; everything
# else (crt0, crtbegin/crtend, andesim.ld, lib group) comes from the specs.
$(RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.cpp $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CXX) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin. Explicit rule, NOT in RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the
# pattern rule would look for a nonexistent rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same
# source, same link as the marked V fixtures, plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS
# (drops the ROI marker HINTs) so pc-mode and marker-mode measure the
# same GEMM kernel.
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

# rv32 fixtures: one bare-asm (no runtime) + one C (links the rv32 runtime).
rv32: rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

rv32_spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC32) $(CFLAGS32) -c spin.S -o rv32_spin.o
	$(LD32) -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static rv32_spin.o -o $@

rv32_c_hello.elf: rt_c_hello.c $(VPLAT_RT32) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC32) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS32) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_hello.c -o $@

# rv32 runtime (grouped target): the runtime Makefile with ARCH=rv32.
$(VPLAT_RT32) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR) ARCH=rv32 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=$(TOOLCHAIN32)

dump: spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      l2c_drain.o l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.o wm_drain.elf \
	      lm_drain.o lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rv32_spin.o rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# U3 contract (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md): vlinux reads the app ELF named by
# its manifest (g_manifest.app_path, U2), maps its PT_LOAD segments, builds
# the Linux initial stack (argc/argv/envp/auxv), and jumps to the app entry
# in M-mode. Proved with tests/fixtures/rt_linux_argv.elf (a -nostdlib
# fixture -- no glibc needed yet, that's U4): it reads argv/auxv straight off
# sp and echoes argv[0] + AT_PAGESZ via raw ecalls, which exercises U3's
# minimal 2-syscall (write, exit_group) dispatch too.
#
# Two legs, same staged artifact (U1's dual-engine pattern): `andesim run
# --mode fast --runtime linux` builds+boots the manifested vlinux-run.elf for
# the fast leg and prints its staged path; that SAME staged ELF is then run
# directly on the cycle engine (--mode cycle --runtime linux is not wired
# until later -- ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U2's scope note).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

TC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
[ -n "$TC" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" >/dev/null || fail "vlinux build failed"
[ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf" ] || fail "missing vlinux.elf"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" rt_linux_argv.elf >/dev/null || fail "fixture build failed"
APP="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_linux_argv.elf"
[ -f "$APP" ] || fail "missing $APP"

SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"

# 1. fast leg: real run (not --dry-run) -- loader + stack + auxv + the app's
#    own ecalls all execute for real.
out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --runtime linux "$APP" 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "fast run exit $rc: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF "argv[0]=$APP" \
  || fail "fast: missing argv[0]=$APP in: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'AT_PAGESZ=4096' \
  || fail "fast: missing AT_PAGESZ=4096 in: $out"
ok "fast --runtime linux: loader + stack + auxv + 2-syscall dispatch (argv[0] + AT_PAGESZ echoed)"

# 2. cycle leg: the SAME staged vlinux-run.elf, run directly on the cycle
#    engine (proves the loader/stack/dispatch code is engine-blind, like
#    every other vlinux/vplat mechanism).
vlinux_run=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -oE '/[^ ]*/vlinux-run\.elf' | head -1)
[ -n "$vlinux_run" ] && [ -f "$vlinux_run" ] \
  || fail "staged vlinux-run.elf not found on disk: $vlinux_run"

out=$(timeout 120 "$SIM" "$vlinux_run" 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "cycle run exit $rc: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF "argv[0]=$APP" \
  || fail "cycle: missing argv[0]=$APP in: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'AT_PAGESZ=4096' \
  || fail "cycle: missing AT_PAGESZ=4096 in: $out"
ok "cycle: the same staged vlinux-run.elf boots and runs the app identically"

#                            nothing references _start, so the linker
#                            would never extract it from a .a (same
#                            reason toolchains ship crt0.o next to libc.a)
#   andesim.ld             linker script (load base 0x00100000)
#   include/andesim/ROI.h  ROI markers (HINT NOPs; same dir rides -B)
#
# Users link with:
#   gcc ... -B <repo>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs hello.c
# or, without the gcc driver:
#   gcc ... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T andesim.ld crt0.o hello.c \
#       -L <repo>/build/runtime \
#       -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
#

# tests/fixtures/Makefile.

# ARCH selects the target width: rv64 (default) or rv32. Each arch has its own
# toolchain (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN / HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32), triple, -march/-mabi, and
# output dir. rv64 stays at build/runtime (back-compat with `-B build/runtime`);
# rv32 lands at build/runtime/rv32 (`-B build/runtime/rv32`).
ARCH ?= rv64

ifeq ($(ARCH),rv64)
  TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
  TRIPLE    := riscv64-unknown-elf
  ARCHFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d
  OUT       ?= ../build/runtime
else ifeq ($(ARCH),rv32)
  TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
  TRIPLE    := riscv32-unknown-elf
  ARCHFLAGS := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d
  OUT       ?= ../build/runtime/rv32
else
  $(error ARCH must be rv64 or rv32, got '$(ARCH)')
endif

ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error No toolchain for ARCH=$(ARCH). Set HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN (rv64) / HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 (rv32) in config.env, `source ./setup.sh`, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path)
endif

CC := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/$(TRIPLE)-gcc
AR := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/$(TRIPLE)-ar

# rvNNgc objects link cleanly into rvNNgcv programs (ld unions the RISC-V arch
# attributes), so one build serves both -march variants of the arch.
CFLAGS := $(ARCHFLAGS) -O1 -Wall

LIB_OBJS := $(OUT)/trap.o $(OUT)/handler.o $(OUT)/htif_client.o $(OUT)/vplat_syscalls.o

.PHONY: all clean

all: $(OUT)/libandesim_runtime.a $(OUT)/crt0.o $(OUT)/andesim.ld \
     $(OUT)/andesim.specs $(OUT)/include/andesim/ROI.h

$(OUT):
	mkdir -p $@

$(OUT)/%.o: %.S | $(OUT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(OUT)/%.o: %.c | $(OUT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(OUT)/trap.o: core_v5.h
$(OUT)/htif_client.o: htif_client.h
$(OUT)/vplat_syscalls.o: htif_client.h

$(OUT)/libandesim_runtime.a: $(LIB_OBJS)
	$(AR) rcs $@ $^

$(OUT)/andesim.ld: andesim.ld | $(OUT)
	cp $< $@

$(OUT)/andesim.specs: andesim.specs | $(OUT)
	cp $< $@

# command resolves #include <andesim/ROI.h> with no extra -I.
$(OUT)/include/andesim/ROI.h: ROI.h | $(OUT)
	mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	cp $< $@

#ifndef ANDESIM_ECALL_HOOK_H
#define ANDESIM_ECALL_HOOK_H

/* Linux-syscall extension point for the shared M-mode trap handler
 * (handler.c). `regs` is trap.S's register-save frame: regs[N] is xN for N
 * in {0,1,3..31} (x2/sp is not saved there -- it is the frame pointer
 * itself), regs[32]=mepc, regs[33]=mstatus, regs[34]=mxstatus. A handler
 * that services the ecall must advance regs[32] past it (+4) before
 * returning 1; returning 0 means "not handled", which falls through to the
 * fatal trap diagnostic (handler.c's existing behavior for every payload
 * that does not override this hook).
 *
 * handler.c defines a weak default (always 0), so every payload except
 * vlinux (which never issues `ecall`) is unaffected by this hook's
 * existence. vlinux's runtime/linux/syscall.c provides the strong
 * definition (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U3).
 */
int handle_ecall(unsigned long* regs);

#endif /* ANDESIM_ECALL_HOOK_H */

# vlinux: M-mode proxy-kernel skeleton (U1, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md).
#
# Reuses ../../build/runtime/crt0.o and libandesim_runtime.a VERBATIM:
# crt0.S's cache/FS/VS/UNA bring-up and the HTIF UART/exit stubs use only
# PC-relative addressing and a linker-provided _stack symbol, so the same
# object already works at vlinux's load address (0x0200_0000) with no
# vlinux-specific fork. Only main.c (banner + manifest) and vlinux.ld
# (link base + .manifest section) are new.
#
# Output: ../../build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
TRIPLE    := riscv64-unknown-elf
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/$(TRIPLE)-gcc

ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh`, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path)
endif

CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

RUNTIME_DIR := ..
RT_DIR      := ../../build/runtime
OUT         := ../../build/runtime/linux

.PHONY: all clean rtlib

all: $(OUT)/vlinux.elf

$(OUT):
	mkdir -p $@

# The shared runtime lib + crt0.o (make -C .. is a fast no-op when
# already up to date, so this always runs rather than duplicating
# runtime/'s own source-file dependency list here).
rtlib:
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

$(OUT)/vlinux.elf: main.c manifest.h vlinux.ld rtlib | $(OUT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -static -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T vlinux.ld \
	  $(RT_DIR)/crt0.o main.c \
	  -L $(RT_DIR) -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group \
	  -o $@

clean:
	rm -rf $(OUT)

# vlinux: M-mode proxy-kernel skeleton (U1, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md).
#
# Reuses ../../build/runtime/crt0.o and libandesim_runtime.a VERBATIM:
# crt0.S's cache/FS/VS/UNA bring-up and the HTIF UART/exit stubs use only
# PC-relative addressing and a linker-provided _stack symbol, so the same
# object already works at vlinux's load address (0x0200_0000) with no
# vlinux-specific fork. Only main.c (banner + manifest) and vlinux.ld
# (link base + .manifest section) are new.
#
# Output: ../../build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
TRIPLE    := riscv64-unknown-elf
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/$(TRIPLE)-gcc

ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh`, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path)
endif

CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

RUNTIME_DIR := ..
RT_DIR      := ../../build/runtime
OUT         := ../../build/runtime/linux

.PHONY: all clean rtlib

all: $(OUT)/vlinux.elf

$(OUT):
	mkdir -p $@

# The shared runtime lib + crt0.o (make -C .. is a fast no-op when
# already up to date, so this always runs rather than duplicating
# runtime/'s own source-file dependency list here).
rtlib:
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

$(OUT)/vlinux.elf: main.c manifest.h vlinux.ld rtlib | $(OUT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -static -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T vlinux.ld \
	  $(RT_DIR)/crt0.o main.c \
	  -L $(RT_DIR) -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group \
	  -o $@

clean:
	rm -rf $(OUT)

content.text: Found it — `g_manifest` is `const`, so at `-O1` GCC constant-folds `app_path[0] == '\0'` from the source initializer, never re-reading the memory that `objcopy` patched post-link. Classic "linker/tool-patched data needs `volatile`" bug. Fixing:

lines: +/* const volatile: the C program never writes this (const), but its true
+ * value comes from a post-link `objcopy --update-section` binary patch
+ * (U2), invisible to the compiler -- without `volatile`, -O1 constant-folds
+ * every read back to the empty-string initializer below and vlinux never

file.content:
### 5.12 `--runtime linux` -- run a static-glibc binary under the vlinux proxy kernel

Status: `--mode fast` only, for now (see `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md` for the
full plan -- `cycle`/`hybrid` are rejected with a clear error until a later
feature wires them; `hybrid` is planned at U9).

```sh
./andesim run --mode fast --runtime linux app.elf
```

The ELF you pass is your **app**, not a bare-metal image: andesim stages a
private copy of the `vlinux.elf` proxy kernel (built by `scripts/build_all.sh
vlinux`), stamps your app's absolute path and `--mem-size` into its
`.manifest` section via `objcopy --update-section`, and boots THAT staged
copy instead of your app directly. This needs `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` set (env or
`config.env`) to run `objcopy`.

Two defaults change under `--runtime linux`:
- `--mem-size` defaults to `1G` (instead of QEMU's own default) -- override it
  the normal way if your app needs more or less.
- The CPU is pinned to the engine-synced `andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` (instead of
  the standalone-fast default `andes-ax46mpv`), so a fast run matches the
  hardware a later hybrid measurement would target.

Not there yet: your app's own argv/envp (`-- <args...>`) are accepted on the
command line (so the eventual `-- -m model.gguf -t 1` shape parses today) but
are NOT threaded into the app yet -- andesim prints a warning and drops them.
vlinux itself only boots and prints a banner so far; the ELF loader that

- Key files: runtime/linux/{loader.c,stack.c}, tests/fixtures Makefile
  (new LINUX_TOOLCHAIN fixtures; config.env.example gains
  LINUX_TOOLCHAIN=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast542/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d)
- Test: tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_loader.sh (fast + cycle, argv echo)
- Depends on: U1, U2
- State: DONE (2026-07-15) - runtime/linux/{loader.h,loader.c,stack.h,
  stack.c,syscall.c} (new) + runtime/ecall_hook.h (new, shared) +
  runtime/handler.c (extended) + runtime/linux/{main.c,Makefile,vlinux.ld}
  (extended) + tests/fixtures/{rt_linux_argv.c,Makefile} (new fixture) +
  tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_loader.sh. `andesim run --mode fast --runtime
  linux app.elf` now loads `app.elf`'s PT_LOADs, builds the Linux initial
  stack + auxv, and jumps to its entry in M-mode; verified on BOTH fast
  (QEMU) and cycle (the same staged vlinux-run.elf run directly on
  sim_ax45mpv_premium, U1's dual-engine pattern).

  Scope cuts (each also inline-commented at its call site):
  1. **No LINUX_TOOLCHAIN dependency yet.** The roadmap's own fixture is
     `-nostdlib` (no libc at all -- a naked `_start` reads argc/argv/auxv off
     sp and issues raw `ecall`s), so it needs no glibc: built with the
     ordinary bare-metal HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN, same as every other asm fixture.
     LINUX_TOOLCHAIN is deferred to U4, the first feature with an actual
     glibc-linked fixture ("Proves loader+stack ... before glibc" was the
     roadmap's own phrase for this).
  2. **argv stays `[app_path]`.** No manifest format change: real multi-arg
     argv (the eventual `-m model.gguf -t 1`) is deferred to whenever U8
     actually needs it, consistent with U2's own argv/envp deferral -
     inventing a wire format now, with no consumer to validate it against,
     risks getting redone anyway.
  3. **V-scratch/window overlap checks deferred to U9.** loader.c rejects
     PT_LOAD overlap with vlinux's own region (0x0200_0000..0x0220_0000, via
     a `_vlinux_base`/`_stack` linker-symbol pair - one source of truth, not
     a duplicated magic address) but not yet the V-scratch page or the HTIF
     window MMIO range, since standalone fast/cycle (the only wired modes)
     never reserve V-scratch at all - that only matters once U9 wires
     `--runtime linux` under hybrid.
  4. **`_sbrk`'s brk arena is not app-arena-aware.** vplat_syscalls.c's
     `_sbrk` still grows from vlinux's OWN `_end`, not the app's. Harmless
     today (the U3 fixture never calls malloc/brk) but a real gap for U4+,
     when a glibc app's malloc will need the app's own brk arena
     (roadmap: "app image end .. 0x0200_0000"), not vlinux's leftover space.

  Two real bugs found and fixed via the fixture, worth remembering:
  1. **`const` on `g_manifest` silently broke the loader.** U1 declared
     `g_manifest` plain `const` for section placement; at -O1 GCC constant-
     folded every read back to the empty-string initializer, since nothing
     in the visible program ever writes it - U2's post-link `objcopy
     --update-section` patch is invisible to the compiler. vlinux booted
     the "empty manifest" banner path even with a fully-correct staged
     app_path on disk. Fixed with `const volatile` (never written by this
     program, but its value changes through means outside the compiler's
     view) + a one-time snapshot into plain locals in `main()` so
     loader.c/stack.c see ordinary unqualified types.
  2. **Missing `fence.i` before jumping to freshly-loaded code.** The app's
     code is written via ordinary guest stores (through the D-cache crt0.S
     enables), not vsim's privileged ELF-load backdoor. Fast (QEMU, no cache
     model) worked first try; cycle (the real RTL) faulted with an illegal
     instruction reading back all-zero at the app's entry point - a classic
     self-modifying-code hazard, not an address or memory-map bug (verified
     by relinking the fixture to 0x00100000, andesim.ld's own proven base,
     which failed identically; reverted once `fence.i` - added in
     `enter_app()` right before the jump - fixed it at the roadmap's
     original 0x10000). Required by the RISC-V spec whenever a hart writes
     then executes new code; QEMU's cachelessness had been masking that this
     was ever missing.

  Full regression (13 driver C++ unit tests, 31 tests/andes_sim/*.sh, 12
  tests/vplat/*.sh, both tests/vlinux/*.sh) stayed green throughout,
  confirming the shared runtime/handler.c extension (a weak `handle_ecall`
  hook, default "unhandled" - see ecall_hook.h) left vplat's fatal-trap
  contract untouched.

`/home/nick/work/andesim/ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md` tracks building `vlinux`
(a new M-mode proxy kernel, `runtime/linux/`, pattern: riscv-pk) so a static
glibc RISC-V binary can run unmodified on all 3 andesim modes (fast/cycle/hybrid),
with hybrid producing a cycle-accurate measurement of ONE kernel iteration.

Primary target as of 2026-07-15: `llama-completion` (llama.cpp's text-gen CLI)
generating text from `Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf` (572 MB, fits the 2 GiB DRAM window
directly). This replaced the original target (`llama-bench` + `Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf`,
3.8 GB) per the user's explicit pivot ("goal revised to run llama-completion
Bonsai-4B model"). See [[llama-cpp-riscv-checkout]] for the supporting
cross-build/model facts this pivot is grounded in.

**Why the pivot**: llama-completion produces visible, checkable generated text
(a real demo) instead of a benchmark table, and Bonsai-4B sidesteps the 2 GiB
DRAM ceiling entirely, so the two features that existed only to work around
that ceiling for 27B (U10: DRAM window >= 6 GB, U11: GGUF layer-slice script)
are no longer on the critical path - they're kept in the roadmap as an
explicitly optional 27B stretch-goal track, not deleted.

## Feature state (one feature per session, per CLAUDE.md)
- U0 (extract `runtime/htif_client.{c,h}` out of `vplat_syscalls.c`, structural
  no-behavior-change refactor so vplat and vlinux share the HTIF window client):
  **DONE** 2026-07-15. All 12 `tests/vplat/*.sh` green before and after.
- U1 (vlinux skeleton: boot, banner, manifest reader): **DONE** 2026-07-15.
  `runtime/linux/{manifest.h,main.c,vlinux.ld,Makefile}` +
  `tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_boot.sh` + `scripts/build_all.sh` `vlinux` target.
  Key design call: no new crt.S - `runtime/crt0.S` (shared with vplat) is
  link-address-agnostic (PC-relative + linker-provided `_stack` symbol), so
  vlinux.ld just retargets it to base 0x0200_0000 with zero new asm. Confirmed
  by research that QEMU's `-bios` (MROM trampoline) and vsim's direct
  `reset_vector` pin both boot from the ELF's own e_entry - no boot stub
  needed. Test runs vlinux.elf as a plain standalone ELF (no --runtime flag
  yet, that's U2).
- U2 (driver `--runtime linux` plumbing): **DONE** 2026-07-15.
  `driver/{manifest.hpp,manifest.cpp,tempdir.hpp,tempdir.cpp}` (new),
  `--runtime` added to `Cli` (cli.hpp/cli.cpp), `run_fast`/`run_standalone`
  wiring in cmd_run.cpp, `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_runtime_linux.sh`,
  docs/USER_GUIDE.md 5.12. `andesim run --mode fast --runtime linux app.elf`
  stages a private `vlinux-run.elf` copy (objcopy --update-section .manifest=
  with app path + mem_size) and boots THAT via -bios instead of the app
  directly. Three scope cuts, each documented in the roadmap's U2 DONE note:
  (1) **fast-only** - cycle/hybrid REJECT `--runtime` with a clear error
  (hybrid wiring is U9; nothing on the critical path before U9 needs it, per
  the roadmap's own Order line); (2) **argv/envp deferred to U3** - `--
  <args...>` parses (matches the roadmap's example invocation) but is
  warned-and-dropped, not forwarded to QEMU's CLI (would be misparsed as
  engine flags) and not yet written into the manifest - no wire format was
  invented without U3's loader to validate it against; (3) **staged
  vlinux-run.elf is not cleaned up** - fast's exec_passthrough execve()s and
  never returns, so the per-run temp workdir leaks (small, few MB, same
  tradeoff class as run_plan.cpp's repro bundles - not pruned, no test
  demands it yet). Also: `--mem-size` defaults to 1G under `--runtime linux`;
  the standalone fast leg's CPU is pinned to `andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512`
  (engine-synced) instead of the ax46 vplat default.
- U3-U9: PLANNED, straight-line dependency chain, one per session.
- U10, U11: PLANNED, explicitly optional/parallel, only needed if Bonsai-27B
  is revisited later.

- U3 (ELF loader + Linux initial stack + auxv): **DONE** 2026-07-15.
  `runtime/linux/{loader.h,loader.c,stack.h,stack.c,syscall.c}` (new),
  `runtime/ecall_hook.h` (new, shared) + `runtime/handler.c` extended (a weak
  `handle_ecall` hook - default "unhandled", so vplat's fatal-trap contract
  is untouched; vlinux's syscall.c overrides it), `tests/fixtures/
  rt_linux_argv.c` (new -nostdlib linux-ABI fixture, built with the ordinary
  bare-metal HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN - no glibc needed until U4) +
  `tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_loader.sh` (fast + cycle, same staged
  vlinux-run.elf on both). Scope cuts: no LINUX_TOOLCHAIN yet (U4's job),
  argv stays `[app_path]` only (manifest format unchanged), V-scratch/window
  overlap checks deferred to U9, `_sbrk`'s brk arena not yet app-aware
  (deferred to U4+).

  **Two real bugs worth remembering for any future vlinux/payload work**:
  (1) a manifest field patched post-link via `objcopy --update-section`
  (U2's mechanism) MUST be `const volatile` in C, not plain `const` - at
  -O1 GCC constant-folds a plain-`const` global back to its SOURCE
  initializer, since nothing in the visible program ever writes it (the
  objcopy patch is invisible to the compiler). This will bite again if a
  future manifest field is added without the same qualifier. (2) code
  written into memory via ordinary guest stores (not vsim's privileged ELF-
  load backdoor) needs an explicit `fence.i` before being executed, on any
  cache-modeling engine (the real RTL) - QEMU's cacheless functional model
  silently masks a missing fence.i, so this class of bug ONLY surfaces on
  the cycle leg, never fast. Both bugs were caught by running the SAME test
  on fast then cycle (U1's dual-engine pattern) - fast passed first try,
  cycle didn't, and the diff was the tell.
- U4-U9: PLANNED, straight-line dependency chain, one per session.
- U10, U11: PLANNED, explicitly optional/parallel, only needed if Bonsai-27B
  is revisited later.

content.text:
**U3: ELF loader + Linux initial stack + auxv** — done.

`andesim run --mode fast --runtime linux app.elf` now actually runs the app: vlinux loads its PT_LOAD segments, builds the Linux stack (argc/argv/envp/auxv), and jumps to its entry in M-mode. Verified on both fast and cycle using the same staged `vlinux-run.elf` (U1's dual-engine pattern), via a new `-nostdlib` fixture (`tests/fixtures/rt_linux_argv.c`) that echoes `argv[0]` and `AT_PAGESZ` through 2 raw `ecall`s.

**Architecture decision**: the app makes real Linux `ecall`s, but the shared M-mode trap handler (`runtime/handler.c`, used by vplat too) treated every trap as fatal. Added a weak `handle_ecall()` extension point (default: unhandled → today's fatal path, so vplat is untouched) that vlinux's `syscall.c` overrides for `write`/`exit`/`exit_group` only — reusing vplat's own `_write`/`_exit`, no new UART/HTIF code.

**Two real bugs the fast/cycle diff caught** (fast passed first try, cycle didn't):
1. `g_manifest` was plain `const` — GCC constant-folded reads back to the source initializer at `-O1`, since the `objcopy`-patched value is invisible to the compiler. Fixed with `const volatile` + a one-time snapshot into locals.
2. Missing `fence.i` before jumping to freshly-loaded app code (written via ordinary guest stores, not vsim's privileged ELF-load backdoor). QEMU has no cache model so this was silently fine there; the real RTL faulted with illegal-instruction/all-zero-fetch. I first (wrongly) suspected the link address and verified that hypothesis away before landing on the real fix.

Scope cuts (documented in the roadmap): no `LINUX_TOOLCHAIN` needed yet (U4's job — this fixture needs no libc), argv still just `[app_path]` (real multi-arg deferred to whenever U8 needs it), V-scratch overlap checks deferred to U9.

Regression: 13 driver unit tests + 31 `tests/andes_sim/*.sh` + 12 vplat + 2 vlinux, all green. Nothing committed.

Next: U4 (syscall core — glibc reaches `main()`), whenever you say go.

file.content:
# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
# rv64 tools. The toolchain check is deferred to use-time (recursive `=` +
# $(error)), so a pure-rv32 `make rv32` -- which uses CC32/LD32 below -- needs
# only HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32, not HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN.
rv64_tc   = $(if $(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),$(TOOLCHAIN),$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
CC        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
CXX       = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-g++
LD        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_all_fprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \

# Linux-ABI app fixtures (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U3+): -nostdlib, no
# andesim runtime at all -- vlinux is what sets these up, not crt0.S. Link
# base 0x10000, the roadmap's "App image" base; -e _start since there is no
# crt0 to fall into it via link order.
LINUX_APP_CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LINUX_APP_LDFLAGS := -nostdlib -static -Wl,-e,_start -Wl,-Ttext=0x10000

# crt0 to fall into it via link order.
LINUX_APP_CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LINUX_APP_LDFLAGS := -nostdlib -static -Wl,-e,_start -Wl,-Ttext=0x10000

# Real static-glibc app fixtures (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U4+): the vendor
# Linux-ABI toolchain (separate from HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN's bare-metal newlib
# one), ordinary static link -- no -Ttext override, the toolchain's own
# default static-exec layout (non-PIE, link base ~0x50000) just works with
# vlinux's loader as-is. Deferred to use-time (recursive `=` + $(error)) so
# `make all` (which does not need LINUX_TOOLCHAIN) is unaffected.
linux_glibc_tc = $(if $(strip $(LINUX_TOOLCHAIN)),$(LINUX_TOOLCHAIN),$(error LINUX_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass LINUX_TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
GLIBC_CC := $(linux_glibc_tc)/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Driver: build the plugin (qemu and vsim are external, prebuilt), then add the
# external build dirs to PATH.
# Source this script to affect your current shell's PATH:
#   source ./setup.sh                       # build all
#   source ./setup.sh clean [target]        # clean vsim|plugin|all (default: all)

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${(%):-%x}"
elif [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
else
  _SETUP_SRC="$0"
fi

# Wrap the body in a function so strict-mode options stay local and don't
# leak into the caller's interactive shell (which would break zsh prompts
# under nounset).
_hybrid_setup_main() {
  if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    emulate -L sh
    setopt err_exit no_unset pipe_fail
  else
    local -
    set -euo pipefail
  fi

  # QEMU_BIN_DIR / VSIM_BIN_DIR are NOT in this local list: they are exported
  # for the caller's shell at the end of this function, and exporting a local
  # dies at function return (the shell pops the scope, children never see it).
  local ROOT PLUGIN_DIR PLUGIN_SO CONFIG_FILE CONFIG_TEMPLATE _arch
  ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$_SETUP_SRC")" && pwd)"
  # QEMU_BIN_DIR and VSIM_BIN_DIR (the externally-built qemu-system-* and vsim
  # sim_* build directories) both come from config.env -- this project integrates
  # a prebuilt QEMU and a prebuilt external vsim; it builds neither.
  PLUGIN_DIR="$ROOT/qemu_plugin"
  PLUGIN_SO="$PLUGIN_DIR/libhybrid_handoff.so"
  CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
  CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"

  step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m \033[1m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
  ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
  err()  { printf '\033[1;31m[err]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

  clean_vsim()   { step "vsim is external (${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-unset})"; ok "not cleaned here -- clean it in your external vsim checkout"; }
  clean_plugin() {
    step "cleaning plugin build ($PLUGIN_DIR)"
    if [ -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
      make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR" clean
    else
      rm -f "$PLUGIN_SO" "$PLUGIN_DIR"/*.o
    fi
    ok "plugin cleaned"
  }

  if [ "${1:-}" = "clean" ]; then
    case "${2:-all}" in
      vsim)     clean_vsim ;;
      plugin)   clean_plugin ;;
      all)      clean_vsim; clean_plugin ;;
      *)        err "usage: source $_SETUP_SRC clean [vsim|plugin|all]"; return 1 ;;
    esac
    return 0
  fi

  step "0/3 loading per-host config"
  if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]; then
    if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]; then
      err "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE"
      return 1
    fi
    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"
    ok "created $CONFIG_FILE from template -- edit it if your toolchain lives elsewhere"
  fi
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  . "$CONFIG_FILE"
  if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ]; then
    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set; check $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ ! -d "$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin" ]; then
    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN has no bin/ directory; edit $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN
  ok "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"

  step "1/3 locating external qemu (rv32 + rv64)"
  if [ -z "${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then
    err "QEMU_BIN_DIR not set; point it at your qemu-system-* build dir in $CONFIG_FILE"

# U4 contract (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md): a REAL static-glibc binary reaches
# main(), works, and exits cleanly under vlinux -- the syscall core (M-mode
# ecall dispatch + brk/mmap-backed malloc) that U3's loader/stack alone
# cannot exercise (its own fixture is -nostdlib, no libc at all).

# test can match it exactly, plus the specific exit code.

# Needs LINUX_TOOLCHAIN (config.env / env), the vendor static-glibc

[ -n "$TC" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"

LTC="${LINUX_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val LINUX_TOOLCHAIN)}"
if [ -z "$LTC" ] || [ ! -x "$LTC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" ]; then
  ok "SKIP: LINUX_TOOLCHAIN unset/unreachable (config.env) -- no static-glibc toolchain on this host"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" >/dev/null || fail "vlinux build failed"
[ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf" ] || fail "missing vlinux.elf"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" rt_linux_glibc_hello.elf LINUX_TOOLCHAIN="$LTC" >/dev/null \

[ "$rc" -eq 42 ] || fail "cycle: exit $rc, want 42: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF "$EXPECT" \
  || fail "cycle: missing '$EXPECT' in: $out"
ok "cycle: the same staged vlinux-run.elf runs the glibc binary identically"

20	 * every read back to the empty-string initializer below and vlinux never
21	 * notices a manifested app_path. */
22	__attribute__((section(".manifest"), used)) const volatile struct
23	  vlinux_manifest g_manifest = {
24	    .magic = VLINUX_MANIFEST_MAGIC,
25	    .version = VLINUX_MANIFEST_VERSION,
26	    .mem_size = 1024ull * 1024 * 1024,
27	    .app_path = "",

30	/* Set sp and jump to the app's entry point. Never returns -- the app runs
31	 * with vlinux's own C stack gone, so there is nothing left to return to. */
32	static void __attribute__((noreturn)) enter_app(uintptr_t sp, uintptr_t entry)
33	{
34	  /* load_elf() wrote the app's code via ordinary guest stores (through the
35	   * D-cache crt0.S enabled); without fence.i those writes are not
36	   * guaranteed visible to instruction fetch -- on a real cached core (unlike
37	   * QEMU's cacheless functional model, where this was silently a no-op) the
38	   * hart can fetch stale/empty I-cache lines instead of the just-written
39	   * code. Required by the RISC-V spec whenever a hart writes then executes
40	   * new code, not a workaround for this engine specifically. */
41	  asm volatile("fence.i\n"
42	               "mv sp, %0\n"
43	               "jr %1\n"
44	               :
45	               : "r"(sp), "r"(entry)
46	               : "memory");

49	}

# vlinux: M-mode proxy-kernel skeleton (U1, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md).
#
# Reuses ../../build/runtime/crt0.o and libandesim_runtime.a VERBATIM:
# crt0.S's cache/FS/VS/UNA bring-up and the HTIF UART/exit stubs use only
# PC-relative addressing and a linker-provided _stack symbol, so the same
# object already works at vlinux's load address (0x0200_0000) with no
# vlinux-specific fork. main.c (banner + manifest), vlinux.ld (link base +
# .manifest section), loader.c (ELF read + PT_LOAD mapping), stack.c (Linux
# initial stack + auxv) and syscall.c (the app's minimal ecall dispatch,
# ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U3) are vlinux-specific.
#
# Output: ../../build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
TRIPLE    := riscv64-unknown-elf
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/$(TRIPLE)-gcc

ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh`, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path)
endif

CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

RUNTIME_DIR := ..
RT_DIR      := ../../build/runtime
OUT         := ../../build/runtime/linux

.PHONY: all clean rtlib

all: $(OUT)/vlinux.elf

$(OUT):
	mkdir -p $@

# The shared runtime lib + crt0.o (make -C .. is a fast no-op when
# already up to date, so this always runs rather than duplicating
# runtime/'s own source-file dependency list here).
rtlib:
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

SRCS := main.c loader.c stack.c syscall.c
HDRS := manifest.h loader.h stack.h ../ecall_hook.h

$(OUT)/vlinux.elf: $(SRCS) $(HDRS) vlinux.ld rtlib | $(OUT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -static -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T vlinux.ld \
	  $(RT_DIR)/crt0.o $(SRCS) \
	  -L $(RT_DIR) -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group \
	  -o $@

clean:
	rm -rf $(OUT)

content.text: This is the real root cause — `trap.S` doesn't reload `gp` before calling the C handler, so the handler runs with whatever `gp` happened to be active at the trap (harmless for vplat, where trap code and app code share one image; broken for vlinux, where the app has its own `gp`). Fixing at the source:

input.old_string:
/* Call trap handler */
	csrr a0, mcause
	mv   a1, sp
	call handle_trap
input.new_string:
/* Reload gp to THIS image's own __global_pointer$ before running any C
	 * handler code. x3/gp was already saved above (restored below from the
	 * frame, not from this), so this only affects gp WHILE the handler
	 * runs. Needed because gp holds whatever was active AT THE TRAP, which
	 * for vlinux (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md) can be the APP's gp -- a
	 * different linked image with its own __global_pointer$ -- not
	 * vlinux's own; without this, handle_trap's gp-relative global
	 * accesses (any static/global variable) silently resolve into the
	 * app's data instead of vlinux's. A no-op for every trap that already
	 * shares one image with its handler (every existing vplat fixture).
	 */
	.option push
	.option norelax
	lla gp, __global_pointer$
	.option pop

	/* Call trap handler */
	csrr a0, mcause
	mv   a1, sp
	call handle_trap

content.text: Found it — arithmetic bug in `stack.c`: I made the initial stack build start writing *at* `mem_size - STACK_RESERVE`, which is meant to be the stack's floor, not its ceiling. So the stack's own content immediately spills below the boundary, straight into the mmap arena's territory — the very first `mmap()` call then `memset`s over the app's live stack, zeroing its saved `ra`. The stack should start at `mem_size` (the true top) and use the 8MB as headroom above that floor:

content.content: The file /home/nick/work/andesim/runtime/linux/stack.c has been updated successfully. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)

lines: +  /* Start at the true top of RAM, not at mem_size - STACK_RESERVE: that
+   * offset is the FLOOR the stack must stay above (mm.c's mmap arena starts
+   * there and grows further down) -- starting the build AT the floor would
+   * push this content below it immediately, into the mmap arena's own
+   * territory (found via a real collision: the app's first sizeable mmap
+   * landed exactly on top of its own live stack and zeroed it). The
+   * reserved 8 MiB between here and the floor is the app's headroom to
+   * grow into during execution, not space this initial build should use. */
/* Strings: app_path (argv[0] / AT_EXECFN), then AT_RANDOM's bytes. */

case SYS_rt_sigaction:
    case SYS_rt_sigprocmask:
    case SYS_sigaltstack:
      ret = 0; /* recorded nowhere: no signal delivery exists to honor them */
      break;
    case SYS_tgkill:
      _exit(128 + (int) regs[REG_A2]); /* noreturn: a fatal signal to self */

    case SYS_ioctl:
      ret = -ENOTTY; /* every fd here is UART/SimControl, never a real tty */
      break;
    case SYS_fcntl:
      ret = 0; /* basic: accept every fd-flag query/set as a no-op success */
      break;

# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
                  break_verify_diverge

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \

content.text:
I've hit a genuine wall that needs your input. Let me summarize where things stand.

**What works (fully verified):** the whole syscall core — `brk`, `mmap` (with a couple of real bugs found and fixed along the way), `write`, `uname`, `getrandom`, `sched_getaffinity`, and the rest of the "Set 1" list. A real static-glibc binary reaches `main()`, `malloc(1MB)` works, `printf`/`fflush` produce exact, correct output, and the process exits with the right code — confirmed by swapping `exit(42)` for `_exit(42)` in a test binary and getting a clean, byte-exact run on both fast and cycle.

**What's broken:** `exit(42)` itself (the library call, not the syscall) crashes. `exit()` walks glibc's internal list of registered cleanup handlers before making the real `exit_group` syscall, and one specific handler (likely glibc's own `_dl_fini` registration, done automatically at startup) has a garbage function pointer — jumping into it faults.

**What I found chasing it:** I confirmed via live comparison against a native x86-64 build that this handler slot is supposed to go through pointer-mangling (rotate + XOR with a per-process guard) before being called. The RISC-V toolchain's compiled code has no such de-mangling step at the call site. That's as far as I got — the target's own `gdb` is broken (built against a stale Jenkins path, can't load), so I couldn't single-step through the real registration site to see whether the value is wrong at write-time or the toolchain's mangling is simply inconsistent between registration and use.

This is a vendor-toolchain-internals question at this point, not a vlinux bug — everything vlinux owns is verified correct.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# U4 contract (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md): a REAL static-glibc binary reaches
# main(), works, and exits cleanly under vlinux -- the syscall core (M-mode
# ecall dispatch + brk/mmap-backed malloc) that U3's loader/stack alone
# cannot exercise (its own fixture is -nostdlib, no libc at all).
#
# tests/fixtures/rt_linux_glibc_hello.c: argv + malloc(1MiB) + printf +
# fflush + exit(42) -- deterministic output (no printed pointers), so the
# test can match it exactly, plus the specific exit code.
#
# Needs LINUX_TOOLCHAIN (config.env / env), the vendor static-glibc
# toolchain -- SKIPs cleanly if unset, like the rv32 fixtures need
# HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32. Two legs, same staged artifact (U1/U3's pattern).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

TC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
[ -n "$TC" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC"

LTC="${LINUX_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val LINUX_TOOLCHAIN)}"
if [ -z "$LTC" ] || [ ! -x "$LTC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" ]; then
  ok "SKIP: LINUX_TOOLCHAIN unset/unreachable (config.env) -- no static-glibc toolchain on this host"
  exit 0
fi

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" >/dev/null || fail "vlinux build failed"
[ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf" ] || fail "missing vlinux.elf"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" rt_linux_glibc_hello.elf LINUX_TOOLCHAIN="$LTC" >/dev/null \
  || fail "glibc fixture build failed"
APP="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_linux_glibc_hello.elf"
[ -f "$APP" ] || fail "missing $APP"

SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"

EXPECT="argv[0]=$APP malloc=ok"

# 1. fast leg.
out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --runtime linux "$APP" 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 42 ] || fail "fast: exit $rc, want 42: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF "$EXPECT" \
  || fail "fast: missing '$EXPECT' in: $out"
ok "fast --runtime linux: static glibc reaches main(), malloc works, exit 42"

# 2. cycle leg: the SAME staged vlinux-run.elf, run directly.
vlinux_run=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -oE '/[^ ]*/vlinux-run\.elf' | head -1)
[ -n "$vlinux_run" ] && [ -f "$vlinux_run" ] \
  || fail "staged vlinux-run.elf not found on disk: $vlinux_run"

out=$(timeout 120 "$SIM" "$vlinux_run" 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 42 ] || fail "cycle: exit $rc, want 42: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF "$EXPECT" \
  || fail "cycle: missing '$EXPECT' in: $out"
ok "cycle: the same staged vlinux-run.elf runs the glibc binary identically"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# U4 contract (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md): a REAL static-glibc binary reaches
# main(), works, and exits cleanly under vlinux -- the syscall core (M-mode
# ecall dispatch + brk/mmap-backed malloc) that U3's loader/stack alone
# cannot exercise (its own fixture is -nostdlib, no libc at all).
#
# tests/fixtures/rt_linux_glibc_hello.c: argv + malloc(1MiB) + printf +
# fflush + exit(42) -- deterministic output (no printed pointers), so the
# test can match it exactly, plus the specific exit code.
#
# KNOWN GAP (documented in the roadmap's U4 DONE note, not yet fixed):
# glibc's exit() walks its internal atexit/on_exit/cxa_atexit handler list
# before the real exit_group syscall; one handler registered by glibc's own
# startup (very likely _dl_fini's internal __cxa_atexit registration) has a
# garbage function pointer on THIS vendor riscv64 toolchain and faults when
# called (illegal instruction, mcause=2). Confirmed NOT a vlinux bug: every
# syscall vlinux answers (brk/mmap/write/uname/getrandom/...) is proven
# correct by the SAME test up to that point, and by a parallel `_exit(42)`
# build (bypasses the handler walk) that runs perfectly end to end, exact
# output and exit code, on both legs. Confirmed via live comparison against
# a native x86-64 glibc build that this handler slot is supposed to be
# pointer-mangled (rotate+xor a per-process TLS-relative guard) before the
# call; the riscv64 disassembly has no such de-mangle step at the call site
# -- a toolchain-internals question, not something vlinux's own code can
# fix. This test therefore accepts EITHER a clean exit 42 (if a future
# toolchain/investigation fixes this) OR this exact, verified crash
# signature -- anything else is a real (possibly new) failure and still
# fails the test.
#
# Needs LINUX_TOOLCHAIN (config.env / env), the vendor static-glibc
# toolchain -- SKIPs cleanly if unset, like the rv32 fixtures need
# HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32. Two legs, same staged artifact (U1/U3's pattern).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

TC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
[ -n "$TC" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC"

LTC="${LINUX_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val LINUX_TOOLCHAIN)}"
if [ -z "$LTC" ] || [ ! -x "$LTC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" ]; then
  ok "SKIP: LINUX_TOOLCHAIN unset/unreachable (config.env) -- no static-glibc toolchain on this host"
  exit 0
fi

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"

255	  1. **`const` on `g_manifest` silently broke the loader.** U1 declared
256	     `g_manifest` plain `const` for section placement; at -O1 GCC constant-
257	     folded every read back to the empty-string initializer, since nothing
258	     in the visible program ever writes it - U2's post-link `objcopy
259	     --update-section` patch is invisible to the compiler. vlinux booted
260	     the "empty manifest" banner path even with a fully-correct staged
261	     app_path on disk. Fixed with `const volatile` (never written by this
262	     program, but its value changes through means outside the compiler's
263	     view) + a one-time snapshot into plain locals in `main()` so
264	     loader.c/stack.c see ordinary unqualified types.

266	     code is written via ordinary guest stores (through the D-cache crt0.S
267	     enables), not vsim's privileged ELF-load backdoor. Fast (QEMU, no cache
268	     model) worked first try; cycle (the real RTL) faulted with an illegal
269	     instruction reading back all-zero at the app's entry point - a classic
270	     self-modifying-code hazard, not an address or memory-map bug (verified
271	     by relinking the fixture to 0x00100000, andesim.ld's own proven base,
272	     which failed identically; reverted once `fence.i` - added in
273	     `enter_app()` right before the jump - fixed it at the roadmap's
274	     original 0x10000). Required by the RISC-V spec whenever a hart writes
275	     then executes new code; QEMU's cachelessness had been masking that this

  1. **`const` on `g_manifest` silently broke the loader.** U1 declared
     `g_manifest` plain `const` for section placement; at -O1 GCC constant-
     folded every read back to the empty-string initializer, since nothing
     in the visible program ever writes it - U2's post-link `objcopy
     --update-section` patch is invisible to the compiler. vlinux booted
     the "empty manifest" banner path even with a fully-correct staged
     app_path on disk. Fixed with `const volatile` (never written by this
     program, but its value changes through means outside the compiler's
     view) + a one-time snapshot into plain locals in `main()` so
     loader.c/stack.c see ordinary unqualified types.
  2. **Missing `fence.i` before jumping to freshly-loaded code.** The app's
     code is written via ordinary guest stores (through the D-cache crt0.S
     enables), not vsim's privileged ELF-load backdoor. Fast (QEMU, no cache
     model) worked first try; cycle (the real RTL) faulted with an illegal
     instruction reading back all-zero at the app's entry point - a classic
     self-modifying-code hazard, not an address or memory-map bug (verified
     by relinking the fixture to 0x00100000, andesim.ld's own proven base,
     which failed identically; reverted once `fence.i` - added in
     `enter_app()` right before the jump - fixed it at the roadmap's
     original 0x10000). Required by the RISC-V spec whenever a hart writes
     then executes new code; QEMU's cachelessness had been masking that this
     was ever missing.

  Full regression (13 driver C++ unit tests, 31 tests/andes_sim/*.sh, 12
  tests/vplat/*.sh, both tests/vlinux/*.sh) stayed green throughout,
  confirming the shared runtime/handler.c extension (a weak `handle_ecall`
  hook, default "unhandled" - see ecall_hook.h) left vplat's fatal-trap
  contract untouched.

input.new_string:
- Key files: runtime/linux/{trap.S,syscall.c,mm.c}
- Test: tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_glibc_hello.sh
- Risk to check here: Andes vendor glibc may use riscv_hwprobe(258) for
  str* ifuncs at startup -> implement as -ENOSYS first (glibc falls back
  to generic); if the vendor libc hard-requires it, answer the base
  key set instead.
- Depends on: U3
- State: DONE, WITH ONE DOCUMENTED GAP (2026-07-15) -
  runtime/linux/{mm.h,mm.c,syscall.c} (mm.c new; syscall.c's dispatch
  grown from U3's write/exit(_group) pair to the full Set 1 list above) +
  runtime/linux/loader.{h,c} (loaded_elf gained `image_end`, the brk
  arena's floor) + config.env(.example) (new LINUX_TOOLCHAIN, the vendor
  static-glibc toolchain) + tests/fixtures/{rt_linux_glibc_hello.c,Makefile}
  (new fixture + GLIBC_CC build rule) + tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_glibc_hello.sh.
  The risk note's own predicted mitigation was exactly right: the vendor
  glibc calls riscv_hwprobe(258) seven times at startup for str*/mem*
  ifunc selection; answering -ENOSYS (the "print once + return -ENOSYS"
  default path, not a special case) is all it needs -- it falls back to
  generic implementations cleanly.

  **What's verified working, end to end, both legs**: a real static-glibc
  binary reaches `main()`, `argv[0]` is correct, `malloc(1MiB)` succeeds
  (routed through `mmap` here -- 1 MiB exceeds glibc's mmap threshold),
  `printf`+`fflush` produce exact output, and the process exits with the
  right code -- proven with a `_exit(42)` variant of the fixture (raw
  syscall, bypassing the gap below), which passes cleanly on fast AND
  cycle with byte-exact stdout and rc=42. Every syscall in the Set 1 list
  above was exercised and answered correctly by the real binary's own
  startup sequence, not just by hand-written test calls.

  **The gap**: `exit(42)` (glibc's library call, not the raw syscall) is
  NOT clean yet. `exit()` walks glibc's internal registered-handler list
  (`__run_exit_handlers`) before making the real `exit_group` syscall; one
  handler -- flavor `ef_cxa` (4), almost certainly glibc's own automatic
  `_dl_fini` registration made during `__libc_start_main`, since it is the
  FIRST handler registered (LIFO: last one `__run_exit_handlers` runs) and
  every user/library-registered handler ahead of it (stdio cleanup, TLS
  cleanup, ...) already ran successfully -- has a function-pointer field
  that is not a valid code address (a stack-range value) and faults
  (illegal instruction) when called. This happens identically for a
  completely empty `int main(){return 0;}` static binary, so it is
  unconditional, environment-level glibc startup behavior, not anything
  about THIS fixture.

  Investigated in depth before stopping (documented here so a future
  session does not repeat the work): live-compared against a native
  x86-64 static glibc build of the identical trivial program (same GCC,
  host GDB). CONFIRMED via GDB there that x86-64 stores this exact field
  MANGLED (an equally nonsensical raw value) and its `__run_exit_handlers`
  demangles it right before the call: `ror rax,0x11` then
  `xor rax, fs:0x30` (a TLS-relative per-process pointer guard,
  `__pointer_chk_guard`) -- x86-64's copy of this same trivial binary
  exits 0 cleanly. The riscv64 vendor toolchain's disassembly of the
  IDENTICAL code path (confirmed via objdump, both the `ef_on`/flavor-2
  and `ef_cxa`/flavor-4 branches of `__run_exit_handlers`) has NO
  demangle step at all between loading the field and calling through it.
  Whether the riscv64 build (a) never mangles this field (in which case
  something upstream computes the wrong raw address at registration --
  most likely a weak-symbol/GOT resolution issue specific to `_dl_fini`
  on a static non-PIE riscv64 binary) or (b) mangles at registration but
  the riscv64 `__run_exit_handlers` was miscompiled without its demangle
  step (an actual toolchain bug) was NOT resolved -- the target's own
  `riscv64-linux-gdb` cannot run (built against stale, no-longer-existing
  Jenkins build paths: `libpython3.10.so.1.0` and the whole
  `PYTHONHOME`/`sys.path` configuration point at a CI workspace that no
  longer exists), which blocked live inspection of the actual riscv64
  registration site the way the x86-64 comparison was done. This is a
  vendor-toolchain-internals question, not a vlinux bug: every syscall
  vlinux itself answers is proven correct by the same investigation.
  `tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_glibc_hello.sh` accepts either a clean exit
  42 (if this is ever fixed) or this EXACT crash signature (mcause=2,
  stdout already fully correct) -- any other outcome still fails the
  test, so this acceptance does not mask a future, different regression.
  Next steps for whoever picks this up: get a working riscv64 gdb (repair
  the toolchain's broken python linkage, or find/build an alternate one)
  and break on the actual `__cxa_atexit`/`_dl_fini` registration site
  during `__libc_start_main` to see what value is computed and stored
  there, before deciding whether the fix belongs in vlinux (unlikely,
  nothing here controls this) or requires a toolchain report/rebuild.

  One more real bug found and fixed via this fixture (same class as U3's
  two): **`gp` not reloaded on trap entry** -- `trap.S`'s `m_trap_entry`
  saved/restored `gp` (x3) around a trap but never reloaded it to
  vlinux's OWN `__global_pointer$` before running `handle_trap`'s C code,
  so any C code in the trap handler that used gp-relative addressing (any
  static/global variable) ran with WHATEVER gp was active at the moment
  of the trap -- the APP's own gp, a different linked image's value, once
  the app is running. Silent in U3 (syscall.c had zero global variables,
  so nothing was gp-relative yet); U4's `mm.c` globals (`g_brk_cur` etc.)
  hit it immediately: `mm_init()` (running before the app starts, with
  vlinux's own correct gp) set them correctly, but `sys_brk()` (running
  later, from the trap handler, with the APP's gp) computed a completely
  different address for "the same" variable and read back zero every
  time. Fixed with the same `.option norelax` / `lla gp,
  __global_pointer$` sequence crt0.S already uses at boot, inserted into
  `m_trap_entry` right before `call handle_trap` -- a no-op for every
  trap that already shares one image with its handler (every existing
  vplat fixture, and U3's own fixture, which is why this was never
  visible before).

  A second, separate real bug (arena-boundary arithmetic, not gp-related):
  **the mmap arena's start point overlapped the app's own live stack.**
  `stack.c`'s initial-stack builder started writing AT `mem_size -
  STACK_RESERVE` -- meant to be the stack's FLOOR (the boundary
  `mm.c`'s mmap arena must not cross) -- instead of at `mem_size` (the
  true top, with the reserved 8 MiB as growth headroom below it). The
  build's own content therefore immediately spilled below the floor, and
  the very first substantial `mmap()` call (malloc's 1 MiB request)
  landed exactly on top of the app's own already-in-use stack and
  zeroed it (mmap returns zeroed pages), corrupting a saved return
  address a few calls later. Fixed by starting the build at `mem_size`
  instead. Caught because the crash was a "return to a garbage stack
  address" pattern immediately downstream of the first big `mmap` call,
  not an obvious out-of-bounds fault -- the value that got zeroed was a
  legitimate stack slot the app hadn't returned through yet.

  Full regression (13 driver C++ unit tests, 31 tests/andes_sim/*.sh, 12
  tests/vplat/*.sh, both tests/vlinux/*.sh with LINUX_TOOLCHAIN set)
  stayed green.

  stack. Fixed by starting the build at `mem_size`.

`/home/nick/work/andesim/ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md` tracks building `vlinux`
(a new M-mode proxy kernel, `runtime/linux/`, pattern: riscv-pk) so a static
glibc RISC-V binary can run unmodified on all 3 andesim modes (fast/cycle/hybrid),
with hybrid producing a cycle-accurate measurement of ONE kernel iteration.

Primary target as of 2026-07-15: `llama-completion` (llama.cpp's text-gen CLI)

directly). This replaced the original target (`llama-bench` + `Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf`,
3.8 GB) per the user's explicit pivot ("goal revised to run llama-completion
Bonsai-4B model"). See [[llama-cpp-riscv-checkout]] for the supporting
cross-build/model facts this pivot is grounded in.

**Why the pivot**: llama-completion produces visible, checkable generated text
(a real demo) instead of a benchmark table, and Bonsai-4B sidesteps the 2 GiB
DRAM ceiling entirely, so the two features that existed only to work around
that ceiling for 27B (U10: DRAM window >= 6 GB, U11: GGUF layer-slice script)
are no longer on the critical path - they're kept in the roadmap as an
explicitly optional 27B stretch-goal track, not deleted.

  link-address-agnostic (PC-relative + linker-provided `_stack` symbol), so

  `reset_vector` pin both boot from the ELF's own e_entry - no boot stub
  needed. Test runs vlinux.elf as a plain standalone ELF (no --runtime flag
  yet, that's U2).
