# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
# rv64 tools. The toolchain check is deferred to use-time (recursive `=` +
# $(error)), so a pure-rv32 `make rv32` -- which uses CC32/LD32 below -- needs
# only HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32, not HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN.
rv64_tc   = $(if $(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),$(TOOLCHAIN),$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
CC        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
CXX       = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-g++
LD        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_all_fprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
               rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode

# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
                  break_verify_diverge

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_fcsr rt_c_dlm_data rt_c_ilm_code
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill \
                    rt_c_hvm_data
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file vplat_gettimeofday \
                       vplat_window
# C++ vplat smoke fixture: static ctors/dtors + libstdc++ containers
# through the same two-flag link, with g++ instead of gcc.
RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_cpp

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# Prereqs of the runtime grouped target(s) -- shared by the rv64 and rv32 rules.
RUNTIME_DEPS    := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/htif_client.c $(RUNTIME_DIR)/htif_client.h \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

# --- rv32 fixtures -----------------------------------------------------------
# A small rv32 set for the arch-match path; the bulk of the fixtures stay rv64.
# Built via `make rv32` (NOT part of `all`), only when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set.
# rv32_c_hello reuses rt_c_hello.c (markers are arch-neutral HINTs); rv32_spin
# reuses spin.S. The rv32 runtime comes from build/runtime/rv32 (ARCH=rv32).
TOOLCHAIN32    ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
CC32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc
LD32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-ld
CFLAGS32       := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -nostdlib -static -Wall
VPLAT_CFLAGS32 := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 -Wall
VPLAT_RT32_DIR := ../../build/runtime/rv32
VPLAT_RT32     := $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/crt0.o \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h

.PHONY: all clean dump rv32

# Linux-ABI app fixtures (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U3+): -nostdlib, no
# andesim runtime at all -- vlinux is what sets these up, not crt0.S. Link
# base 0x10000, the roadmap's "App image" base; -e _start since there is no
# crt0 to fall into it via link order.
LINUX_APP_CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LINUX_APP_LDFLAGS := -nostdlib -static -Wl,-e,_start -Wl,-Ttext=0x10000

# Real static-glibc app fixtures (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U4+): the vendor
# Linux-ABI toolchain (separate from HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN's bare-metal newlib
# one), ordinary static link -- no -Ttext override, the toolchain's own
# default static-exec layout (non-PIE, link base ~0x50000) just works with
# vlinux's loader as-is. Deferred to use-time (recursive `=` + $(error)) so
# `make all` (which does not need LINUX_TOOLCHAIN) is unaffected.
linux_glibc_tc = $(if $(strip $(LINUX_TOOLCHAIN)),$(LINUX_TOOLCHAIN),$(error LINUX_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass LINUX_TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
GLIBC_CC = $(linux_glibc_tc)/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc

all: spin.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     rt_linux_argv.elf \
     l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
     hvm_readback.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# spin.elf: benign program at a mapped reset address; the engine-registration
# probe (tests/engines/probe_engine.sh, sim --probe) halts it mid-run via the
# DM. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

rt_linux_argv.elf: rt_linux_argv.c
	$(CC) $(LINUX_APP_CFLAGS) $(LINUX_APP_LDFLAGS) $< -o $@

# NOT part of `all` -- needs the optional LINUX_TOOLCHAIN (env-gated, like
# the rv32 fixtures need HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32). Build individually:
# make rt_linux_glibc_hello.elf
rt_linux_glibc_hello.elf: rt_linux_glibc_hello.c
	$(GLIBC_CC) -static -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -Wall $< -o $@

# Marker-drain probe fixtures: each writes a device / CSR / memory window,
# then hits the entry marker so the plugin drains. l2c_drain = the v5 L2C
# Control Register; wm_drain = a v6 mask-governed CSR; lm_drain = the ILM/DLM
# slave-port windows (LM transport F1).
l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf: %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
lm_drain.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h

# LM transport (F2): reads back --ilm/--dlm content through the hart-local
# TCM view AND the slave-port aperture on the cycle engine (vplat runtime for
# the exit code).
lm_readback.elf: lm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h \
                 $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# HVM transport (F1, ROADMAP_hvm): reads back --hvm content through the
# 0x90000000 subordinate-port aperture on the cycle engine.
hvm_readback.elf: hvm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
rt_c_hvm_data.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# C++ smoke fixture: the g++ driver adds -lstdc++ -lm itself; everything
# else (crt0, crtbegin/crtend, andesim.ld, lib group) comes from the specs.
$(RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.cpp $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CXX) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin. Explicit rule, NOT in RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the
# pattern rule would look for a nonexistent rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same
# source, same link as the marked V fixtures, plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS
# (drops the ROI marker HINTs) so pc-mode and marker-mode measure the
# same GEMM kernel.

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# U5 contract (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md): the File I/O syscall set (openat,
# close, read, pread64, lseek, fstat, fstatat, statx, faccessat, getcwd,
# readlinkat, getdents64) bridged onto the existing HTIF window ops.
#
# tests/fixtures/rt_linux_file.c: fopen/fwrite/fclose then fopen/fseek/
# ftell/fread/fclose (ordinary glibc stdio -- openat/write/close/lseek/
# read/fstat), then direct syscall() probes for the rest of the set.
# Deterministic output (fixed payload, no printed pointers/times), so the
# test matches it exactly on both legs.
#
# Needs LINUX_TOOLCHAIN (config.env / env) -- SKIPs cleanly if unset, same
# as test_vlinux_glibc_hello.sh.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

TC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
[ -n "$TC" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC"

LTC="${LINUX_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val LINUX_TOOLCHAIN)}"
if [ -z "$LTC" ] || [ ! -x "$LTC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" ]; then
  ok "SKIP: LINUX_TOOLCHAIN unset/unreachable (config.env) -- no static-glibc toolchain on this host"
  exit 0
fi

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" >/dev/null || fail "vlinux build failed"
[ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf" ] || fail "missing vlinux.elf"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" rt_linux_file.elf LINUX_TOOLCHAIN="$LTC" >/dev/null \
  || fail "file-io fixture build failed"
APP="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_linux_file.elf"
[ -f "$APP" ] || fail "missing $APP"

SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"

EXPECT_LINES=(
  "FILEIO: stdio size=37 ok"
  "FILEIO: fstat size=37 ok"
  "FILEIO: pread64 ok"
  "FILEIO: fstatat ok"
  "FILEIO: faccessat ok"
  "FILEIO: readlinkat correctly EINVAL"
  "file io ok"
)

check_leg() {
  local label="$1" rc="$2" out="$3"
  local line
  for line in "${EXPECT_LINES[@]}"; do
    printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF "$line" \
      || fail "$label: missing '$line' in: $out"
  done
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "$label: exit $rc != 0: $out"
  ok "$label: openat/close/read/pread64/lseek/fstat/fstatat/faccessat/getcwd/readlinkat/getdents64 all correct"
}

# 1. fast leg. Runs from the driver's own workdir -- the tmp file lands
#    there, same convention as tests/vplat's vplat_file.c.
out=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --runtime linux "$APP" 2>&1); rc=$?
check_leg "fast" "$rc" "$out"

# 2. cycle leg: the SAME staged vlinux-run.elf, run directly (U1's
#    dual-engine pattern). File I/O syscalls are cheap (no glibc startup
#    cost beyond U4's already-measured baseline), so no extended timeout
#    is needed here.
vlinux_run=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -oE '/[^ ]*/vlinux-run\.elf' | head -1)
[ -n "$vlinux_run" ] && [ -f "$vlinux_run" ] \
  || fail "staged vlinux-run.elf not found on disk: $vlinux_run"

out=$(timeout 120 "$SIM" "$vlinux_run" 2>&1); rc=$?
check_leg "cycle" "$rc" "$out"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# U5 contract (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md): the File I/O syscall set (openat,
# close, read, pread64, lseek, fstat, fstatat, statx, faccessat, getcwd,
# readlinkat, getdents64) bridged onto the existing HTIF window ops.
#
# tests/fixtures/rt_linux_file.c: fopen/fwrite/fclose then fopen/fseek/
# ftell/fread/fclose (ordinary glibc stdio -- openat/write/close/lseek/
# read/fstat), then direct syscall() probes for the rest of the set.
# Deterministic output (fixed payload, no printed pointers/times), so the
# test matches it exactly on both legs.
#
# Needs LINUX_TOOLCHAIN (config.env / env) -- SKIPs cleanly if unset, same
# as test_vlinux_glibc_hello.sh.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

TC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
[ -n "$TC" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC"

LTC="${LINUX_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val LINUX_TOOLCHAIN)}"
if [ -z "$LTC" ] || [ ! -x "$LTC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" ]; then
  ok "SKIP: LINUX_TOOLCHAIN unset/unreachable (config.env) -- no static-glibc toolchain on this host"
  exit 0
fi

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" >/dev/null || fail "vlinux build failed"
[ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf" ] || fail "missing vlinux.elf"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" rt_linux_file.elf LINUX_TOOLCHAIN="$LTC" >/dev/null \
  || fail "file-io fixture build failed"
APP="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_linux_file.elf"
[ -f "$APP" ] || fail "missing $APP"

SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"

EXPECT_LINES=(
  "FILEIO: stdio size=37 ok"
  "FILEIO: fstat size=37 ok"
  "FILEIO: pread64 ok"
  "FILEIO: fstatat ok"
  "FILEIO: faccessat ok"
  "FILEIO: readlinkat correctly EINVAL"
  "file io ok"
)

check_leg() {
  local label="$1" rc="$2" out="$3"
  local line
  for line in "${EXPECT_LINES[@]}"; do
    printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF "$line" \
      || fail "$label: missing '$line' in: $out"
  done
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "$label: exit $rc != 0: $out"
  ok "$label: openat/close/read/pread64/lseek/fstat/fstatat/faccessat/getcwd/readlinkat/getdents64 all correct"
}

# 1. fast leg. Runs from the driver's own workdir -- the tmp file lands
#    there, same convention as tests/vplat's vplat_file.c.
out=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --runtime linux "$APP" 2>&1); rc=$?
check_leg "fast" "$rc" "$out"

# 2. cycle leg: the SAME staged vlinux-run.elf, run directly (U1's
#    dual-engine pattern). File I/O syscalls are cheap (no glibc startup
#    cost beyond U4's already-measured baseline), so no extended timeout
#    is needed here.
vlinux_run=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -oE '/[^ ]*/vlinux-run\.elf' | head -1)
[ -n "$vlinux_run" ] && [ -f "$vlinux_run" ] \
  || fail "staged vlinux-run.elf not found on disk: $vlinux_run"

out=$(timeout 120 "$SIM" "$vlinux_run" 2>&1); rc=$?
check_leg "cycle" "$rc" "$out"

content.content:
562	### 5.12 `--runtime linux` -- run a static-glibc binary under the vlinux proxy kernel
563	
564	Status: `--mode fast` only, for now (see `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md` for the
565	full plan -- `cycle`/`hybrid` are rejected with a clear error until a later
566	feature wires them; `hybrid` is planned at U9).
567	
568	```sh
569	./andesim run --mode fast --runtime linux app.elf
570	```
571	
572	The ELF you pass is your **app**, not a bare-metal image: andesim stages a
573	private copy of the `vlinux.elf` proxy kernel (built by `scripts/build_all.sh
574	vlinux`), stamps your app's absolute path and `--mem-size` into its
575	`.manifest` section via `objcopy --update-section`, and boots THAT staged
576	copy instead of your app directly. This needs `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` set (env or
577	`config.env`) to run `objcopy`.
578	
579	Two defaults change under `--runtime linux`:
580	- `--mem-size` defaults to `1G` (instead of QEMU's own default) -- override it
581	  the normal way if your app needs more or less.
582	- The CPU is pinned to the engine-synced `andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` (instead of
583	  the standalone-fast default `andes-ax46mpv`), so a fast run matches the
584	  hardware a later hybrid measurement would target.
585	
586	vlinux loads your app's PT_LOAD segments, builds the Linux initial stack
587	(argc/argv/envp/auxv) and jumps to its entry point in M-mode, so it runs like
588	an ordinary freestanding Linux-ABI ELF -- but only `argv[0]` (your app's own
589	path) is populated so far. Not there yet: real argv/envp (`-- <args...>`) are
590	accepted on the command line (so the eventual `-- -m model.gguf -t 1` shape
591	parses today) but are NOT threaded into the app yet -- andesim prints a
592	warning and drops them.
593	
594	A real static-glibc binary now runs: it reaches `main()`, `malloc`/`mmap`/
595	`brk` work, and `printf`-style I/O goes out through vlinux's UART. Known gap:
596	glibc's `exit()` (the library call -- not the raw exit syscall) crashes while
597	running its own internal cleanup-handler list, on what looks like a vendor
598	riscv64 toolchain issue (see `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md` U4 for the full

### 5.12 `--runtime linux` -- run a static-glibc binary under the vlinux proxy kernel

Status: `--mode fast` only, for now (see `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md` for the
full plan -- `cycle`/`hybrid` are rejected with a clear error until a later
feature wires them; `hybrid` is planned at U9).

```sh
./andesim run --mode fast --runtime linux app.elf
```

The ELF you pass is your **app**, not a bare-metal image: andesim stages a
private copy of the `vlinux.elf` proxy kernel (built by `scripts/build_all.sh
vlinux`), stamps your app's absolute path and `--mem-size` into its
`.manifest` section via `objcopy --update-section`, and boots THAT staged
copy instead of your app directly. This needs `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` set (env or
`config.env`) to run `objcopy`.

Two defaults change under `--runtime linux`:
- `--mem-size` defaults to `1G` (instead of QEMU's own default) -- override it
  the normal way if your app needs more or less.
- The CPU is pinned to the engine-synced `andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` (instead of
  the standalone-fast default `andes-ax46mpv`), so a fast run matches the
  hardware a later hybrid measurement would target.

vlinux loads your app's PT_LOAD segments, builds the Linux initial stack
(argc/argv/envp/auxv) and jumps to its entry point in M-mode, so it runs like
an ordinary freestanding Linux-ABI ELF -- but only `argv[0]` (your app's own
path) is populated so far. Not there yet: real argv/envp (`-- <args...>`) are
accepted on the command line (so the eventual `-- -m model.gguf -t 1` shape
parses today) but are NOT threaded into the app yet -- andesim prints a
warning and drops them.

A real static-glibc binary now runs: it reaches `main()`, `malloc`/`mmap`/
`brk` work, and `printf`-style I/O goes out through vlinux's UART. Known gap:
glibc's `exit()` (the library call -- not the raw exit syscall) crashes while
running its own internal cleanup-handler list, on what looks like a vendor
riscv64 toolchain issue (see `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md` U4 for the full
investigation); a program that calls the raw `_exit()`/`_Exit()` instead
exits cleanly today. Any other unimplemented syscall prints
`vlinux: ENOSYS <nr>` once and returns -ENOSYS rather than crashing. Track
progress in `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md`.

input.new_string:
- Key files: runtime/linux/syscall.c, runtime/htif_client.h
- Test: tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_file.sh
- Depends on: U4
- State: DONE (2026-07-15) - runtime/linux/syscall.c grown with openat/
  close/read/pread64/lseek/fstat/fstatat/statx/faccessat/getcwd (all
  bridged onto the existing HTIF window ops, no host-side/htif_client.h
  changes needed) + readlinkat(-EINVAL)/getdents64(-ENOSYS) explicit stubs
  (silent, not the loud ENOSYS-default path -- known/intentional gaps, same
  tier as U4's rseq) + tests/fixtures/rt_linux_file.c (new fixture) +
  tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_file.sh. Verified fast AND cycle: a real
  static-glibc binary's fopen/fwrite/fclose, fopen/fseek/ftell/fread/fclose
  (ordinary stdio) plus direct syscall() probes for the rest of the set all
  produce correct, byte-identical results on both legs.

  Two ABI-translation facts this feature stands on, verified against
  LINUX_TOOLCHAIN's own sysroot headers rather than assumed (asm-generic/
  unistd.h for every syscall number, asm-generic/stat.h and bits/types/
  struct_statx.h for the struct layouts, bits/fcntl-linux.h for the O_*
  bit values):
  1. **The HTIF host's open/openat handlers speak newlib's (BSD-derived)
     O_* flag bits, not Linux's.** vplat (newlib) already matched this
     convention; a static-glibc app's `flags` argument uses the Linux
     bit layout instead (only the low 2 access-mode bits agree -- O_CREAT
     is 0x40 in Linux vs 0x200 in newlib, etc.). `linux_to_newlib_open_flags()`
     translates at the syscall boundary -- exactly a proxy kernel's job,
     not a workaround. Missing this would silently drop O_CREAT
     (`andes_ae350.c`'s own comment documents this exact failure mode for
     the untranslated case) and `fopen(path, "w")` would fail ENOENT.
  2. **The HTIF host's fstat/fstatat handlers fill exactly two fixed
     byte offsets in whatever buffer address they are given -- st_mode
     (u32 @ +4) and st_size (u64 @ +16) -- not a whole-struct bounce**
     (`andes_ae350.c andesim_store_guest_stat`, matching vsim's mirror).
     Those offsets happen to line up with newlib's own `struct stat`
     (which is what the existing vplat client relies on), but Linux's
     riscv64 `struct stat` puts st_mode at +16 and st_size at +48 --
     completely different layout. `fill_stat_from_host()`/`sys_statx()`
     read the host's two fields into a small scratch buffer, then
     construct a real Linux-shaped `struct stat`/`struct statx` at the
     correct offsets (zeroing everything not known; `statx`'s `stx_mask`
     correctly reports only the fields actually filled, per the statx(2)
     contract -- not a shortcut). Also verified: `faccessat` (syscall 48)
     takes exactly 3 arguments at the raw-syscall ABI level (dirfd, path,
     mode) -- no flags, unlike the `faccessat()` library wrapper, which
     implements `AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW`/`AT_EACCESS` itself in userspace --
     so the 4th register is never forwarded as flags (would be garbage).
     `getcwd`'s host op returns a buffer ADDRESS-or-0 (a `char*`-returning
     convention, shared with vplat's own `_getcwd`), translated to the
     real `getcwd(2)` syscall's "bytes written including NUL" return by
     measuring the string vlinux just read back.

  One real bug found and fixed (same class as U3/U4's: fast tolerates it,
  the cycle-accurate RTL correctly rejects it): **`htif_win_load` is
  documented (`htif_client.h`) as u64-load-only with an 8-aligned `woff`
  requirement** (its own implementation dereferences a `uint64_t*` at
  `WIN_DATA_VA+woff`). The first cut of the mode/size extraction called
  `htif_win_load(&m, woff+4, 4)` -- a 4-byte read at a non-8-aligned
  offset. QEMU's byte-addressable MMIO model silently tolerated it and
  returned the right bytes anyway, so the fast leg passed outright; the
  cycle-accurate engine's real uncached-device bus logic correctly
  faulted (load access fault, mcause=5, mtval pointing exactly at the
  misaligned window address) on the illegal access pattern. Fixed by
  loading the whole 24-byte aligned block in one compliant call and
  extracting st_mode/st_size locally via little-endian shifts -- the
  third occurrence of this exact "fast is permissive, cycle enforces the
  real hardware contract" pattern in this roadmap (U3: `fence.i`; U4: `gp`
  reload; U5: window access alignment), worth remembering as a recurring
  class of bug whenever new HTIF/DMI-adjacent code is added.

  Full regression (13 driver C++ unit tests, 43 tests/andes_sim + tests/vplat
  scripts, all 4 tests/vlinux/*.sh) stayed green throughout.

  speak NEWLIB's O_* flag bits, not Linux's (only the low 2 access-mode
  bits agree - O_CREAT is 0x40 in Linux vs 0x200 in newlib) - a static
  glibc app's flags need translating at the syscall boundary
  (`linux_to_newlib_open_flags()`) or O_CREAT silently drops and
  `fopen(path,"w")` fails ENOENT. (2) the HTIF host's fstat/fstatat
  handlers fill exactly 2 fixed byte offsets (st_mode u32@+4, st_size
  u64@+16) in whatever buffer they're given - NOT a whole-struct bounce,
  and those offsets match newlib's struct stat (what vplat relies on) but
  NOT Linux riscv64's struct stat (mode@+16, size@+48) or struct statx at
  all - vlinux must construct the real Linux-shaped struct from those 2
  host-given fields, zeroing/reasonable-defaulting the rest.

  **Third occurrence of the "fast tolerates it, cycle enforces the real
  HW contract" bug class** (see U3's fence.i, U4's gp-reload): the first
  cut read st_mode via `htif_win_load(&m, woff+4, 4)` - htif_client.h
  documents this primitive as u64-load-only with an 8-ALIGNED woff
  requirement (it dereferences a `uint64_t*`); QEMU's byte-addressable
  MMIO silently tolerated the misaligned 4-byte read and returned the
  right bytes anyway (fast passed outright), but the cycle-accurate
  engine's real uncached-device bus logic faulted (mcause=5 load access
  fault, mtval pointing exactly at the misaligned window address). Fixed
  by loading a whole 8-aligned 24-byte block and extracting fields
  locally via little-endian shifts. Worth watching for again: any new
  HTIF/DMI-adjacent code that reads/writes sub-8-byte or misaligned
  chunks of a window/register interface will pass on fast and fault only
  on cycle - always test both legs, never trust fast alone for this class
  of code.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# U6 contract (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md): clock_gettime (REALTIME +
# MONOTONIC), clock_getres, nanosleep, clock_nanosleep -- the pattern
# ggml_time_us() (llama.cpp's own timing helper) uses unpatched.
#
# tests/fixtures/rt_linux_time.c: two CLOCK_MONOTONIC stamps around a 10M-
# iteration loop must never go backward (delta is real host wall-clock
# time, not deterministic, so the test greps a pattern not an exact value).
#
# Needs LINUX_TOOLCHAIN (config.env / env) -- SKIPs cleanly if unset, same
# as test_vlinux_glibc_hello.sh / test_vlinux_file.sh.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

TC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
[ -n "$TC" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC"

LTC="${LINUX_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val LINUX_TOOLCHAIN)}"
if [ -z "$LTC" ] || [ ! -x "$LTC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" ]; then
  ok "SKIP: LINUX_TOOLCHAIN unset/unreachable (config.env) -- no static-glibc toolchain on this host"
  exit 0
fi

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" >/dev/null || fail "vlinux build failed"
[ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf" ] || fail "missing vlinux.elf"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" rt_linux_time.elf LINUX_TOOLCHAIN="$LTC" >/dev/null \
  || fail "time fixture build failed"
APP="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_linux_time.elf"
[ -f "$APP" ] || fail "missing $APP"

SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"

check_leg() {
  local label="$1" rc="$2" out="$3"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qE 'TIME: monotonic delta=[0-9]+ us ok' \
    || fail "$label: missing monotonic delta line in: $out"
  local line
  for line in "TIME: realtime ok" "TIME: clock_getres ok" \
              "TIME: nanosleep ok" "TIME: clock_nanosleep ok" "time ok"; do
    printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF "$line" \
      || fail "$label: missing '$line' in: $out"
  done
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "$label: exit $rc != 0: $out"
  ok "$label: clock_gettime(REALTIME+MONOTONIC)/clock_getres/nanosleep/clock_nanosleep all correct"
}

# 1. fast leg.
out=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --runtime linux "$APP" 2>&1); rc=$?
check_leg "fast" "$rc" "$out"

# 2. cycle leg: the SAME staged vlinux-run.elf (U1's dual-engine pattern).
#    Same ~7min glibc-startup cost as U4/U5 (see those tests' comments).
vlinux_run=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -oE '/[^ ]*/vlinux-run\.elf' | head -1)
[ -n "$vlinux_run" ] && [ -f "$vlinux_run" ] \
  || fail "staged vlinux-run.elf not found on disk: $vlinux_run"

out=$(timeout 600 "$SIM" "$vlinux_run" 2>&1); rc=$?
check_leg "cycle" "$rc" "$out"

[ -n "$TC" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC"

LTC="${LINUX_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val LINUX_TOOLCHAIN)}"
if [ -z "$LTC" ] || [ ! -x "$LTC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" ]; then
  ok "SKIP: LINUX_TOOLCHAIN unset/unreachable (config.env) -- no static-glibc toolchain on this host"
  exit 0
fi

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" >/dev/null || fail "vlinux build failed"
[ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf" ] || fail "missing vlinux.elf"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" rt_linux_time.elf LINUX_TOOLCHAIN="$LTC" >/dev/null \
  || fail "time fixture build failed"
APP="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_linux_time.elf"
[ -f "$APP" ] || fail "missing $APP"

SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"

check_leg() {
  local label="$1" rc="$2" out="$3"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qE 'TIME: monotonic delta=[0-9]+ us ok' \
    || fail "$label: missing monotonic delta line in: $out"
  local line
  for line in "TIME: realtime ok" "TIME: clock_getres ok" \
              "TIME: nanosleep ok" "TIME: clock_nanosleep ok" "time ok"; do
    printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF "$line" \
      || fail "$label: missing '$line' in: $out"
  done
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "$label: exit $rc != 0: $out"
  ok "$label: clock_gettime(REALTIME+MONOTONIC)/clock_getres/nanosleep/clock_nanosleep all correct"
}

# 1. fast leg.
out=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --runtime linux "$APP" 2>&1); rc=$?
check_leg "fast" "$rc" "$out"

# 2. cycle leg: the SAME staged vlinux-run.elf (U1's dual-engine pattern).
#    Same ~7min glibc-startup cost as U4/U5 (see those tests' comments).
vlinux_run=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -oE '/[^ ]*/vlinux-run\.elf' | head -1)
[ -n "$vlinux_run" ] && [ -f "$vlinux_run" ] \
  || fail "staged vlinux-run.elf not found on disk: $vlinux_run"

out=$(timeout 600 "$SIM" "$vlinux_run" 2>&1); rc=$?
check_leg "cycle" "$rc" "$out"

input.new_string:
- Key files: runtime/linux/syscall.c
- Test: tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_time.sh
- Depends on: U4
- State: DONE (2026-07-15) - runtime/linux/syscall.c grown with
  clock_gettime/clock_getres (both backed by the existing
  VH_SYS_GETTIMEOFDAY host clock) + nanosleep/clock_nanosleep (immediate
  0, no timer exists) + tests/fixtures/rt_linux_time.c (new fixture) +
  tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_time.sh. Verified fast AND cycle.

  CLOCK_MONOTONIC has no dedicated host primitive -- only the wall-clock
  VH_SYS_GETTIMEOFDAY exists -- so it is synthesized as "elapsed time
  since this process's first CLOCK_MONOTONIC query" (a lazily-captured
  static baseline, subtracted on every later call): never goes backward
  under normal operation, the one guarantee real CLOCK_MONOTONIC callers
  actually depend on, at the acknowledged cost of losing meaning across a
  host wall-clock step (not a concern for a single simulator run).

  One test-design correction, not a syscall bug: the Input/Output line's
  "10M-loop" figure was written with the fast (QEMU, MHz-speed) leg in
  mind. The first cycle-leg run produced no output at all within the
  600s timeout -- not a crash, a hang-until-killed -- because an
  unoptimized (-O0) 10-million-iteration loop on the ~8.7 kHz
  cycle-accurate engine costs many minutes on top of the ~7min
  glibc-startup baseline U4/U5 already measured. The fixture's actual
  contract is "monotonic delta >= 0" (delta==0 also passes), a property
  fully independent of loop size, so the loop was shrunk to 10K
  iterations (~tens of seconds on cycle) with no loss of verification
  power -- documented here so a future fixture doesn't repeat the same
  "sized for fast, times out on cycle" mistake in a workload that runs on
  both legs, a fourth reminder in the same spirit as the fast/cycle
  DIVERGENCE class of bugs (U3/U4/U5), though this one is a test-harness
  sizing mistake, not a hardware-contract violation.

  Full regression (13 driver C++ unit tests, 43 tests/andes_sim + tests/vplat
  scripts, all 5 tests/vlinux/*.sh) stayed green throughout.

---
name: fast-leg-permissive-cycle-enforces-hw-contract
description: QEMU's functional/MMIO model silently tolerates real-hardware-contract violations (missing fence.i, stale gp, misaligned device access) that vsim's cycle-accurate RTL correctly faults on -- always verify new low-level code on the cycle leg, not just fast.
metadata:
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 5eeca9dc-9078-4a2c-9aec-f331d1142619
---

Recurring bug class in the vlinux/hybrid work (3 occurrences across
[[andesim-linux-runtime-roadmap]] U3, U4, U5, same root shape each time):
code that violates a real RISC-V/hardware contract passes cleanly on the
**fast** leg (QEMU) because QEMU's functional model is permissive, then
fails -- often confusingly, via a trap or a hang, not an obvious "wrong
value" -- on the **cycle** leg (vsim, real RTL) because that engine
actually enforces the contract.

Concrete instances:
1. **Missing `fence.i`** after writing freshly-loaded code via ordinary
   guest stores (U3): QEMU has no I-cache model, so stale/empty fetch
   never happens there; vsim's real cache faulted with an illegal
   instruction. Required by the RISC-V spec whenever a hart writes then
   executes new code.
2. **Stale `gp` in a trap handler** (U4): `trap.S` never reloaded `gp` to
   the handler's own `__global_pointer$` before running C trap-handler
   code, so gp-relative global access used whatever gp was active at trap
   time (the app's gp, once the app is running) instead of the handler's
   own. Silent on both engines UNTIL the trap handler's C code actually
   touched a global variable -- functionally this is engine-independent,
   but it was found in a cycle-leg debugging session precisely because
   fast/cycle divergence is the standing way these bugs get caught.
3. **Misaligned/sub-width HTIF window access** (U5): `htif_win_load` is
   documented (`runtime/htif_client.h`) as u64-load-only with an
   8-aligned `woff` requirement (it dereferences a `uint64_t*` at
   `WIN_DATA_VA+woff`). A 4-byte read at a non-8-aligned offset returned
   the right bytes on QEMU's byte-addressable MMIO model, then faulted
   (mcause=5, load access fault, mtval pointing exactly at the bad
   address) on vsim's real uncached-device bus logic.

**Why**: QEMU is a functional simulator (correct architectural state,
permissive about HOW you got there); vsim is cycle-accurate RTL (models
the real bus/cache/pipeline, so it enforces every real hardware
constraint: natural alignment on device accesses, I-cache coherency
needing explicit fences, whatever register state actually happens to be
live at a given PC). QEMU passing is necessary but never sufficient
evidence that low-level RISC-V/device code is correct.

**How to apply**: for any new code that (a) writes then executes memory,
(b) touches global/static state from a trap/handler context, or (c) does
raw MMIO/window/register-window access at a sub-natural width or a
computed (non-obviously-aligned) offset -- do not trust a fast-leg-only
pass. Run the cycle leg before calling such a feature done. When a
cycle-leg failure looks bizarre (silent hang, fault at an odd address,
wrong value read back) and the SAME code passed on fast, suspect this
class first: check for a missing fence.i, a stale register assumed live
across a context switch, or a violated access-width/alignment contract,
before assuming a logic bug in the new code itself.

#ifndef ANDESIM_HTIF_CLIENT_H
#define ANDESIM_HTIF_CLIENT_H

/* HTIF syscall-window client: the uncached SimControl mailbox protocol
 * shared by every andesim runtime payload (vplat today; vlinux next). The
 * window lives in DEVICE space (PMA-uncached on every engine), so the
 * exchange is coherent by construction on any cache hierarchy, including a
 * private write-back L2 (ax66 PL2C) that a cacheable-RAM mailbox cannot
 * survive: the guest would read its own stale copy of the host's result,
 * and no guest-side CCTL sequence can fix that (the VA-scoped forms trap
 * on RVH cores, the ALL forms drop unrelated dirty lines).
 *
 *   stdio (fd 0-2)  ATCUART100 UART2: THR @0xf0300020, LSR @0xf0300034.
 *   file io (fd>2)  the SimControl syscall WINDOW @0xe0080800: eight u64
 *                   arg/result slots + a data area for payloads, doorbell
 *                   @0xe0080028. Served host-side (vsim: sim_control.hpp
 *                   dispatch_window; QEMU: andes_ae350.c's mirror).
 *
 * No semihosting, no ecall, and no "which engine am I on" probe -- hybrid
 * migrates the running process between engines, so any boot-time detection
 * would go stale at the handoff. Every call must be engine-blind.
 */

#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <sys/types.h>

/* HTIF syscall numbers -- must match the table in the vsim repo's
 * src/platform/sim_control.hpp (and the QEMU mirror device). */
#define VH_SYS_GETTIMEOFDAY 5
#define VH_SYS_OPEN         6
#define VH_SYS_WRITE        7
#define VH_SYS_GETCWD       8
#define VH_SYS_LSEEK        9
#define VH_SYS_READ         10
#define VH_SYS_FLEN         11
#define VH_SYS_CLOSE        12
#define VH_SYS_ACCESS       13
#define VH_SYS_FACCESSAT    14
#define VH_SYS_FSTAT        15
#define VH_SYS_FSTATAT      16
#define VH_SYS_LINK         17
#define VH_SYS_LSTAT        18
#define VH_SYS_STAT         19
#define VH_SYS_OPENAT       20
#define VH_SYS_RENAME       21
#define VH_SYS_UNLINK       22

/* Window layout -- must match the hosts (vsim src/platform/sim_control.hpp
 * SYSCALL_WINDOW_*; QEMU hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c ANDESIM_SYSCALL_*). All
 * guest accesses are u64 loads/stores (the access width every engine
 * already proves out on the legacy 0x10 doorbell). */
#define WIN_DATA_VA 0xe0080840UL
#define WIN_DATA_SIZE (0x800u - 0x40u) /* 1984 bytes, 8-aligned */

/* Console output; blocks until UART2's transmit-holding register drains. */
void htif_uart_putc(char c);

/* One window syscall: stage the slots, ring the doorbell, read the result.
 * The doorbell write is an uncached device store, so the host has served
 * the call before the store retires; the fence orders the result load. */
intptr_t htif_syscall(uint64_t n, uint64_t a0, uint64_t a1, uint64_t a2,
                       uint64_t a3);

/* Raw copies into/out of the window data area (u64 accesses only). `woff`
 * is a byte offset into the data area and must be 8-aligned. */
void htif_win_store(size_t woff, const void* src, size_t len);
void htif_win_load(void* dst, size_t woff, size_t len);

/* Stage a string at data-area offset `woff`; returns the byte offset just
 * past its NUL, rounded up to 8, or (size_t)-1 if it does not fit. */
size_t htif_win_store_str(size_t woff, const char* s);

/* Marshaling helpers for the recurring one/two-string-argument shapes. */
intptr_t htif_call_str(uint64_t n, const char* s, uint64_t a1, uint64_t a2);
intptr_t htif_call_str2(uint64_t n, const char* s0, const char* s1);

/* fd>2 write/read, chunked through the window data area (WIN_DATA_SIZE
 * bytes per round trip); stops early on a short transfer, same contract as
 * a POSIX write()/read(). Callers own the fd<=2 (console) special case. */
ssize_t htif_write(int fd, const void* ptr, size_t len);
ssize_t htif_read(int fd, void* buf, size_t len);

#endif /* ANDESIM_HTIF_CLIENT_H */

/* mmap(2): bump-allocates from the top of the mmap arena downward.
 * MAP_ANONYMOUS is zeroed (the POSIX guarantee); `addr` is ignored (no
 * MAP_FIXED support). MAP_PRIVATE file-backed (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md
 * U7, llama.cpp's default GGUF load path): the [offset, offset+length)
 * range is eagerly read (htif_pread) into the freshly-allocated arena
 * space -- a real, private, independently-owned COPY, which is exactly
 * what MAP_PRIVATE promises (writes never propagate back to the file;
 * there is simply nowhere for this relay to route them even if it wanted
 * to). MAP_SHARED is not supported (-ENOSYS): this relay has no way to
 * write a shared mapping's changes back to the host file. Returns a
 * negative errno on failure, matching the raw syscall (not the libc
 * wrapper's -1 + errno) convention. */
long sys_mmap(unsigned long addr, unsigned long length, long prot,
             long flags, long fd, long offset);

/* munmap(2)/mprotect(2): the bump allocator never reclaims or changes
 * protection (there is no MMU here -- every page is already RWX), so both
 * are accepted no-ops for ANY address/length, mapped or not -- POSIX
 * itself allows this (munmap(2): "it is not an error if the indicated
 * range does not contain any mapped pages"), so llama.cpp's partial
 * unmap of an unused GGUF tail range is answered correctly without
 * needing to track individual mappings. A real munmap would let the
 * arena run out sooner than it should; that is a leak, not a crash. */
long sys_munmap(unsigned long addr, unsigned long length);
long sys_mprotect(unsigned long addr, unsigned long length, long prot);

/* mremap(2): always refused (-ENOMEM, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U7) -- the
 * bump allocator has no in-place-grow or relocate-and-copy capability, so
 * a caller (llama.cpp does not use this for GGUF loading) gets a loud,
 * correct failure instead of silent corruption. */
long sys_mremap(unsigned long old_addr, unsigned long old_size,
                unsigned long new_size, unsigned long flags);

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# U7 contract (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md): file-backed MAP_PRIVATE mmap --
# llama.cpp's default GGUF load path (mmap(fd, MAP_PRIVATE, PROT_READ)),
# partial munmap of unused tail ranges, and mremap correctly refused
# (ENOMEM, not silent corruption).
#
# tests/fixtures/rt_linux_mmap.c: mmaps a 256 KB host file, checksums it,
# partially unmaps, re-checksums the remainder, confirms mremap fails.
#
# Needs LINUX_TOOLCHAIN (config.env / env) -- SKIPs cleanly if unset, same
# as the other U4+ glibc tests.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

TC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
[ -n "$TC" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC"

LTC="${LINUX_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val LINUX_TOOLCHAIN)}"
if [ -z "$LTC" ] || [ ! -x "$LTC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" ]; then
  ok "SKIP: LINUX_TOOLCHAIN unset/unreachable (config.env) -- no static-glibc toolchain on this host"
  exit 0
fi

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" >/dev/null || fail "vlinux build failed"
[ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf" ] || fail "missing vlinux.elf"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" rt_linux_mmap.elf LINUX_TOOLCHAIN="$LTC" >/dev/null \
  || fail "mmap fixture build failed"
APP="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_linux_mmap.elf"
[ -f "$APP" ] || fail "missing $APP"

SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"

check_leg() {
  local label="$1" rc="$2" out="$3"
  local line
  for line in "MMAP: checksum ok" "MMAP: partial munmap ok, remaining half intact" \
              "MMAP: full munmap ok" "MMAP: mremap correctly ENOMEM" "mmap ok"; do
    printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF "$line" \
      || fail "$label: missing '$line' in: $out"
  done
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "$label: exit $rc != 0: $out"
  ok "$label: file-backed MAP_PRIVATE mmap + partial munmap + mremap-refused all correct"
}

# 1. fast leg.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# U7 contract (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md): file-backed MAP_PRIVATE mmap --
# llama.cpp's default GGUF load path (mmap(fd, MAP_PRIVATE, PROT_READ)),
# partial munmap of unused tail ranges, and mremap correctly refused
# (ENOMEM, not silent corruption).
#
# tests/fixtures/rt_linux_mmap.c: mmaps a 16 KB host file, checksums it,
# partially unmaps, re-checksums the remainder, confirms mremap fails.
#
# Needs LINUX_TOOLCHAIN (config.env / env) -- SKIPs cleanly if unset, same
# as the other U4+ glibc tests.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

TC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
[ -n "$TC" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC"

LTC="${LINUX_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val LINUX_TOOLCHAIN)}"
if [ -z "$LTC" ] || [ ! -x "$LTC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" ]; then
  ok "SKIP: LINUX_TOOLCHAIN unset/unreachable (config.env) -- no static-glibc toolchain on this host"
  exit 0
fi

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" >/dev/null || fail "vlinux build failed"
[ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf" ] || fail "missing vlinux.elf"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" rt_linux_mmap.elf LINUX_TOOLCHAIN="$LTC" >/dev/null \
  || fail "mmap fixture build failed"
APP="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_linux_mmap.elf"
[ -f "$APP" ] || fail "missing $APP"

SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"

check_leg() {
  local label="$1" rc="$2" out="$3"
  local line
  for line in "MMAP: checksum ok" "MMAP: partial munmap ok, remaining half intact" \
              "MMAP: full munmap ok" "MMAP: mremap correctly ENOMEM" "mmap ok"; do
    printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF "$line" \
      || fail "$label: missing '$line' in: $out"
  done
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "$label: exit $rc != 0: $out"
  ok "$label: file-backed MAP_PRIVATE mmap + partial munmap + mremap-refused all correct"
}

out=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --runtime linux "$APP" 2>&1); rc=$?
check_leg "fast" "$rc" "$out"

vlinux_run=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -oE '/[^ ]*/vlinux-run\.elf' | head -1)
[ -n "$vlinux_run" ] && [ -f "$vlinux_run" ] \
  || fail "staged vlinux-run.elf not found on disk: $vlinux_run"

out=$(timeout 600 "$SIM" "$vlinux_run" 2>&1); rc=$?

- Key files: runtime/linux/mm.c
- Test: tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_mmap.sh
- Depends on: U5
- State: DONE (2026-07-15) - runtime/linux/mm.{h,c} grown with the
  file-backed MAP_PRIVATE branch of sys_mmap (allocate from the arena,
  htif_pread the [offset,offset+length) range into it -- a private owned
  copy, exactly the MAP_PRIVATE contract) + sys_mremap (always -ENOMEM) +
  tests/fixtures/rt_linux_mmap.c (new fixture) +
  tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_mmap.sh. Verified fast AND cycle: mmap,
  checksum, partial munmap of the tail (the exact llama.cpp pattern),
  re-checksum the remainder (intact), full munmap, then confirm mremap is
  refused rather than corrupting anything.

  One structural (Tidy-First) step before the behavioral change: the
  "seek to offset, read, restore original offset" logic already written
  for U5's `pread64` was extracted out of syscall.c into a new shared
  primitive, `htif_pread()` in runtime/htif_client.{h,c} -- both
  `sys_pread64` and the new file-backed mmap path need the exact same
  positional-read behavior, and htif_client.h is the correct shared
  layer for it (parallel to the existing `htif_read`/`htif_write`), not
  something to duplicate a second time or reach across files for a
  `static` function. `sys_pread64` itself shrank to a one-line call.

  `sys_munmap` needed NO change: real POSIX munmap(2) already tolerates
  unmapping any range, mapped or not ("it is not an error if the
  indicated range does not contain any mapped pages"), so the existing
  always-succeeds no-op (in place since U4, originally written for the
  anonymous-mmap case) already answers llama.cpp's partial-tail-unmap
  pattern correctly with zero new code -- a "region table" turned out to
  be unneeded speculative complexity once POSIX's own tolerance for this
  exact case was checked, not a shortcut (real Linux's own munmap makes
  the same simplification, in effect, for any address a caller no longer
  cares about tracking precisely).

  Non-bug lesson, same class as U6's: the first cycle-leg run of the
  fixture (originally sized at 256 KB, ~258 window round trips) hung
  past a 600s timeout with zero output -- not a crash. Rather than guess,
  ran a direct 4 KB diagnostic first: it completed in 435s, matching the
  ~7min glibc-startup baseline U4/U5/U6 already measured almost exactly,
  confirming the mmap logic itself was correct and this was purely a
  data-size/timeout budget question, not a bug. Settled on 16 KB (~9
  round trips each way -- still meaningfully multi-chunk, not a single
  transfer) plus a 900s cycle timeout for margin. Third occurrence of
  "a fixture's data size/loop count must be chosen for the SLOWER leg
  it also runs on, not just the fast leg it was easiest to reason about
  first" (U6 was the first) -- confirmed by direct measurement each time,
  not assumed.

---
name: cycle-leg-fixture-sizing
description: A cycle-leg (vsim, ~8.7kHz) test fixture sized for the fast (QEMU) leg silently times out with NO crash trace and NO output -- diagnose by shrinking the workload first, not by assuming a bug or blindly raising the timeout.
metadata:
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 5eeca9dc-9078-4a2c-9aec-f331d1142619
---

Recurring pattern while building [[andesim-linux-runtime-roadmap]]'s vlinux
test fixtures (U6, U7 -- two occurrences in one session): a fixture whose
loop count / data size was chosen with only the fast (QEMU, MHz-speed) leg
in mind runs fine there, then on the cycle-accurate leg (vsim, ~8.7 kHz)
just... times out. No crash, no error trace, no partial output beyond the
boot banner -- the process is genuinely still running, just far slower
than the timeout budget assumed.

Concrete numbers from this session (`ax45mpv_premium`, ~8.7 kHz):
- A static-glibc binary's own startup (TLS setup, riscv_hwprobe loop,
  ...) costs a fixed ~400-435s baseline REGARDLESS of what the fixture's
  own code does -- this alone is why every glibc-linked vlinux fixture
  needs a several-hundred-second timeout, not the ~1-2min a bare-metal
  fixture needs.
- On TOP of that baseline, a 10-million-iteration `-O0` busy loop (U6)
  and a 256 KB / ~258-window-round-trip file transfer (U7) BOTH blew a
  600s total budget. Shrinking to 10K iterations and a 16 KB / ~9-round-
  trip transfer respectively fixed both, with zero loss of what the test
  actually verifies (a monotonic-delta check and a checksum-after-mmap
  check do not care how big the workload was).

**This is a DIFFERENT failure signature from the fast-permissive/cycle-
enforces-hardware-contract bug class** ([[fast-leg-permissive-cycle-enforces-hw-contract]]):
that class always produces a distinct fault (illegal instruction, load
access fault, specific mcause/mtval) that fast never sees. THIS class
produces no fault at all -- just silence until the harness's own
`timeout` kills it. If a NEW cycle-leg fixture times out with zero
output beyond the boot lines, check data size/loop count BEFORE assuming
a functional bug.

**How to apply**: when writing a new fixture that runs on both fast and
cycle:
1. Size loops/data transfers for the SLOWER leg from the start, not just
   whatever number reads well in the fast-leg output. If the roadmap or
   spec gives an illustrative size (e.g. "64 MB", "10M iterations"),
   treat it as a fast-leg-only suggestion and scale it down for the
   automated cycle-leg test, with a comment explaining why.
2. If a cycle-leg run times out with no crash trace: do NOT immediately
   assume a logic bug and start debugging the syscall/feature code. Run
   a much-smaller-input diagnostic version FIRST (a few minutes) to
   confirm the code path is actually correct and just slow, before
   spending time on speculative debugging of correct code.
3. Once confirmed as a sizing issue, prefer shrinking the workload over
   just raising the timeout -- keeps the regression suite fast for every
   future run, not just this one. A modest timeout bump on top (for
   margin) is fine; relying on timeout alone is not, since it makes the
   whole suite slower forever.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# U3 contract (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md): vlinux reads the app ELF named by
# its manifest (g_manifest.app_path, U2), maps its PT_LOAD segments, builds
# the Linux initial stack (argc/argv/envp/auxv), and jumps to the app entry
# in M-mode. Proved with tests/fixtures/rt_linux_argv.elf (a -nostdlib
# fixture -- no glibc needed yet, that's U4): it reads argv/auxv straight off
# sp and echoes argv[0] + AT_PAGESZ via raw ecalls, which exercises U3's
# minimal 2-syscall (write, exit_group) dispatch too.
#
# Two legs, same staged artifact (U1's dual-engine pattern): `andesim run
# --mode fast --runtime linux` builds+boots the manifested vlinux-run.elf for
# the fast leg and prints its staged path; that SAME staged ELF is then run
# directly on the cycle engine (--mode cycle --runtime linux is not wired
# until later -- ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U2's scope note).
#
# U8 addition: `-- extra args` after the app ELF thread through as
# argv[1..] (deferred by U2/U3, needed once U8's real invocation --
# `llama-completion -- -m model.gguf -t 1` -- has actual flags to pass).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

TC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
[ -n "$TC" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" >/dev/null || fail "vlinux build failed"
[ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf" ] || fail "missing vlinux.elf"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" rt_linux_argv.elf >/dev/null || fail "fixture build failed"
APP="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_linux_argv.elf"
[ -f "$APP" ] || fail "missing $APP"

SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"

23	 * every read back to the empty-string initializer below and vlinux never

25	__attribute__((section(".manifest"), used)) const volatile struct
26	  vlinux_manifest g_manifest = {

33	/* Set sp and jump to the app's entry point. Never returns -- the app runs
34	 * with vlinux's own C stack gone, so there is nothing left to return to. */
35	static void __attribute__((noreturn)) enter_app(uintptr_t sp, uintptr_t entry)
36	{
37	  /* load_elf() wrote the app's code via ordinary guest stores (through the
38	   * D-cache crt0.S enabled); without fence.i those writes are not
39	   * guaranteed visible to instruction fetch -- on a real cached core (unlike
40	   * QEMU's cacheless functional model, where this was silently a no-op) the
41	   * hart can fetch stale/empty I-cache lines instead of the just-written
42	   * code. Required by the RISC-V spec whenever a hart writes then executes
43	   * new code, not a workaround for this engine specifically. */
44	  asm volatile("fence.i\n"
45	               "mv sp, %0\n"
46	               "jr %1\n"
47	               :
48	               : "r"(sp), "r"(entry)
49	               : "memory");
50	  for (;;)
51	    ; /* unreachable */
52	}

SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"

# 1. fast leg: real run (not --dry-run) -- loader + stack + auxv + the app's
#    own ecalls all execute for real. "-- extra1 extra2" must land as
#    argv[1]/argv[2] (U8), not be silently dropped (U2/U3's old behavior).
out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --runtime linux "$APP" -- extra1 extra2 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "fast run exit $rc: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF "argv[0]=$APP" \
  || fail "fast: missing argv[0]=$APP in: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF 'argv[1]=extra1' \
  || fail "fast: missing argv[1]=extra1 in: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF 'argv[2]=extra2' \
  || fail "fast: missing argv[2]=extra2 in: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'AT_PAGESZ=4096' \
  || fail "fast: missing AT_PAGESZ=4096 in: $out"
ok "fast --runtime linux: loader + stack + auxv + 2-syscall dispatch (argv[0..2] + AT_PAGESZ echoed)"

# 2. cycle leg: the SAME staged vlinux-run.elf, run directly on the cycle
#    engine (proves the loader/stack/dispatch code is engine-blind, like
#    every other vlinux/vplat mechanism).
vlinux_run=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -oE '/[^ ]*/vlinux-run\.elf' | head -1)
[ -n "$vlinux_run" ] && [ -f "$vlinux_run" ] \
  || fail "staged vlinux-run.elf not found on disk: $vlinux_run"

out=$(timeout 120 "$SIM" "$vlinux_run" 2>&1); rc=$?

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# U3 contract (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md): vlinux reads the app ELF named by
# its manifest (g_manifest.app_path, U2), maps its PT_LOAD segments, builds
# the Linux initial stack (argc/argv/envp/auxv), and jumps to the app entry
# in M-mode. Proved with tests/fixtures/rt_linux_argv.elf (a -nostdlib
# fixture -- no glibc needed yet, that's U4): it reads argv/auxv straight off
# sp and echoes argv[0] + AT_PAGESZ via raw ecalls, which exercises U3's
# minimal 2-syscall (write, exit_group) dispatch too.
#
# Two legs, same staged artifact (U1's dual-engine pattern): `andesim run
# --mode fast --runtime linux` builds+boots the manifested vlinux-run.elf for
# the fast leg and prints its staged path; that SAME staged ELF is then run
# directly on the cycle engine (--mode cycle --runtime linux is not wired
# until later -- ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U2's scope note).
#
# U8 addition: `-- extra args` after the app ELF thread through as
# argv[1..] (deferred by U2/U3, needed once U8's real invocation --
# `llama-completion -- -m model.gguf -t 1` -- has actual flags to pass).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

TC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
[ -n "$TC" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" >/dev/null || fail "vlinux build failed"
[ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf" ] || fail "missing vlinux.elf"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" rt_linux_argv.elf >/dev/null || fail "fixture build failed"
APP="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_linux_argv.elf"
[ -f "$APP" ] || fail "missing $APP"

SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"

# 1. fast leg: real run (not --dry-run) -- loader + stack + auxv + the app's
#    own ecalls all execute for real. "-- extra1 extra2" must land as
#    argv[1]/argv[2] (U8), not be silently dropped (U2/U3's old behavior).
out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --runtime linux "$APP" -- extra1 extra2 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "fast run exit $rc: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF "argv[0]=$APP" \
  || fail "fast: missing argv[0]=$APP in: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF 'argv[1]=extra1' \

printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF 'argv[2]=extra2' \

printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'AT_PAGESZ=4096' \

## 11. Walkthrough: llama.cpp text generation under vlinux

`ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md` U8: a real static-glibc `llama-completion`
(llama.cpp's text-generation CLI) generating text under `--runtime linux`
on the fast leg. This needs the vendor static-glibc `LINUX_TOOLCHAIN`
(`config.env`/env; see section 5.12) and a checkout of
[llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp).

### Build

A fresh **static** build, separate from any dynamic build you may already
have (a dynamic build cannot run here -- there is no dynamic linker under
vlinux):

```sh
TC=$LINUX_TOOLCHAIN   # the static-glibc toolchain, config.env's LINUX_TOOLCHAIN
cmake -B build-rv64-static \
  -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Linux -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR=riscv64 \
  -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-g++ \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=-mext-zvlsseg -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-mext-zvlsseg \
  -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS=-static \
  -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF \
  -DGGML_RV_ZFH=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF -DGGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF \
  -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF \
  -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DLLAMA_BUILD_COMMON=ON -DLLAMA_BUILD_TOOLS=ON

cmake --build build-rv64-static -j$(nproc) --target llama-completion
```

What each non-obvious flag is for:
- `-static` (the linker flag, not just `BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF`): without
  it the binary still dynamically links libc/libstdc++/the dynamic
  linker itself -- there is no dynamic linker under vlinux, so this is
  required, not optional.
- `-mext-zvlsseg`: the Andes toolchain gates RVV segment-load/store
  intrinsics behind this flag; ggml's RVV kernels use them.
- `GGML_RV_ZFH=OFF GGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF`: the target engine (`ax45mpv_premium`,
  ELEN=32) has no scalar or vector half-precision float support; leaving
  these on produces code that traps.
- `GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF`: repacking picks tensor layouts tuned for
  specific microarchitectures vlinux is not modeling.
- `GGML_OPENMP=OFF`: no OpenMP runtime here. This does NOT remove
  threading -- ggml's CPU backend still spawns its own thread pool via
  `pthread_create`/futex when `-t` asks for more than one thread. vlinux
  has no `clone`/futex support (no threads, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md's
  own non-goal), so **always pass `-t 1`** at run time.
- `LLAMA_CURL=OFF`: no network stack here; only needed for llama.cpp's
  optional model-download-by-URL feature.

### Run

```sh
./andesim run --mode fast --runtime linux \
  build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion \
  -- -m models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
     --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 32 -t 1
```

`--mem-size` defaults to `1G` under `--runtime linux` (section 5.12),
which comfortably covers the 572 MB Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf model plus
vlinux's own arenas; pass `--mem-size` explicitly for a larger model.
Text streams out through vlinux's UART as it generates; the process exits
0 when done. `exit()`'s known cleanup-handler crash (section 5.12) means
a run may show that exact crash signature instead of a clean exit code
-- the generated text itself is unaffected either way (it is printed
well before `exit()` runs).

Found it: llama.cpp's actual `llama-mmap.cpp` uses `MAP_SHARED` (not `MAP_PRIVATE` as the roadmap assumed) with `PROT_READ` only. For a read-only mapping, MAP_SHARED and MAP_PRIVATE are observably identical (the distinction only matters for writes) — so accepting MAP_SHARED-without-PROT_WRITE is the correct fix, not a workaround.

void mm_init(uint64_t app_image_end, uint64_t mem_size);

/* brk(2): addr==0 queries the current break; otherwise tries to set it.
 * Linux syscall convention: always returns the RESULTING break (old value
 * on failure, not -1) -- glibc's brk() wrapper compares it against what it
 * asked for. */
long sys_brk(unsigned long addr);

/* mmap(2): bump-allocates from the top of the mmap arena downward.
 * MAP_ANONYMOUS is zeroed (the POSIX guarantee); `addr` is ignored (no
 * MAP_FIXED support). MAP_PRIVATE file-backed (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md
 * U7, llama.cpp's default GGUF load path): the [offset, offset+length)
 * range is eagerly read (htif_pread) into the freshly-allocated arena
 * space -- a real, private, independently-owned COPY, which is exactly
 * what MAP_PRIVATE promises (writes never propagate back to the file;
 * there is simply nowhere for this relay to route them even if it wanted
 * to). MAP_SHARED is not supported (-ENOSYS): this relay has no way to
 * write a shared mapping's changes back to the host file. Returns a
 * negative errno on failure, matching the raw syscall (not the libc
 * wrapper's -1 + errno) convention. */
long sys_mmap(unsigned long addr, unsigned long length, long prot,
             long flags, long fd, long offset);

/* munmap(2)/mprotect(2): the bump allocator never reclaims or changes
 * protection (there is no MMU here -- every page is already RWX), so both
 * are accepted no-ops for ANY address/length, mapped or not -- POSIX
 * itself allows this (munmap(2): "it is not an error if the indicated
 * range does not contain any mapped pages"), so llama.cpp's partial
 * unmap of an unused GGUF tail range is answered correctly without
 * needing to track individual mappings. A real munmap would let the
 * arena run out sooner than it should; that is a leak, not a crash. */
long sys_munmap(unsigned long addr, unsigned long length);
long sys_mprotect(unsigned long addr, unsigned long length, long prot);

/* mremap(2): always refused (-ENOMEM, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U7) -- the
 * bump allocator has no in-place-grow or relocate-and-copy capability, so
 * a caller (llama.cpp does not use this for GGUF loading) gets a loud,

long sys_mremap(unsigned long old_addr, unsigned long old_size,
                unsigned long new_size, unsigned long flags);

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# U2 contract (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md): `andesim run --mode fast --runtime
# linux app.elf -- <app argv>` stages a manifested vlinux.elf (this run's app
# path + mem-size stamped into its .manifest section via objcopy) and boots
# THAT under -bios, instead of the app ELF directly.
#
# Scope for U2: only --mode fast is wired (cycle/hybrid are rejected for now;
# hybrid wiring is ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U9). App argv (-- ...) is accepted
# but not yet threaded into the manifest -- U3 adds the vlinux loader that
# consumes argv/envp -- so this run only proves the objcopy step + manifest
# app-path round-trip, matching the roadmap's Input/Output contract.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

TC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
[ -n "$TC" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" >/dev/null || fail "vlinux build failed"
[ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf" ] || fail "missing vlinux.elf"

elf=$(ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf 2>/dev/null \
      || ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/*.elf 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -n "$elf" ] || fail "no fixture ELF under tests/fixtures"

# 1. dry-run contract: objcopy step printed, -bios <workdir>/vlinux-run.elf,
#    engine-synced CPU, the 1G mem-size default, qemu itself stays a preview.
out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --runtime linux --dry-run "$elf" \
      -- -m x.gguf -t 1 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "dry-run exit $rc: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'riscv64-unknown-elf-objcopy' \
  || fail "missing the objcopy step: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '--update-section .manifest=' \
  || fail "missing --update-section .manifest=: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'dry-run: 1 command' \
  || fail "qemu itself should stay a preview (1 command), not run: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qE -- '-bios [^ ]*/vlinux-run\.elf' \
  || fail "missing -bios <workdir>/vlinux-run.elf: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '-m 1024M' \
  || fail "--runtime linux should default --mem-size to 1G: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512' \
  || fail "missing the engine-synced CPU override: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qi 'not wired yet' \
  || fail "should warn that app argv (-- ...) is not threaded through yet: $out"
ok "fast --runtime linux --dry-run: objcopy step + -bios <workdir>/vlinux-run.elf"

# 2. manifest content round-trips: readelf -p on the staged ELF's .manifest
#    section shows this run's app path (the staged file is not cleaned up).
vlinux_run=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -oE '[^ ]*/vlinux-run\.elf' | head -1)
[ -n "$vlinux_run" ] && [ -f "$vlinux_run" ] \
  || fail "staged vlinux-run.elf not found on disk: $vlinux_run"
READELF="$TC/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-readelf"
[ -x "$READELF" ] || fail "missing toolchain readelf: $READELF"
"$READELF" -p .manifest "$vlinux_run" 2>/dev/null | grep -qF "$elf" \
  || fail "manifest .manifest section does not contain the app path $elf"
ok "manifest blob round-trips: readelf -p .manifest shows the app path"

# 3. --mem-size still overrides the 1G default.
out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --runtime linux --mem-size 256M \
      --dry-run "$elf" 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "--mem-size 256M dry-run exit $rc: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '-m 256M' \
  || fail "--mem-size should override the 1G default: $out"
ok "--mem-size overrides the --runtime linux default"

# 4. negative: unknown --runtime value.
out=$(timeout 10 "$BIN" run --mode fast --runtime bogus "$elf" --dry-run 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "--runtime bogus should exit 2, got $rc: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qi "unknown --runtime" \
  || fail "missing the unknown --runtime diagnostic: $out"
ok "--runtime bogus rejected"

# 5. negative: --runtime linux requires --mode fast (cycle/hybrid: U9).
out=$(timeout 10 "$BIN" run --mode cycle --runtime linux "$elf" --dry-run 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "--runtime linux --mode cycle should exit 2, got $rc: $out"
ok "--runtime linux --mode cycle rejected (fast-only for now)"

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# U8 contract (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md): a real static-glibc llama.cpp
# binary (llama-completion) generates real text from Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf
# under `--runtime linux` on the fast leg.
#
# Manual-tier (like tests/andes_sim/*): NOT part of scripts/run_e2e.sh's
# automated sweep. Needs three things this script does not build itself:
#   1. LINUX_TOOLCHAIN (config.env / env) -- the vendor static-glibc toolchain.
#   2. A static riscv64 build of llama-completion at
#      $LLAMA_COMPLETION_BIN (default: $LLAMA_CPP_DIR/build-rv64-static/bin/
#      llama-completion) -- see docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 11 for the exact
#      cmake recipe. Building it here would make an ordinary test run take
#      many minutes; it is a one-time setup step, not a per-run cost.
#   3. The Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf model at $BONSAI_GGUF (default:
#      $LLAMA_CPP_DIR/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf).
# SKIPs cleanly if any of the three is missing.
#
# Measured on this host: model load ~93s, prompt eval + 4 tokens ~275s
# total under QEMU's functional (not accelerated) RVV emulation -- real
# matrix math on a real 4B-parameter model is slow here by design (fast
# mode trades cycle accuracy for pure functional correctness, not speed).
# -n 32 (the roadmap's own example) scales roughly linearly with token
# count; 2400s gives ample headroom.
#
# --mem-size 2G (not the --runtime linux default of 1G): the model's own
# mmap (572 MB) plus its KV cache buffer (576 MB at -c 512) exceeds 1G:
# discovered by direct measurement, not assumed from the roadmap's
# original (too optimistic) "1G covers it" estimate.
#
# Known gap (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U4): glibc's exit() may crash in
# its handler-list walk AFTER all real work (generation, perf stats) is
# already complete and printed -- same documented, non-vlinux gap every
# U4+ glibc test already accepts. This test checks for it explicitly so
# a DIFFERENT failure still fails the test.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

TC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
[ -n "$TC" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC"

LTC="${LINUX_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val LINUX_TOOLCHAIN)}"
if [ -z "$LTC" ] || [ ! -x "$LTC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" ]; then
  ok "SKIP: LINUX_TOOLCHAIN unset/unreachable (config.env) -- no static-glibc toolchain on this host"
  exit 0
fi

LLAMA_DIR="${LLAMA_CPP_DIR:-$(cfg_val LLAMA_CPP_DIR)}"
BIN="${LLAMA_COMPLETION_BIN:-$LLAMA_DIR/build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion}"
GGUF="${BONSAI_GGUF:-$LLAMA_DIR/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf}"
if [ -z "$LLAMA_DIR" ] || [ ! -x "$BIN" ]; then
  ok "SKIP: no static llama-completion at \$LLAMA_COMPLETION_BIN or \$LLAMA_CPP_DIR/build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion (see docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 11 to build one)"
  exit 0
fi
if [ ! -f "$GGUF" ]; then

have (a dynamic build cannot run here -- there is no dynamic linker under
vlinux):

```sh
TC=$LINUX_TOOLCHAIN   # the static-glibc toolchain, config.env's LINUX_TOOLCHAIN
cmake -B build-rv64-static \
  -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Linux -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR=riscv64 \
  -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-g++ \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=-mext-zvlsseg -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-mext-zvlsseg \
  -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS=-static \
  -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF \

  -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF \
  -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DLLAMA_BUILD_COMMON=ON -DLLAMA_BUILD_TOOLS=ON

```

What each non-obvious flag is for:
- `-static` (the linker flag, not just `BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF`): without
  it the binary still dynamically links libc/libstdc++/the dynamic
  linker itself -- there is no dynamic linker under vlinux, so this is
  required, not optional.
- `-mext-zvlsseg`: the Andes toolchain gates RVV segment-load/store
  intrinsics behind this flag; ggml's RVV kernels use them.
- `GGML_RV_ZFH=OFF GGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF`: the target engine (`ax45mpv_premium`,
  ELEN=32) has no scalar or vector half-precision float support; leaving
  these on produces code that traps.
- `GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF`: repacking picks tensor layouts tuned for
  specific microarchitectures vlinux is not modeling.
- `GGML_OPENMP=OFF`: no OpenMP runtime here. This does NOT remove
  threading -- ggml's CPU backend still spawns its own thread pool via
  `pthread_create`/futex when `-t` asks for more than one thread. vlinux
  has no `clone`/futex support (no threads, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md's
  own non-goal), so **always pass `-t 1`** at run time.
- `LLAMA_CURL=OFF`: no network stack here; only needed for llama.cpp's
  optional model-download-by-URL feature.

### Run

```sh
./andesim run --mode fast --runtime linux \
  build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion \
  -- -m models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
     --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 32 -t 1
```

`--mem-size` defaults to `1G` under `--runtime linux` (section 5.12),
which comfortably covers the 572 MB Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf model plus
vlinux's own arenas; pass `--mem-size` explicitly for a larger model.
Text streams out through vlinux's UART as it generates; the process exits
0 when done. `exit()`'s known cleanup-handler crash (section 5.12) means
a run may show that exact crash signature instead of a clean exit code
-- the generated text itself is unaffected either way (it is printed
well before `exit()` runs).

  not reusable as-is. Run: `./andesim run --mode fast --runtime linux
