- State: DONE (2026-07-15) - a real static-glibc `llama-completion`
  correctly generates "The capital of France is Paris." from
  Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf under `--runtime linux` on the fast leg, verified
  end to end at both `-n 4` and the roadmap's own `-n 32` example.
  docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 11 (new) + tests/fixtures build recipe +
  tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_llama_smoke.sh (new, manual-tier) +
  config.env(.example) gained `LLAMA_CPP_DIR`.

  **A real, un-anticipated prerequisite: argv threading.** U2/U3
  deliberately deferred real multi-arg argv ("-- -m model.gguf -t 1")
  until "whenever U8 actually needs it" - U8 is that point, since
  llama-completion needs its real CLI flags. Implemented in this session
  (not a separate roadmap feature - direct part of U8's own scope):
  - `runtime/linux/manifest.h` v2: `argv_extra_count`/`argv_extra_len`/
    `argv_extra_buf[4096]` (a flat NUL-separated buffer + count, not one
    fixed-size slot per arg - real invocations have args of very
    different lengths). Up to 64 extra args / 4096 bytes.
  - `driver/manifest.{hpp,cpp}`: `build_manifest_blob`/`stage_linux_runtime`
    gained an `extra_argv` parameter; overflow (too many args, or bytes
    that don't fit) is an error, same no-silent-truncation discipline as
    the existing app_path overflow case.
  - `driver/cmd_run.cpp`: the U2-era "warn and drop `-- args`" block is
    gone - `cli.passthrough` now threads straight into
    `stage_linux_runtime`. QEMU itself still never sees these args
    (`cli2.passthrough.clear()` stays, unconditionally) - they are app
    argv, not engine flags.
  - `runtime/linux/stack.{h,c}`: `build_initial_stack` gained
    `extra_argv_buf`/`extra_argv_count` parameters; pushes each extra
    arg's string (capturing its pointer, same as app_path/argv[0]),
    then pushes the argv pointer array in REVERSE order (argv[argc-1]
    first, argv[0] last, landing right above argc) so a forward scan
    from the final sp reads argc, argv[0..N-1], NULL correctly.
  - **The one genuinely delicate piece**: the fixed auxv/envp/argv/argc
    block's total size is a multiple of 16 (the RISC-V psABI's required
    stack alignment at a function entry) only for ODD argc - true only
    by COINCIDENCE for U1-U7's argc==1. A real invocation has an even
    argc (llama-completion's real flags land on argc==10, for instance).
    Fixed by computing the block size from the REAL argc and inserting
    an 8-byte pad word whenever it comes out 8-mod-16, so the block's
    END (== final sp) is always 16-aligned regardless of argc parity.
    Verified DIRECTLY on both fast AND cycle with an even argc (not just
    trusting the math): test_vlinux_loader.sh now passes 3 extra args
    (argc==4) instead of U3's original 2, specifically to exercise the
    new padding branch, not just re-test the old argc==1 coincidence -
    matches the by-now-established pattern of never trusting an
    alignment-sensitive change on fast alone.
  - `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_runtime_linux.sh` (U2's own test)
    needed updating: its old assertion ("should warn argv is not
    threaded yet") became a real regression once this landed - flipped
    to assert the OPPOSITE (no such warning) plus that the staged
    manifest's `.manifest` section actually contains the extra argv
    bytes (readelf -p grep for `x.gguf`).

  **New syscalls, all discovered by running the REAL llama-completion
  binary against `--help` then the real model** (the same closed-loop
  "run it, read the next ENOSYS, fix it" process that worked for U4's
  riscv_hwprobe): `futex`(98), `sysinfo`(179), `fadvise64`(223),
  `madvise`(233).
  - **`futex`**: even at `-t 1`, glibc's OWN internal locking (malloc
    arena locks, static-init guards, ...) uses futex-based mutexes
    pervasively, not just for explicit application threading - this was
    NOT anticipated by the roadmap's own "-t 1 verified: uncontended
    glibc mutexes never reach futex" note, which turned out to be true
    only for a much simpler prior test, not real glibc/libstdc++
    startup machinery. Answered `0` unconditionally for every op:
    FUTEX_WAIT "already available" (a spurious wake, which the futex(2)
    contract explicitly requires callers to tolerate - spec-legal, not
    a shortcut), FUTEX_WAKE(_BITSET) "0 waiters woken" (there never are
    any), FUTEX_LOCK_PI/TRYLOCK_PI/UNLOCK_PI "success" (0 is their
    success code too) - all correct because a single-hart, single-thread
    system can never have real contention to get wrong.
  - **`sysinfo`/`fadvise64`/`madvise`**: straightforward. sysinfo reports
    `totalram`=`freeram`=mm.c's own manifest-supplied RAM size (an
    optimistic overestimate - no cheap way to account for what the two
    arenas have already handed out, and callers use this for a rough
    sizing heuristic, not a correctness-critical value) and zero/absent
    for everything with no meaning on this target (load averages, swap,
    shared/buffer/highmem, process count). fadvise64/madvise are pure
    access-pattern hints with no readahead/cache policy to tune, so both
    are accepted no-ops - the same "HINT is safe as a no-op" philosophy
    the ROI markers themselves rely on.

  **A real bug, found by running the real GGUF loader, not assumed from
  the roadmap's own text**: `sys_mmap`'s file-backed path (U7) only
  accepted `MAP_PRIVATE`, matching the roadmap's own U7 description
  ("mmap(fd, MAP_PRIVATE, PROT_READ...)"). llama.cpp's ACTUAL mmap call
  (`src/llama-mmap.cpp`) uses `MAP_SHARED` - the roadmap's own
  description was a guess that turned out wrong, caught immediately by
  running the real binary (`mmap failed: Function not implemented`), not
  discovered by re-reading the roadmap text more carefully. Fixed by
  accepting `MAP_SHARED` whenever `PROT_WRITE` is not requested: for a
  read-only mapping there is no OBSERVABLE difference between
  `MAP_PRIVATE` and `MAP_SHARED` (the distinction is entirely about
  write visibility, which never applies to a read-only mapping) - a
  genuinely correct fix, not a permissive relaxation. A writable
  `MAP_SHARED` request is still refused (`-ENOSYS`; no write-back path
  exists here).

  **A cross-repo change, not a vlinux one: llama.cpp's async logger
  needed a small upstream patch.** llama.cpp's own status logger
  (`common/log.cpp`) unconditionally spawns a background `std::thread`
  on the FIRST log call, via `common_log_main()`'s lazily-constructed
  singleton - and the generated completion text ITSELF is printed
  through this same logger (`LOG("%s", token_str.c_str())` in
  `tools/completion/completion.cpp`), not a separate direct-stdout path,
  so this could not be worked around by simply accepting lost log output.
  Since `clone`/`clone3` are `ENOSYS` here (real threading is the
  roadmap's own deliberate non-goal - implementing it would mean a real
  cooperative context-switching scheduler, a vastly disproportionate
  scope expansion for one feature), `std::thread`'s constructor throws
  `std::system_error`, UNCAUGHT, crashing the whole process before
  `main()`'s own code ever runs (confirmed via `--help` alone, before any
  model/argument work). Root-caused as a genuine llama.cpp ROBUSTNESS
  GAP, not a vlinux issue: a background-logging PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION
  should never be able to crash an otherwise-working program on ANY
  platform where thread creation can fail, not just this one. Fixed with
  a small, targeted patch to `common/log.cpp` (full diff in
  docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 11): catch the `std::thread` construction
  failure in `resume()`, set a `synchronous` flag, and have `add()`
  print immediately instead of queueing for a worker that will never
  run (`pause()` also needed a matching guard, since it unconditionally
  `thrd.join()`s otherwise). This is llama.cpp SOURCE, not vlinux -
  applied directly to the `/home/nick/work/llama.cpp` checkout (untracked
  by this repo); anyone rebuilding llama-completion from a fresh
  checkout needs to re-apply it (documented in USER_GUIDE.md, not just
  here).

  **Memory sizing: the roadmap's own "1G covers it" estimate was wrong,
  found by direct measurement.** The model's file-backed mmap (572 MB)
  plus its KV cache buffer (576 MB at `-c 512`, llama.cpp's
  `common_fit_params` computes this from context size) together exceed
  the `--runtime linux` default of 1G - confirmed by an actual failure
  (`ggml_aligned_malloc: insufficient memory`), not assumed. `--mem-size
  2G` plus an explicit `-c 512` (bounding the KV cache; the model's own
  default context, 32768, would need much more memory for no benefit on
  a short prompt) is the verified-working configuration.

  Real generation quality/performance data point (this host, `ax45mpv_premium`-
  synced QEMU, functional not cycle-accurate): model load ~93s, prompt
  eval ~165s (5 tokens), generation ~36.6s/token. `-n 32` takes on the
  order of 20+ minutes total - QEMU's functional RVV emulation of a real
  4B-parameter model's matrix math is slow by design (fast mode trades
  throughput for cycle-independent functional correctness); this is
  exactly why U9's hybrid ROI measures ONE kernel iteration, not a whole
  token, let alone 32.

  Same documented, non-blocking gap as every U4+ glibc fixture: `exit()`
  may crash in its handler-list walk AFTER all real work (generation,
  perf stats) is already complete and printed.
  `test_vlinux_llama_smoke.sh` accepts either outcome, matching every
  other U4+ test's acceptance pattern.

  Full regression (14 driver C++ unit tests including the manifest
  extra-argv encoding tests, 43 tests/andes_sim + tests/vplat scripts
  with test_andes_sim_runtime_linux.sh's assertion flipped for the new
  argv-threading contract, all 6 tests/vlinux/*.sh) stayed green
  throughout; test_vlinux_llama_smoke.sh itself is manual-tier (needs
  LINUX_TOOLCHAIN + a pre-built llama-completion + the GGUF model, none
  of which the automated sweep provides) but was run manually to
  completion during this session, twice (`-n 4` and `-n 32`).

input.new_string:
- U8 (llama.cpp acceptance on fast leg): **DONE** 2026-07-15 - the primary
  goal itself. Real static-glibc `llama-completion` correctly generates
  "The capital of France is Paris." from Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf under
  `--runtime linux` fast, verified at both `-n 4` and the roadmap's own
  `-n 32`. Full details in the roadmap's U8 DONE note (long - covers 5
  distinct sub-findings). Highlights:
  - **Argv threading** (U2/U3's deferred prerequisite, implemented as
    direct U8 scope, not a separate feature): manifest v2 adds a flat
    NUL-separated `argv_extra_buf`+count (64 args / 4096 bytes max);
    driver/cmd_run.cpp's old "warn and drop -- args" became "thread
    into stage_linux_runtime"; stack.c builds a real multi-entry argv[].
    The one delicate part: the fixed auxv/envp/argv/argc block's size is
    16-aligned only for ODD argc - true by COINCIDENCE for U1-U7's
    argc==1 only. Fixed by computing block size from real argc + an
    8-byte pad word when needed. Verified DIRECTLY with an even argc on
    BOTH fast and cycle (not trusted from the math alone) - the
    established "never trust an alignment change from fast alone" habit
    ([[fast-leg-permissive-cycle-enforces-hw-contract]]) paid off again.
  - **New syscalls, all found via the real binary** (`--help` then real
    model), same closed-loop process as U4's riscv_hwprobe: `futex`(98)
    - even at `-t 1`, glibc's OWN internal locking (malloc arena,
    static-init guards) uses it pervasively, not just explicit
    threading, contradicting the roadmap's own too-optimistic "-t 1:
    uncontended mutexes never reach futex" note; answered `0`
    unconditionally (spec-legal spurious-wake tolerance, safe because a
    single-hart system can never have real contention). `sysinfo`(179),
    `fadvise64`(223), `madvise`(233): straightforward, hint/no-op style.
  - **A real bug from an unverified roadmap assumption**: U7's own
    description said llama.cpp uses `MAP_PRIVATE` for its GGUF mmap;
    the REAL source (`llama-mmap.cpp`) uses `MAP_SHARED`. Caught
    immediately by running the real binary, not by re-reading roadmap
    text more carefully - a concrete instance of "verify against source,
    not against a prior design note." Fixed correctly (not permissively):
    MAP_SHARED without PROT_WRITE is OBSERVABLY IDENTICAL to MAP_PRIVATE
    for a mapping nothing ever writes through.
  - **A genuine cross-repo change**: llama.cpp's async status logger
    (`common/log.cpp`) unconditionally spawns a `std::thread` on the
    FIRST log call - and the GENERATED COMPLETION TEXT ITSELF prints
    through this same logger, not a separate path, so losing it was not
    an option. Since `clone` is `ENOSYS` (real threading is the
    roadmap's deliberate non-goal - a full cooperative scheduler would
    be a wildly disproportionate scope expansion), the thread
    constructor throws uncaught, crashing before main() runs. Root-caused
    as a genuine llama.cpp robustness gap (crashing on a failed
    PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION is bad on any platform), not a vlinux
    issue - fixed with a small patch (full diff in
    docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 11) making the logger fall back to
    synchronous printing when thread creation fails. This patch lives in
    `/home/nick/work/llama.cpp` (untracked by the andesim repo) -
    anyone rebuilding from a fresh checkout must re-apply it.
  - **Memory sizing**: the roadmap's own "1G covers it" estimate was
    wrong (didn't account for the KV cache buffer, 576 MB at `-c 512`,
    on top of the 572 MB model mmap) - found by an actual OOM failure,
    not assumed. `--mem-size 2G -c 512` is the verified-working config.
  - Perf data point (this host, functional QEMU, not cycle-accurate):
    load ~93s, prompt eval ~165s/5 tokens, generation ~36.6s/token - a
    real 4B model's RVV matmuls are slow under pure functional
    emulation by design, which is exactly why U9 measures ONE kernel
    iteration, not a whole token.
- U9: PLANNED - the last step to the primary goal (hybrid ROI measurement
  of an actual llama.cpp kernel). Note: U4's exit() gap does not block it
  (doesn't need glibc's exit() to complete cleanly), though it should be
  fixed before claiming a full end-user acceptance milestone.

--- runtime/linux Makefile ---
# vlinux: M-mode proxy-kernel skeleton (U1, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md).
#
# Reuses ../../build/runtime/crt0.o and libandesim_runtime.a VERBATIM:
# crt0.S's cache/FS/VS/UNA bring-up and the HTIF UART/exit stubs use only
# PC-relative addressing and a linker-provided _stack symbol, so the same
# object already works at vlinux's load address (0x0200_0000) with no
# vlinux-specific fork. main.c (banner + manifest), vlinux.ld (link base +
# .manifest section), loader.c (ELF read + PT_LOAD mapping), stack.c (Linux
# initial stack + auxv), mm.c (brk/mmap arenas) and syscall.c (the app's
# ecall dispatch, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U3/U4) are vlinux-specific.
#
# Output: ../../build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
TRIPLE    := riscv64-unknown-elf
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/$(TRIPLE)-gcc

ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh`, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path)
endif

CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

RUNTIME_DIR := ..
RT_DIR      := ../../build/runtime
OUT         := ../../build/runtime/linux

.PHONY: all clean rtlib

all: $(OUT)/vlinux.elf

$(OUT):
	mkdir -p $@

# The shared runtime lib + crt0.o (make -C .. is a fast no-op when
# already up to date, so this always runs rather than duplicating
# runtime/'s own source-file dependency list here).
rtlib:
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

SRCS := main.c loader.c stack.c mm.c syscall.c
HDRS := manifest.h loader.h stack.h mm.h ../ecall_hook.h

$(OUT)/vlinux.elf: $(SRCS) $(HDRS) vlinux.ld rtlib | $(OUT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -static -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T vlinux.ld \
	  $(RT_DIR)/crt0.o $(SRCS) \
	  -L $(RT_DIR) -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group \
	  -o $@

clean:
	rm -rf $(OUT)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# U2 contract (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md): `andesim run --mode fast --runtime
# linux app.elf -- <app argv>` stages a manifested vlinux.elf (this run's app
# path + mem-size stamped into its .manifest section via objcopy) and boots
# THAT under -bios, instead of the app ELF directly.
#
# Scope for U2: only --mode fast is wired (cycle/hybrid are rejected for now;
# hybrid wiring is ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U9). App argv (-- ...) threads
# into the manifest as argv[1..] (U8) -- this dry-run test proves the
# objcopy step + manifest app-path AND argv round-trip, matching the
# roadmap's Input/Output contract.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

TC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
[ -n "$TC" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" >/dev/null || fail "vlinux build failed"
[ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf" ] || fail "missing vlinux.elf"

elf=$(ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf 2>/dev/null \
      || ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/*.elf 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -n "$elf" ] || fail "no fixture ELF under tests/fixtures"

# 1. dry-run contract: objcopy step printed, -bios <workdir>/vlinux-run.elf,
#    engine-synced CPU, the 1G mem-size default, qemu itself stays a preview.
out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --runtime linux --dry-run "$elf" \
      -- -m x.gguf -t 1 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "dry-run exit $rc: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'riscv64-unknown-elf-objcopy' \
  || fail "missing the objcopy step: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '--update-section .manifest=' \
  || fail "missing --update-section .manifest=: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'dry-run: 1 command' \
  || fail "qemu itself should stay a preview (1 command), not run: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qE -- '-bios [^ ]*/vlinux-run\.elf' \
  || fail "missing -bios <workdir>/vlinux-run.elf: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '-m 1024M' \
  || fail "--runtime linux should default --mem-size to 1G: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512' \
  || fail "missing the engine-synced CPU override: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qi 'not wired yet' \
  && fail "app argv (-- ...) should thread through now (U8), not warn-and-drop: $out"
ok "fast --runtime linux --dry-run: objcopy step + -bios <workdir>/vlinux-run.elf"

# 2. manifest content round-trips: readelf -p on the staged ELF's .manifest
#    section shows this run's app path AND its extra argv (U8) -- the
#    staged file is not cleaned up.
vlinux_run=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -oE '[^ ]*/vlinux-run\.elf' | head -1)
[ -n "$vlinux_run" ] && [ -f "$vlinux_run" ] \
  || fail "staged vlinux-run.elf not found on disk: $vlinux_run"
READELF="$TC/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-readelf"
[ -x "$READELF" ] || fail "missing toolchain readelf: $READELF"
manifest_dump=$("$READELF" -p .manifest "$vlinux_run" 2>/dev/null)
printf '%s' "$manifest_dump" | grep -qF "$elf" \
  || fail "manifest .manifest section does not contain the app path $elf"
printf '%s' "$manifest_dump" | grep -qF 'x.gguf' \
  || fail "manifest .manifest section does not contain the app's extra argv (-m x.gguf): $manifest_dump"
ok "manifest blob round-trips: readelf -p .manifest shows the app path AND argv"

# 3. --mem-size still overrides the 1G default.
out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --runtime linux --mem-size 256M \
      --dry-run "$elf" 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "--mem-size 256M dry-run exit $rc: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '-m 256M' \
  || fail "--mem-size should override the 1G default: $out"
ok "--mem-size overrides the --runtime linux default"

out=$(timeout 10 "$BIN" run --mode fast --runtime bogus "$elf" --dry-run 2>&1); rc=$?

# Reuses ../../build/runtime/crt0.o and libandesim_runtime.a VERBATIM:
# crt0.S's cache/FS/VS/UNA bring-up and the HTIF UART/exit stubs use only
# PC-relative addressing and a linker-provided _stack symbol, so the same
# object already works at vlinux's load address (0x0200_0000) with no
# vlinux-specific fork. main.c (banner + manifest), vlinux.ld (link base +
# .manifest section), loader.c (ELF read + PT_LOAD mapping), stack.c (Linux
# initial stack + auxv), mm.c (brk/mmap arenas) and syscall.c (the app's
# ecall dispatch, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U3/U4) are vlinux-specific.
#
# Output: ../../build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
TRIPLE    := riscv64-unknown-elf
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/$(TRIPLE)-gcc

ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh`, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path)
endif

CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

RUNTIME_DIR := ..
RT_DIR      := ../../build/runtime
OUT         := ../../build/runtime/linux

.PHONY: all clean rtlib

all: $(OUT)/vlinux.elf

$(OUT):
	mkdir -p $@

# The shared runtime lib + crt0.o (make -C .. is a fast no-op when
# already up to date, so this always runs rather than duplicating
# runtime/'s own source-file dependency list here).
rtlib:
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

SRCS := main.c loader.c stack.c mm.c syscall.c
HDRS := manifest.h loader.h stack.h mm.h ../ecall_hook.h

$(OUT)/vlinux.elf: $(SRCS) $(HDRS) vlinux.ld rtlib | $(OUT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -static -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T vlinux.ld \
	  $(RT_DIR)/crt0.o $(SRCS) \
	  -L $(RT_DIR) -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group \
	  -o $@

clean:
	rm -rf $(OUT)

/* andesim/ROI.h - ROI markers for cycle measurement.
 *
 * andesim_ROI_begin()/andesim_ROI_end() delimit the region of
 * interest. On `--mode hybrid --trigger marker` the simulator switches
 * QEMU -> vsim at begin and drains at end; the reported window_cycles
 * covers exactly the span between the two markers.
 *
 * The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1).
 * An rd=x0 instruction discards its result, so each marker is an
 * architectural NOP on every conforming core: the SAME binary runs
 * unmodified on --mode fast, --mode cycle, and real silicon.
 *
 * Cycle-attribution contract: the "memory" clobber pins memory accesses
 * across the marker but NOT register-only computation -- the compiler may
 * hoist a register-resident kernel out of the span. To keep a kernel
 * inside the measured window, anchor it through memory (read inputs /
 * write outputs inside the span) or call it as a noinline function
 * between the markers.
 */

#ifndef ANDESIM_ROI_H
#define ANDESIM_ROI_H

static inline void andesim_ROI_begin(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A0\n" ::: "memory");
}

static inline void andesim_ROI_end(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A1\n" ::: "memory");
}

#endif /* ANDESIM_ROI_H */

1	// Glues CsrTrigger and StateDrain. The simulator's run-loop calls on_retire
2	// once per committed PC; the controller decides via the trigger map whether
3	// to drain state and returns the populated hybrid_state_v1 if so. The
4	// caller (simulator.hpp) is responsible for writing the file and exiting
5	// with kExitHandoffToQemu.
6	
7	#pragma once
8	
9	#include "hybrid/csr_trigger.hpp"
10	#include "hybrid/insn_match.h"
11	#include "hybrid/resume_driver.hpp"
12	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
13	#include "hybrid/state_drain.hpp"
14	
15	#include <cstdint>
16	#include <optional>
17	#include <utility>
18	
19	namespace hybrid
20	{
21	
22	template<typename Trigger>
23	class HandoffController
24	{
25	public:
26	  // scratch_gpa (L26): forwarded to StateDrain for the V dump sweep; defaults
27	  // to the unset sentinel (non-V drains never read it). The simulator passes
28	  // the real mmap-top-page GPA. caps: the target core's Andes-CSR support,
29	  // forwarded to StateDrain so the drain re-read skips CSRs the core lacks.
30	  HandoffController(Trigger trigger, DmiBus& bus,
31	                    uint64_t scratch_gpa = kVScratchGpaUnset,
32	                    AndesCaps caps = AndesCaps::all())
33	      : trigger_{std::move(trigger)}, drain_{bus, scratch_gpa, caps}
34	  {}
35	
36	  // Snapshot of the QEMU 1 input state. When set, drain merges FP/CSR/V
37	  // fields from the snapshot into the freshly drained GPRs+PC, avoiding
38	  // a per-field DM Abstract Command on every handoff.
39	  void set_passthrough_input(hybrid_state_v1 input)
40	  {
41	    passthrough_ = input;
42	  }
43	
44	  // #1: when enabled, an EXIT drains only mcycle/minstret (StateDrain::
45	  // drain_counters_only) and passes every other field through from the
46	  // passthrough snapshot, instead of reading back the full register file. The
47	  // driver turns this on whenever --verify is off, where only the vsim mcycle
48	  // delta is consumed -- so the ~190 full-drain abstract commands are wasted.
49	  void set_minimal_drain(bool on)
50	  {
51	    minimal_drain_ = on;
52	  }
53	
54	  // v5: forward the engine's L2C presence + MMIO base to the exit drain, so it
55	  // re-reads the writable L2C config registers for --verify (dual of the resume
56	  // side's set_l2c). Off unless the engine has an L2C.
57	  void set_l2c(bool present, uint64_t base) { drain_.set_l2c(present, base); }
58	
59	  // V2: forward a per-op recorder to the exit drain (see StateDrain::
60	  // set_op_log). The simulator renders the events after the drain returns.
61	  void set_op_log(OpLog* log) { drain_.set_op_log(log); }
62	
63	  auto on_retire(uint64_t pc) -> std::optional<hybrid_state_v1>
64	  {
65	    const auto hit = trigger_.lookup(pc);
66	    // Only EXIT drains; entry is QEMU's job, vsim ignores ENTER.
67	    if (!hit || hit->kind != HYBRID_HANDOFF_EXIT)
68	      return std::nullopt;
69	    if (passthrough_)
70	      return minimal_drain_ ? drain_.drain_counters_only(*passthrough_)
71	                            : drain_.drain_with_passthrough(*passthrough_);
72	    return drain_.drain();
73	  }
74	
75	private:
76	  Trigger trigger_;
77	  StateDrain drain_;
78	  std::optional<hybrid_state_v1> passthrough_;
79	  bool minimal_drain_ = false;
80	};
81	
82	}  // namespace hybrid

1	// ELF symbol resolution for pc-trigger boundaries (F9).
2	//
3	// pc mode switches QEMU <-> vsim at two PCs. Either boundary may be a
4	// "0x"-prefixed hex address (used verbatim) OR a symbol defined in the ELF
5	// (resolved against its .symtab). This decouples the switch points from the
6	// workload source -- any function can bound the ROI, with no planted markers.
7	//
8	// C++ port of tests/lib/roi.sh:resolve_pc, reading the ELF .symtab directly via
9	// <elf.h> rather than shelling out to `nm`.
10	#ifndef ANDESIM_ELF_SYMS_HPP
11	#define ANDESIM_ELF_SYMS_HPP
12	
13	#include <cstdint>
14	#include <string>
15	
16	namespace andes_sim {
17	
18	// Resolve a pc-mode boundary to a bare hex address string (no "0x" prefix).
19	//   "0x<h>" / "0X<h>"  -> "<h>" verbatim (prefix stripped, digits unchanged)
20	//   <symbol>           -> the symbol's st_value as lowercase hex
21	// On any failure (undefined symbol, unreadable/!ELF file) returns "" and sets
22	// `err` to a message naming the boundary; on success leaves `err` empty.
23	std::string resolve_pc(const std::string& elf_path, const std::string& boundary,
24	                       std::string& err);
25	
26	// The ELF class width in bits from e_ident[EI_CLASS]: 32 (ELFCLASS32) or 64
27	// (ELFCLASS64). Returns 0 when `elf_path` is unreadable or not an ELF. Reads
28	// only the 16-byte e_ident (the class-independent prefix), so it answers for
29	// rv32 and rv64 alike -- the source of truth for the fast auto-pick of
30	// qemu-system-riscv32/64 and the cycle/hybrid arch-match guard.
31	int elf_xlen(const std::string& elf_path);
32	
33	// L26/F3: the highest byte of the ELF's static memory image -- the maximum
34	// (p_paddr + p_memsz) over PT_LOAD segments. The driver rejects a hybrid run
35	// when this exceeds the V-scratch GPA (ram_base + --mem-size): the static image
36	// would extend into the reserved transport page above the program's RAM.
37	// Returns 0 + err on an unreadable / non-ELFCLASS64 file; 0 with empty err when
38	// the ELF has no loadable segments (nothing to clash with the scratch).
39	uint64_t elf_load_top(const std::string& elf_path, std::string& err);
40	
41	// Reverse lookup: the nearest function symbol at or below `addr`, formatted
42	// "name+0xoff" (or just "name" at offset 0). Returns "" when no covering
43	// function symbol is found or the ELF is unreadable -- the caller always has
44	// the raw pc to fall back on, so this never errors.
45	std::string symbolize(const std::string& elf_path, uint64_t addr);
46	
47	// Returns {st_value, st_value + st_size} for the FUNC symbol covering `addr`.
48	// Both members are 0 when not found or unreadable.
49	std::pair<uint64_t, uint64_t> fn_range(const std::string& elf_path, uint64_t addr);
50	
51	}  // namespace andes_sim
52	
53	#endif  // ANDESIM_ELF_SYMS_HPP

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# U9 contract (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md): a marker'd glibc kernel measured
# under `--runtime linux --mode hybrid --trigger marker`. glibc startup and
# setup run on the fast QEMU leg (negligible time there); only the
# andesim_ROI_begin()/end()-bounded matvec runs on the cycle-accurate vsim
# leg, which is the whole point of hybrid mode -- this is deliberately NOT
# the full ~7min-class glibc-startup cost every standalone --mode cycle
# glibc test pays (U4-U8), since that cost never touches vsim here.
#
# tests/fixtures/rt_linux_matvec.c: a tiny (N=16) scalar matvec between the
# markers, printing a checksum INSIDE the ROI (the marker contract: nothing
# after ROI-end is measured). Checked for: correct checksum, a plausible
# cycle count, and determinism (the SAME cycle count across two runs --
# "N stable across two runs (deterministic single hart)", the roadmap's own
# Input/Output line).
#
# Needs LINUX_TOOLCHAIN (config.env / env) -- SKIPs cleanly if unset, same
# as the other U4+ glibc tests.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

TC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
[ -n "$TC" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC"

LTC="${LINUX_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val LINUX_TOOLCHAIN)}"
if [ -z "$LTC" ] || [ ! -x "$LTC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" ]; then
  ok "SKIP: LINUX_TOOLCHAIN unset/unreachable (config.env) -- no static-glibc toolchain on this host"
  exit 0
fi

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" >/dev/null || fail "vlinux build failed"
[ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf" ] || fail "missing vlinux.elf"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" rt_linux_matvec.elf LINUX_TOOLCHAIN="$LTC" >/dev/null \
  || fail "matvec fixture build failed"
APP="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_linux_matvec.elf"
[ -f "$APP" ] || fail "missing $APP"

SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"

run_once() {
  timeout 120 "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
    --engine "vsim:ax45mpv_premium" --runtime linux "$APP" 2>&1
}

out1=$(cd "$ROOT" && run_once); rc1=$?
[ "$rc1" -eq 0 ] || fail "run 1 exit $rc1: $out1"
printf '%s\n' "$out1" | grep -qE 'ROI: matvec checksum=[0-9]+' \
  || fail "missing 'ROI: matvec checksum=<N>' in: $out1"
cycles1=$(printf '%s\n' "$out1" | grep -oE '\[andesim\] [0-9]+ cycles' | grep -oE '[0-9]+')
[ -n "$cycles1" ] || fail "missing '[andesim] N cycles' in: $out1"
[ "$cycles1" -gt 0 ] || fail "cycle count should be positive, got $cycles1"

out2=$(cd "$ROOT" && run_once); rc2=$?
[ "$rc2" -eq 0 ] || fail "run 2 exit $rc2: $out2"
cycles2=$(printf '%s\n' "$out2" | grep -oE '\[andesim\] [0-9]+ cycles' | grep -oE '[0-9]+')
[ -n "$cycles2" ] || fail "missing '[andesim] N cycles' in run 2: $out2"

[ "$cycles1" -eq "$cycles2" ] \
  || fail "cycle count not deterministic: run1=$cycles1 run2=$cycles2"

ok "hybrid --runtime linux --trigger marker: matvec ROI measured correctly, $cycles1 cycles, stable across two runs"

1. The exact file and function name of this per-node dispatch loop (likely something like `ggml_graph_compute_thread` or a switch/dispatch on `tensor->op` in ggml-cpu.c or ggml-cpu.cpp).

If you can find where the graph gets built (per-layer loop, likely in ggml/src or the llama.cpp model-building code for qwen3) and count how many mul_mat-family ops appear per layer, that would help me pick a good K.

### 5.12 `--runtime linux` -- run a static-glibc binary under the vlinux proxy kernel

Status: `--mode fast` only, for now (see `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md` for the
full plan -- `cycle`/`hybrid` are rejected with a clear error until a later
feature wires them; `hybrid` is planned at U9).

```sh
./andesim run --mode fast --runtime linux app.elf
```

The ELF you pass is your **app**, not a bare-metal image: andesim stages a
private copy of the `vlinux.elf` proxy kernel (built by `scripts/build_all.sh
vlinux`), stamps your app's absolute path and `--mem-size` into its
`.manifest` section via `objcopy --update-section`, and boots THAT staged
copy instead of your app directly. This needs `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` set (env or
`config.env`) to run `objcopy`.

Two defaults change under `--runtime linux`:
- `--mem-size` defaults to `1G` (instead of QEMU's own default) -- override it
  the normal way if your app needs more or less.
- The CPU is pinned to the engine-synced `andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` (instead of
  the standalone-fast default `andes-ax46mpv`), so a fast run matches the
  hardware a later hybrid measurement would target.

vlinux loads your app's PT_LOAD segments, builds the Linux initial stack
(argc/argv/envp/auxv) and jumps to its entry point in M-mode, so it runs like
an ordinary freestanding Linux-ABI ELF. `argv[0]` is your app's own path;
`-- <args...>` becomes argv[1..] (e.g. `-- -m model.gguf -t 1`), up to 64
extra args / 4096 total bytes. envp is always empty -- no test needs it yet.

591	A real static-glibc binary now runs: it reaches `main()`, `malloc`/`mmap`/
592	`brk` work, `printf`-style I/O goes out through vlinux's UART, and ordinary
593	host-file I/O works -- `fopen`/`fread`/`fwrite`/`fseek`/`ftell`, `open`/
594	`openat`/`close`/`read`/`pread64`/`lseek`, `fstat`/`fstatat`/`statx` (basic
595	fields: mode, size, nlink, uid/gid), `faccessat`, `getcwd`. Files are opened
596	relative to the engine process's own working directory, same as the vplat
597	runtime's file I/O. Not implemented: symlinks (`readlinkat` always returns
598	`EINVAL`) and directory listing (`getdents64` always returns `ENOSYS`).
599	`clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME/CLOCK_MONOTONIC)`, `clock_getres`,
600	`nanosleep`/`clock_nanosleep` also work -- the pattern `ggml_time_us()`
601	(llama.cpp's own timing helper) uses -- so timing code compiles and runs
602	unpatched; `nanosleep` returns immediately (there is no timer, so a sleep
603	burns no simulated time) and the values are HOST wall time, meaningful on
604	the fast leg but not inside a vsim ROI (the cycle count is the answer
605	there). File-backed `mmap(fd, MAP_PRIVATE or MAP_SHARED, PROT_READ, ...)`
606	-- llama.cpp's own GGUF load path uses `MAP_SHARED` -- also works: the
607	file's range is eagerly read into a private, independently-owned copy at
608	mmap time (there is no on-demand paging here, no MMU). A `MAP_SHARED`
609	mapping is only accepted without `PROT_WRITE`: for a read-only mapping
610	there is no observable difference from `MAP_PRIVATE` (the distinction is
611	entirely about write visibility), but a writable `MAP_SHARED` request has
612	no host-file write-back path and is refused (`ENOSYS`). `munmap`
613	(including a partial/tail unmap of an already-mapped range) always
614	succeeds without actually reclaiming space, matching POSIX's own
615	"unmapping unmapped memory is not an error" rule. `mremap` always fails
616	(`ENOMEM`) rather than attempt an in-place grow this allocator cannot do.
617	`sysinfo`, `fadvise64`/`madvise` (access-pattern hints -- there is no
618	readahead/cache policy to tune, so both are accepted no-ops) and `futex`
619	also work: `futex` always answers "available"/"0 waiters", which is safe
620	and spec-legal precisely because there is only one hart -- real
621	concurrency never exists to make that wrong. This does NOT mean threads
622	work: `clone`/`clone3` are `ENOSYS` (no threads,
623	`ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md`'s own non-goal), so `pthread_create` still
624	fails -- code that does not gracefully handle that failure will crash.
625	Known gap:
626	glibc's `exit()` (the library call -- not the raw exit syscall) crashes while
627	running its own internal cleanup-handler list, on what looks like a vendor
628	riscv64 toolchain issue (see `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md` U4 for the full
629	investigation); a program that calls the raw `_exit()`/`_Exit()` instead

A real static-glibc binary now runs: it reaches `main()`, `malloc`/`mmap`/
`brk` work, `printf`-style I/O goes out through vlinux's UART, and ordinary
host-file I/O works -- `fopen`/`fread`/`fwrite`/`fseek`/`ftell`, `open`/
`openat`/`close`/`read`/`pread64`/`lseek`, `fstat`/`fstatat`/`statx` (basic
fields: mode, size, nlink, uid/gid), `faccessat`, `getcwd`. Files are opened
relative to the engine process's own working directory, same as the vplat
runtime's file I/O. Not implemented: symlinks (`readlinkat` always returns
`EINVAL`) and directory listing (`getdents64` always returns `ENOSYS`).
`clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME/CLOCK_MONOTONIC)`, `clock_getres`,
`nanosleep`/`clock_nanosleep` also work -- the pattern `ggml_time_us()`
(llama.cpp's own timing helper) uses -- so timing code compiles and runs
unpatched; `nanosleep` returns immediately (there is no timer, so a sleep
burns no simulated time) and the values are HOST wall time, meaningful on
the fast leg but not inside a vsim ROI (the cycle count is the answer
there). File-backed `mmap(fd, MAP_PRIVATE or MAP_SHARED, PROT_READ, ...)`
-- llama.cpp's own GGUF load path uses `MAP_SHARED` -- also works: the
file's range is eagerly read into a private, independently-owned copy at
mmap time (there is no on-demand paging here, no MMU). A `MAP_SHARED`
mapping is only accepted without `PROT_WRITE`: for a read-only mapping
there is no observable difference from `MAP_PRIVATE` (the distinction is
entirely about write visibility), but a writable `MAP_SHARED` request has
no host-file write-back path and is refused (`ENOSYS`). `munmap`
(including a partial/tail unmap of an already-mapped range) always
succeeds without actually reclaiming space, matching POSIX's own
"unmapping unmapped memory is not an error" rule. `mremap` always fails
(`ENOMEM`) rather than attempt an in-place grow this allocator cannot do.
`sysinfo`, `fadvise64`/`madvise` (access-pattern hints -- there is no
readahead/cache policy to tune, so both are accepted no-ops) and `futex`
also work: `futex` always answers "available"/"0 waiters", which is safe
and spec-legal precisely because there is only one hart -- real
concurrency never exists to make that wrong. This does NOT mean threads
work: `clone`/`clone3` are `ENOSYS` (no threads,
`ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md`'s own non-goal), so `pthread_create` still
fails -- code that does not gracefully handle that failure will crash.

### Measuring one kernel iteration under hybrid mode

The fast leg above proves correctness; `--mode hybrid` measures real
cycles for one kernel iteration -- a full token would take hours at
vsim's cycle-accurate clock (~9 kHz) even for a model this size, which is
why hybrid mode exists: everything up to the marker runs on the fast
QEMU leg (negligible time), and only the marked region runs on the
cycle-accurate leg.

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux --mem-size 2G \
  --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
  build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion \
  -- -m models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
     --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
```

This needs `<andesim/ROI.h>` markers inside llama.cpp, bounding ONE
matvec-class operation (not a whole token) -- see `docs/llama_roi_howto.md`
for the exact patch and how the insertion point was chosen. Since ggml
builds its whole computation graph before executing it in one shot,
individual operations are not distinguishable at the application call-site
level (e.g. the per-layer forward-pass code) -- the markers go in ggml's
own generic per-node dispatch loop instead, gated by a counter so only
one specific node's execution is actually measured.

Insertion point: `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c:1836-1839`, the `GGML_OP_MUL_MAT` case inside `ggml_compute_forward()`. Single-threaded at `-t 1` is confirmed safe. One token's forward-pass graph has **253** `GGML_OP_MUL_MAT` nodes (36 layers x 7, +1 lm_head) - empirically measured, not estimated. K=10 or K=50 both land safely inside the transformer stack.

### 1. Dispatch loop location

- Per-node loop: `ggml_graph_compute_thread()`, `ggml-cpu.c:3044-3117`. It walks `cgraph->nodes[node_n]` and calls `ggml_compute_forward(&params, node)` at line 3090.
- Actual op-to-function routing: `ggml_compute_forward()`, `ggml-cpu.c:1711`, a `switch (tensor->op)`. `GGML_OP_MUL_MAT` case is lines 1836-1839, calling `ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat()`.

I checked both functions have exactly one caller each in the whole tree (`grep` confirmed) - no other path reaches `ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat`. I also checked the CPU "repack" fast path (`repack.cpp`, used for AVX/NEON/RVV-optimized quant kernels): it only handles `Q4_0/Q4_K/Q5_K/Q6_K/Q2_K/IQ4_NL/MXFP4/Q8_0`. `Q1_0` is not in that list, so it always falls through to the normal switch - no bypass to worry about for your model.

### 2. Minimal patch (not applied)

```c
// near the other #includes at the top of ggml-cpu.c (after line 16, "common.h")
#include <andesim/ROI.h>

#ifndef ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K
#define ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K 50   // 1-based ordinal of the MUL_MAT node to bracket
#endif
```

```c
// ggml-cpu.c:1836-1839
        case GGML_OP_MUL_MAT:
            {
-               ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat(params, tensor);
+               static int andesim_mul_mat_n = 0;
+               andesim_mul_mat_n++;
+               const bool andesim_roi = (andesim_mul_mat_n == ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K);
+               if (andesim_roi) andesim_ROI_begin();
+               ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat(params, tensor);
+               if (andesim_roi) andesim_ROI_end();
            } break;
```

`K` as a `#define` (overridable with `-DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=...`) avoids re-editing this file per experiment.

### 3. Thread safety at `-t 1`

Safe. Traced `ggml_graph_compute()` (`ggml-cpu.c:3334`): with OpenMP, `n_threads==1` takes the `else` branch (line 3382-3385) and calls `ggml_graph_compute_thread()` directly - no `#pragma omp parallel`, no thread spawn. Without OpenMP, `ggml_threadpool_new_impl()` only `pthread_create`s workers for `j = 1 .. n_threads-1` (line 3309) - with `n_threads=1` that loop body never runs, so worker 0 IS the calling thread. Either way exactly one thread calls `ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat` exactly once per node. A plain `static int` is safe. (This breaks under `nth>1` - same node gets entered by every thread cooperatively - but that's out of scope for your `-t 1` use case.)

I also verified this empirically with a `gdb` breakpoint counter on the real binary (`build-host/bin/llama-completion -t 1`), not just by reading the code.

### 4. Per-layer MUL_MAT count (Bonsai-4B, qwen3, 36 layers, 2560 embd)

Confirmed `Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf` is `general.architecture=qwen3`, `block_count=36`, `embedding_length=2560`, 11 tensors/layer (checked with `gguf-py`). From `src/models/qwen3.cpp` + `src/llama-graph.cpp`, per layer:
- `wq, wk, wv` (separate, not fused - GGUF confirms `attn_q/attn_k/attn_v.weight` exist separately since qwen3 uses GQA with different Q/K/V shapes)
- `wo` (attention output projection)
- `ffn_gate, ffn_up, ffn_down` (SwiGLU FFN)

= 7 `GGML_OP_MUL_MAT` per layer. `attn_q_norm`/`attn_k_norm`/`attn_norm`/`ffn_norm` are RMSNorm gains (elementwise `ggml_mul`, not matmul - don't count). # Off by default: the plain "v" extension implies ELEN>=64 (the RISC-V V
# spec's own minimum). Some real cores (e.g. Andes ax45mpv, andesim's
# hybrid-sim target) implement only the Zve32f embedded-vector profile
# (ELEN=32, no 64-bit vector elements) -- compiling with plain "v" lets
# GCC's auto-vectorizer freely emit e64 vector ops (not just in ggml's own
# hand-written RVV kernels -- ordinary struct-copy-style C code can get
# auto-vectorized this way too), which such a core cannot execute at all.
# On when set, this replaces "v" with "zve32f" in the -march string so the
# compiler never emits anything outside what the real target supports.
option(GGML_RV_ZVE32F        "ggml: constrain riscv v to zve32f (ELEN=32 cores)" OFF)

lines: +// andesim (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U9): GCC's auto-vectorizer emits a
+// 64-bit-element (e64) vector load/store here for these two statics'
+// lazy init -- correct on any real "V"-extension core (which the RISC-V
+// spec requires to support ELEN>=64), but the andesim hybrid-sim target
+// (Andes ax45mpv) implements only Zve32f (ELEN=32), and the (unrelated)
+// -march=...v used to build this file does not tell GCC to avoid that.
+// ggml_backend_device) has no computational reason to be vectorized at
+// all -- this is ordinary lazy-static initialization, not a hot loop --
+// so disabling auto-vectorization for just this function is a precise,
+// zero-cost fix: it does not touch ggml's own hand-written RVV kernels
+// (explicit __riscv_v* intrinsics elsewhere are unaffected either way,
+// since those never depended on the auto-vectorizer to begin with).

516	// spec requires to support ELEN>=64), but the andesim hybrid-sim target
517	// (Andes ax45mpv) implements only Zve32f (ELEN=32), and the (unrelated)
518	// -march=...v used to build this file does not tell GCC to avoid that.
519	// The struct being copied here (ggml_backend_cpu_device_context/
520	// ggml_backend_device) has no computational reason to be vectorized at
521	// all -- this is ordinary lazy-static initialization, not a hot loop --

524	// (explicit __riscv_v* intrinsics elsewhere are unaffected either way,
525	// since those never depended on the auto-vectorizer to begin with).

content.text: File-scoped pragmas aren't reliably suppressing this (likely GCC's struct-copy-to-vector lowering happens at a different compilation phase than the tree-vectorizer). Switching to a real, unambiguous fix: compile `ggml-cpu.cpp` specifically with no vector extension at all via CMake — it's pure backend-dispatch code with no intentional RVV usage of its own, so this can't affect any real kernel.

function(ggml_add_cpu_backend_features cpu_name arch)
    # The feature detection code is compiled as a separate target so that
    # it can be built without the architecture flags
    # Since multiple variants of the CPU backend may be included in the same
    # build, using set_source_files_properties() to set the arch flags is not possible
    set(GGML_CPU_FEATS_NAME ${cpu_name}-feats)
    add_library(${GGML_CPU_FEATS_NAME} OBJECT ggml-cpu/arch/${arch}/cpu-feats.cpp)
    target_include_directories(${GGML_CPU_FEATS_NAME} PRIVATE . ../include)
    target_compile_definitions(${GGML_CPU_FEATS_NAME} PRIVATE ${ARGN})
    target_compile_definitions(${GGML_CPU_FEATS_NAME} PRIVATE GGML_BACKEND_DL GGML_BACKEND_BUILD GGML_BACKEND_SHARED)
    set_target_properties(${GGML_CPU_FEATS_NAME} PROPERTIES POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE ON)
    # Disable LTO for the feature detection code to prevent cross-module optimization
    # from inlining architecture-specific instructions into the score function.
    # Without this, LTO can cause SIGILL when loading backends on older CPUs
    # (e.g., loading power10 backend on power9 crashes before feature check runs).
    target_compile_options(${GGML_CPU_FEATS_NAME} PRIVATE -fno-lto)
    target_link_libraries(${cpu_name} PRIVATE ${GGML_CPU_FEATS_NAME})
endfunction()

function(ggml_add_cpu_backend_variant_impl tag_name)
    if (tag_name)
        set(GGML_CPU_NAME ggml-cpu-${tag_name})
    else()
        set(GGML_CPU_NAME ggml-cpu)
    endif()

    ggml_add_backend_library(${GGML_CPU_NAME})

    list (APPEND GGML_CPU_SOURCES
        ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c
        ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.cpp
        ggml-cpu/repack.cpp
        ggml-cpu/repack.h
        ggml-cpu/hbm.cpp
        ggml-cpu/hbm.h
        ggml-cpu/quants.c
        ggml-cpu/quants.h
        ggml-cpu/traits.cpp
        ggml-cpu/traits.h
        ggml-cpu/amx/amx.cpp

# andesim (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U9): on riscv64 with GGML_RVV, GCC's
    # auto-vectorizer (specifically the SLP/straight-line pass, not the
    # loop vectorizer -- confirmed by testing both `-fno-tree-vectorize`
    # and a #pragma GCC push_options/optimize/pop_options wrapper, neither
    # of which stopped it) lowers an ordinary struct-literal static
    # initialization in ggml-cpu.cpp (registering the CPU backend's device
    # vtable, nothing performance-sensitive) into a 64-bit-element (e64)
    # vector load/store. That is correct for any core meeting the RISC-V
    # V extension's own spec-mandated ELEN>=64 floor, but the andesim
    # hybrid-sim target (Andes ax45mpv) implements only Zve32f (ELEN=32)
    # and traps on it. ggml-cpu.cpp itself has no intentional RVV usage of
    # its own (that lives in vec.cpp/repack.cpp/arch/riscv/*.c, which DO
    # need real e64 support for some reductions and are deliberately left
    # alone here) -- it is backend registration/dispatch, so compiling
    # this ONE file with no vector extension at all is a precise, correct
    # fix: this exact source-level compile-options override pattern is
    # already used above for the KleidiAI sources' own differing arch needs.
    if (GGML_SYSTEM_ARCH STREQUAL "riscv64" AND GGML_RVV)
        set_source_files_properties(ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.cpp PROPERTIES
            COMPILE_OPTIONS "-march=rv64gc_zicbop_zihintpause")
    endif()

    message(STATUS "Adding CPU backend variant ${GGML_CPU_NAME}: ${ARCH_FLAGS} ${ARCH_DEFINITIONS}")
    target_sources(${GGML_CPU_NAME} PRIVATE ${GGML_CPU_SOURCES})
    target_compile_options(${GGML_CPU_NAME} PRIVATE ${ARCH_FLAGS})

If green, mark U8 complete and start U9... the final roadmap feature and the user's stated end goal (run llama-completion under andesim hybrid mode)", and once via a slash-command wrapper) — both reinforcing the same standing goal, not new requests.
   - Standing constraints inherited from global config (apply throughout, unchanged from before): TDD hard gate (RED test/failing-test evidence before any non-test Edit/Write, explicit RED/GREEN/REFACTOR phase statements); Tidy-First discipline (structural changes before behavioral, separated); terse/ASCII-only chat responses; never commit unless explicitly asked; no workarounds/quick fixes — find real root causes; one ROADMAP feature per session with roadmap state updates (relaxed by the goal hook to "all remaining features this session"); don't duplicate code; consider portability; propose architecture the user (non-native-English PM) can understand; always update docs/USER_GUIDE.md when something user-facing changes.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - andesim hybrid RISC-V simulator: QEMU (fast) + vsim (cycle-accurate) sharing state via magic-CSR/HTIF; `--mode fast|cycle|hybrid`.
   - `vlinux`: M-mode proxy kernel in `runtime/linux/`. By this point in the session: full syscall table (U4), file I/O (U5), time (U6), file-backed mmap (U7), argv threading + real llama-completion support (U8), hybrid+marker ROI support (U9, in progress).
   - HTIF window client (`runtime/htif_client.h/.c`): shared UART/file-io/window protocol; `htif_win_load`/`htif_win_store` are strictly u64-load/store-only with an 8-aligned `woff` requirement (documented in the header, source of a real bug in U5).
   - "Fast-permissive/cycle-or-hybrid-enforces" bug class (now recurred 4 times): QEMU's functional model is permissive about things the real hardware (vsim RTL, or even QEMU's own accurately-engine-synced `-readconfig` under hybrid) correctly rejects. Instances: U3 missing `fence.i`, U4 stale `gp` in trap handler, U5 misaligned HTIF window access, and now U9's ELEN=32 vs plain `v`-implied-ELEN64 auto-vectorization bug (caught specifically because hybrid's QEMU1 leg uses an accurately engine-synced `-readconfig` with explicit `elen=32`, unlike fast mode's own hardcoded, less-accurate `-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` string which never constrains ELEN).
   - "Cycle-leg fixture sizing" lesson (recurred twice, U6/U7): a fixture sized for the fast leg silently times out (not crashes) on the ~8.7kHz cycle-accurate engine; diagnose via a much-smaller input first, don't assume a bug.
   - Linux syscall ABI on riscv64: verified via LINUX_TOOLCHAIN sysroot headers directly (never guessed): syscall numbers, `struct stat`/`struct statx` layouts, O_* flag bit differences between Linux and newlib, `AT_FDCWD=-100`, etc.
   - vlinux manifest wire format v2 (`runtime/linux/manifest.h`): `argv_extra_count`/`argv_extra_len`/`argv_extra_buf[4096]` (flat NUL-separated, up to 64 args), added in U8 for argv threading.
   - RISC-V initial-stack 16-byte-alignment requirement: the fixed auxv/envp/argv/argc block's size depends on argc parity; only odd argc was accidentally 16-aligned in the original U1-U7 code.
   - GGML computation graph model: builds the WHOLE graph first (`ggml_mul_mat()` adds nodes), then executes it in one shot via a generic per-node dispatch loop (`ggml_graph_compute_thread` → `ggml_compute_forward`, in `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c`) — individual ops are NOT distinguishable at the application call-site level, so ROI markers for "one op" must go in this generic dispatch loop, counter-gated.
   - RISC-V Vector extension ELEN semantics: plain `v` extension implies the spec-mandated ELEN≥64 minimum; `Zve32f`/`Zve32x` are separate, narrower sub-extensions (ELEN=32, no 64-bit vector elements). The target engine (Andes ax45mpv) is ELEN=32. `vsetvli` requesting an unsupported SEW silently sets `vtype.vill=1` (does not itself trap); the NEXT vector instruction then traps with illegal-instruction.
   - GCC auto-vectorization: SLP (straight-line/superword) vectorizer is DISTINCT from the loop vectorizer and turns plain struct/array copies into vector load/store even absent any programmer-written vector code; confirmed empirically that `-fno-tree-vectorize` alone, the `__attribute__((optimize(...)))` function attribute, and even `#pragma GCC push_options`/`optimize`/`pop_options` all FAILED to suppress this specific SLP-vectorized code generation for the sites found; only a real per-file `-march` override via CMake's `set_source_files_properties(... PROPERTIES COMPILE_OPTIONS ...)` reliably worked (confirmed via objdump).
   - vsim's `CsrTrigger` (`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/csr_trigger.hpp`): STATICALLY pre-scans (via LIEF) the PT_LOAD+PF_X segments of whatever ELF it's given (its own positional CLI arg) for marker HINT instructions at CONFIGURE time — NOT dynamic pattern-matching like QEMU's plugin. This is asymmetric: QEMU's plugin watches the executed instruction stream (content-agnostic, engine-blind); vsim's trigger only "sees" markers physically present in its own boot ELF's static content.
   - `--hybrid-exit-pc <addr>`: an EXISTING, already-supported vsim CLI flag (used for `--trigger pc` mode, via `add_pc_hit` in CsrTrigger) — reused (not newly added) to solve the marker-scanning mismatch without any vsim source changes, honoring the roadmap's explicit "hybrid transport, triggers, plugin, resume driver, and engines need NO changes" constraint.
   - `include/hybrid/insn_match.h`: shared C header (already used by both the QEMU plugin and vsim) exposing `hybrid_match_handoff_insn()` and the exact marker instruction encodings (`HYBRID_MARKER_ENTER_INSN=0x5A002013`, `HYBRID_MARKER_EXIT_INSN=0x5A102013`) — reused directly from the driver (C++) via `#include "hybrid/insn_match.h"` for `find_roi_markers`, avoiding any reimplementation drift.
   - ggml's per-token MUL_MAT count for Bonsai-4B (qwen3, 36 layers, 2560 embd): 253 nodes (36×7 + 1 lm_head), confirmed empirically via gdb breakpoint counting (not just static analysis) by a research agent. K=50 (my chosen ROI target) lands in layer 7's first matmul.

Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. 1	// andesim command-line parsing.
2	//
3	// The grammar is deliberately tiny and stable across all subcommands:
4	//
5	//   andesim [<cmd>] [--mode M] [--engine E] [--trigger T] [positional...]
6	//                   [-- <verbatim engine args...>]
7	//
8	// `run` is the default command: when the first token is not a known
9	// subcommand (and not a top-level help flag), the whole line parses as
10	// `run ...`, so `andesim --mode fast prog.elf` works without typing `run`.
11	//
12	// The single most important rule is the `--` boundary: every token after the
13	// first `--` is captured verbatim into `passthrough` and is NOT interpreted by
14	// the framework. That is what lets `fast`/`cycle` forward an engine's whole
15	// native CLI (e.g. `-gdb tcp::1234 -S`) untouched, so users see one simulator.
16	#ifndef ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
17	#define ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
18	
19	#include <string>
20	#include <string_view>
21	#include <vector>
22	
23	namespace andes_sim {
24	
25	// True for the known command names (run/list/doctor/profile). The single
26	// source of truth shared by the parser (default-command rule) and main's
27	// dispatch.
28	bool is_subcommand(std::string_view name);
29	
30	struct Cli {
31	  std::string subcommand;                 // e.g. "run", "list"; "" if none
32	  std::string model;                      // --mode fast|cycle|hybrid (field stays 'model': the concept, see list models)
33	  std::string engine;                     // --engine <id>
34	  std::string trigger;                    // --trigger marker|pc
35	  // Hybrid trigger args (empty => cmd_run applies the default). pc boundaries
36	  // are a symbol name or 0x address; the sizes stay strings here and are
37	  // parsed where they are used.
38	  std::string pc_start;                   // --pc-start (trigger pc)
39	  std::string pc_end;                     // --pc-end   (trigger pc)
40	  std::string mem_size;                   // --mem-size (guest memory; --mmap-size is a hidden alias)
41	  std::string runtime;                    // --runtime linux (proxy-kernel payload; "" => bare-metal ELF, the default)
42	  std::string kanata;                     // --kanata <file> (marker/pc ROI trace)
43	  std::string objdump;                    // --objdump <file> (kanata labels)
44	  std::string log_level;                  // --log-level 0..6 (vsim scale; "" => info)
45	  std::string log_file;                   // --log-file <path> (full trace capture)
46	  std::vector<std::string> positional;    // non-flag framework args
47	  std::vector<std::string> passthrough;   // verbatim, everything after `--`
48	  bool help = false;                      // -h / --help (before `--`)
49	  bool dry_run = false;                   // --dry-run (build, run, test, ...)
50	  bool print_memmap = false;              // --print-memmap (run --mode hybrid)
51	  bool verify = false;                    // --verify (run --mode hybrid)
52	  bool gdb = false;                       // --gdb (fast: QEMU gdbstub; cycle: vsim JTAG + ICEman)
53	  std::string gdb_port;                   // --gdb-port (fast: default 1234; cycle: default 9104)
54	  // profile's report knobs (values stay strings; cmd_profile applies the
55	  // defaults where they are used, like mem_size/gdb_port above).
56	  std::string limit;                      // --limit (profile; "" => 50)
57	  std::string min_iters;                  // --min-iters (profile; "" => 1)
58	  std::string addr2line;                  // --addr2line (profile; "" => auto)
59	  bool raw = false;                       // --raw (profile: dump the plugin log)
60	  bool llm = true;                        // --llm / --no-llm (profile report format)
61	  bool optimize_rvv = true;               // --optimize-rvv / --no-optimize-rvv (profile)
62	  bool no_source = false;                 // --no-source (profile: skip addr2line)
63	  bool has_passthrough = false;           // a `--` boundary was present
64	  std::string error;                      // non-empty => parse failed
65	};

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Log-level contract: driver chatter is leveled like vsim's --log-level
3	# (0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off; default 2=info).
4	#
5	#   1. default (info): a hybrid --dry-run shows the dry-run commands but NO
6	#      banner and NO mmap line.
7	#   2. --log-level 1 (debug): banner + mmap line appear; the mmap line uses
8	#      the [andesim] prefix and the retired [hsim mmap] prefix is gone.
9	#   3. default (info) on a real hybrid run: program output + the cycle
10	#      figure only -- no banner, no mmap line, no trailing PASS chatter.
11	#   4. an out-of-range --log-level is a clean non-zero error naming 0..6.
12	#
13	# RED-then-green smoke test, run manually during driver development. Not wired
14	# into run_e2e.sh.
15	set -uo pipefail
16	
17	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
18	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
19	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
20	
21	BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
22	ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf"
23	ENGINE="vsim:ax45mpv_premium"
24	
25	bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
26	[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"
27	[ -f "$ELF" ] || fail "missing fixture: $ELF"
28	
29	# 1. default level hides the banner and the mmap line (dry-run: cheap)
30	out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --dry-run "$ELF" 2>&1) \
31	  || fail "hybrid --dry-run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
32	echo "$out" | grep -q "dry-run: 2 command(s)" || fail "dry-run header missing:"$'\n'"$out"
33	echo "$out" | grep -q "model=hybrid" && fail "default level should hide the banner:"$'\n'"$out"
34	echo "$out" | grep -qi "mmap" && fail "default level should hide the mmap line:"$'\n'"$out"
35	
36	# 2. debug level shows them, with the [andesim] prefix (no [hsim mmap])
37	out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --log-level 1 --dry-run "$ELF" 2>&1) \
38	  || fail "hybrid --log-level 1 --dry-run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
39	echo "$out" | grep -q "model=hybrid" || fail "debug level missing banner:"$'\n'"$out"
40	echo "$out" | grep -q "\[andesim\] mmap" || fail "debug level missing [andesim] mmap line:"$'\n'"$out"
41	echo "$out" | grep -q "\[hsim mmap\]" && fail "[hsim mmap] prefix must be gone:"$'\n'"$out"
42	
43	# 2b. the level is forwarded to both legs (visible in the dry-run commands):
44	#     the QEMU plugin gets log_level=N, the vsim leg gets --log-level N
45	echo "$out" | grep -q "log_level=1" || fail "fast-leg plugin missing log_level=1:"$'\n'"$out"
46	echo "$out" | grep -Eq "sim_[a-z0-9_]+ .*--log-level 1" \
47	  || fail "accurate-leg missing --log-level 1:"$'\n'"$out"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Log-level contract: driver chatter is leveled like vsim's --log-level
# (0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off; default 2=info).
#
#   1. default (info): a hybrid --dry-run shows the dry-run commands but NO
#      banner and NO mmap line.
#   2. --log-level 1 (debug): banner + mmap line appear; the mmap line uses
#      the [andesim] prefix and the retired [hsim mmap] prefix is gone.
#   3. default (info) on a real hybrid run: program output + the cycle
#      figure only -- no banner, no mmap line, no trailing PASS chatter.
#   4. an out-of-range --log-level is a clean non-zero error naming 0..6.
#
# RED-then-green smoke test, run manually during driver development. Not wired
# into run_e2e.sh.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf"
ENGINE="vsim:ax45mpv_premium"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"
[ -f "$ELF" ] || fail "missing fixture: $ELF"

# 1. default level hides the banner and the mmap line (dry-run: cheap)
out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --dry-run "$ELF" 2>&1) \
  || fail "hybrid --dry-run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "dry-run: 2 command(s)" || fail "dry-run header missing:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "model=hybrid" && fail "default level should hide the banner:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -qi "mmap" && fail "default level should hide the mmap line:"$'\n'"$out"

# 2. debug level shows them, with the [andesim] prefix (no [hsim mmap])
out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --log-level 1 --dry-run "$ELF" 2>&1) \
  || fail "hybrid --log-level 1 --dry-run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "model=hybrid" || fail "debug level missing banner:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "\[andesim\] mmap" || fail "debug level missing [andesim] mmap line:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "\[hsim mmap\]" && fail "[hsim mmap] prefix must be gone:"$'\n'"$out"

# 2b. the level is forwarded to both legs (visible in the dry-run commands):
#     the QEMU plugin gets log_level=N, the vsim leg gets --log-level N
echo "$out" | grep -q "log_level=1" || fail "fast-leg plugin missing log_level=1:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -Eq "sim_[a-z0-9_]+ .*--log-level 1" \
  || fail "accurate-leg missing --log-level 1:"$'\n'"$out"

# 2c. debug also explains the driver's decisions: engine choice reason ...
echo "$out" | grep -q "^\[andesim\] engine: $ENGINE (selected by --engine)$" \
  || fail "debug: engine decision line missing:"$'\n'"$out"

# ... and pc-trigger symbol resolution
out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine "$ENGINE" --log-level 1 --dry-run \
        --pc-start say_hello --pc-end vplat_roi_end "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf" 2>&1) \
  || fail "pc dry-run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] trigger pc: say_hello -> 0x[0-9a-fA-F]+, vplat_roi_end -> 0x[0-9a-fA-F]+$' \
  || fail "debug: pc resolution line missing:"$'\n'"$out"

# 3. default level on a real hybrid run: program output + cycle figure only;
#    the answer line uses the same [andesim] N cycles shape as cycle mode,
#    with the raw mcycle detail reserved for debug.
out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" "$ELF" 2>&1) \
  || fail "hybrid run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "hello from QEMU1" || fail "program output missing:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] [0-9]+ cycles$' || fail "cycle figure missing:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "window_cycles" && fail "old window_cycles format leaked:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "mcycle=" && fail "mcycle detail leaked at default level:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "model=hybrid" && fail "banner leaked at default level:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -qi "mmap" && fail "mmap line leaked at default level:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "^PASS:" && fail "PASS chatter leaked at default level:"$'\n'"$out"

# 3b. debug level adds the window detail line next to the answer, but the
#     exec command lines stay trace-only
out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --log-level 1 "$ELF" 2>&1) \
  || fail "hybrid --log-level 1 run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] [0-9]+ cycles$' || fail "debug: cycle figure missing:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] window: trigger=marker vsim mcycle=[0-9]+ qemu mcycle=[0-9]+$' \
  || fail "debug: window detail line missing:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "\[andesim\] exec " && fail "exec lines leaked at debug level:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "\[hybrid_handoff\] drained" \
  || fail "debug: plugin drain summary not relayed:"$'\n'"$out"

# 3c. trace level prints each leg's exact command before spawning it
out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --log-level 0 "$ELF" 2>&1) \
  || fail "hybrid --log-level 0 run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] exec fast-leg \[qemu64\]: .*qemu-system-riscv64' \
  || fail "trace: fast-leg exec line missing:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] exec accurate-leg \[vsim:ax45mpv_premium\]: .*sim_ax45mpv_premium' \
  || fail "trace: accurate-leg exec line missing:"$'\n'"$out"

# 3e. trace level prints the standalone command too (fast/cycle share
#     run_standalone): without it a wedged fast run is undiagnosable from
#     logs -- there is no later step to show the command.
out=$("$BIN" --mode fast --log-level 0 "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_exit41.elf" 2>&1)
rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 41 ] || fail "fast vplat_exit41 expected rc 41, got $rc:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] exec standalone \[qemu64\]: .*qemu-system-riscv64' \
  || fail "trace: standalone exec line missing:"$'\n'"$out"

# 3d. --log-file captures EVERY level with timestamps while the console
#     stays at its threshold (default here: still only output + answer)
LOGDIR=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$LOGDIR"' EXIT
LOGFILE="$LOGDIR/run.log"
out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" \
        --log-file "$LOGFILE" "$ELF" 2>&1) \
  || fail "hybrid --log-file run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "model=hybrid" && fail "--log-file must not raise console verbosity:"$'\n'"$out"
[ -f "$LOGFILE" ] || fail "log file not created: $LOGFILE"
grep -q "model=hybrid" "$LOGFILE" || fail "log file missing debug banner:"$'\n'"$(cat "$LOGFILE")"
grep -q "exec fast-leg" "$LOGFILE" || fail "log file missing trace exec line:"$'\n'"$(cat "$LOGFILE")"
grep -Eq "\[andesim\] [0-9]+ cycles" "$LOGFILE" || fail "log file missing answer line:"$'\n'"$(cat "$LOGFILE")"
grep -Eq '^\[20[0-9]{2}-[01][0-9]-[0-3][0-9]T' "$LOGFILE" || fail "log file lines missing timestamps:"$'\n'"$(cat "$LOGFILE")"

# 4. out-of-range level is a clean error
"$BIN" --mode fast --log-level 9 "$ELF" >/dev/null 2>&1 && fail "--log-level 9 should exit non-zero"
out=$("$BIN" --mode fast --log-level 9 "$ELF" 2>&1)
echo "$out" | grep -q "0=trace" || fail "bad --log-level error should name the scale:"$'\n'"$out"

ok "log levels + [andesim] prefix"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# --step-timeout-ms contract: overrides PlanOptions' hardcoded 90000ms
# per-leg spawn timeout, for hybrid ROIs whose cycle-accurate leg needs
# more than 90s of wall clock (e.g. a real transformer matmul).
#
#   1. default: a cheap fixture completes fine (no behavior change).
#   2. --step-timeout-ms 1: an absurdly small budget times out cleanly,
#      naming the ms value, proving the flag reaches PlanOptions.timeout_ms.
#   3. --step-timeout-ms <generous>: still completes fine (raising the
#      budget doesn't break the normal path).
#   4. a non-positive-integer value is a clean non-zero error.
#
# RED-then-green smoke test, run manually during driver development. Not
# wired into run_e2e.sh.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf"
ENGINE="vsim:ax45mpv_premium"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"
[ -f "$ELF" ] || fail "missing fixture: $ELF"

# 1. default timeout: cheap fixture is unaffected
out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" "$ELF" 2>&1) \
  || fail "default-timeout hybrid run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] [0-9]+ cycles$' || fail "default-timeout: cycle figure missing:"$'\n'"$out"

# 2. absurdly small timeout fails cleanly, naming the ms value
out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --step-timeout-ms 1 "$ELF" 2>&1)
rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && fail "--step-timeout-ms 1 should exit non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "timed out after 1 ms" || fail "timeout error should name 1 ms:"$'\n'"$out"

# 3. a generous explicit timeout still completes fine
out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --step-timeout-ms 300000 "$ELF" 2>&1) \
  || fail "--step-timeout-ms 300000 hybrid run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] [0-9]+ cycles$' || fail "generous-timeout: cycle figure missing:"$'\n'"$out"

# 4. non-positive-integer value is a clean error
out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --step-timeout-ms abc "$ELF" 2>&1)
rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && fail "--step-timeout-ms abc should exit non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q -- "--step-timeout-ms: not a positive integer" || fail "bad-value error message missing:"$'\n'"$out"

out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --step-timeout-ms 0 "$ELF" 2>&1)
rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && fail "--step-timeout-ms 0 should exit non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q -- "--step-timeout-ms: not a positive integer" || fail "zero-value error message missing:"$'\n'"$out"

ok "--step-timeout-ms overrides the hybrid per-leg spawn timeout"

content.content:
1	# Linux-Runtime Roadmap: run static glibc binaries (llama.cpp) on andesim
2	
3	Goal: a prebuilt RISC-V **static glibc** binary (built with the Andes
4	`nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d` toolchain) runs on every andesim mode
5	(fast / cycle / hybrid) **unmodified**, with real argv, and hybrid
6	measures ONE kernel iteration (marker or PC trigger) on vsim. Primary
7	target: `llama-completion` (llama.cpp's text-generation CLI, `tools/completion/`
8	in `/home/nick/work/llama.cpp`) generating text from `Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf`.
9	
10	How: a small M-mode **proxy kernel** (`vlinux.elf`, new `runtime/linux/`
11	component, pattern: riscv-pk) that loads the app ELF, builds the Linux
12	initial stack (argc/argv/envp/auxv), and answers the app's `ecall`s by
13	emulating ~30 Linux syscalls on top of the existing HTIF syscall window.
14	The hybrid transport, triggers, plugin, resume driver, and engines need
15	NO changes: the guest stays bare-metal, M-mode, paging-off, single-hart,
16	exactly the current ROI envelope.
17	
18	Non-goals (explicitly out of scope here)
19	- No real Linux kernel boot, no S/U-mode, no paging, no interrupts
20	  (that is FRS FR-109, a separate track).
21	- No threads: `clone` returns -ENOSYS; llama.cpp runs with `-t 1`
22	  (verified: at n_threads=1 ggml never calls pthread_create, and
23	  uncontended glibc mutexes never reach futex).
24	- No dynamic linking: the app must be `-static` (the toolchain ships
25	  `libc.a`; a static hello links at vaddr 0x50000, inside DRAM).
26	- Full 3.8 GB Bonsai-27B residency is blocked by the 2 GiB DRAM window;
27	  that lift is feature U10 (platform track). Until then use a
28	  layer-sliced GGUF (U11) - per-layer kernel shapes are identical.
29	  NOT on the critical path: the primary target Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf
30	  (572 MB) fits the 2 GiB window directly, no slicing needed. U10/U11
31	  stay documented as the 27B stretch-goal track, unblocked but optional.

65	## Guest memory map (vlinux contract, DRAM base 0x0)
66	
67	| Region                  | Range                          | Owner |
68	|-------------------------|--------------------------------|-------|
69	| ILM aperture            | 0x0000_0000 .. 0x0000_FFFF     | platform (apps link at >= 0x10000, no overlap) |
70	| App image (PT_LOADs)    | link base (0x10000/0x50000) .. | app ELF; loader rejects overlap with vlinux |
71	| brk arena               | app image end .. 0x0200_0000   | `brk` grows up; when full glibc malloc falls back to mmap |
72	| vlinux                  | 0x0200_0000 .. 0x0220_0000     | proxy text/data/bss + its own stack (2 MB) |
73	| mmap arena              | 0x0220_0000 .. initial stack   | grows DOWN from just below the app stack |
74	| App initial stack       | top 8 MB below `mem_size`      | built by loader (argc/argv/envp/auxv) |
75	| V-scratch               | `mem_size` .. +4 KB            | hybrid V transport (existing, untouched) |
76	
77	DLM aperture 0x200000..0x207fff sits inside the app-image range; content
78	across it is transported by the existing LM sidecars (probe-verified).
79	Every arena bound is checked: exhaustion returns -ENOMEM / fails loudly
80	(no silent vplat-style `_sbrk` corruption).

385	  so any C code in the trap handler that used gp-relative addressing (any
386	  static/global variable) ran with WHATEVER gp was active at the moment
387	  of the trap -- the APP's own gp, a different linked image's value, once
388	  the app is running. Silent in U3 (syscall.c had zero global variables,
389	  so nothing was gp-relative yet); U4's `mm.c` globals (`g_brk_cur` etc.)
390	  hit it immediately: `mm_init()` (running before the app starts, with
391	  vlinux's own correct gp) set them correctly, but `sys_brk()` (running
392	  later, from the trap handler, with the APP's gp) computed a completely
393	  different address for "the same" variable and read back zero every
394	  time. Fixed with the same `.option norelax` / `lla gp,
395	  __global_pointer$` sequence crt0.S already uses at boot, inserted into
396	  `m_trap_entry` right before `call handle_trap` -- a no-op for every
397	  trap that already shares one image with its handler (every existing
398	  vplat fixture, and U3's own fixture, which is why this was never
399	  visible before).

401	  A second, separate real bug (arena-boundary arithmetic, not gp-related):
402	  **the mmap arena's start point overlapped the app's own live stack.**
403	  `stack.c`'s initial-stack builder started writing AT `mem_size -
404	  STACK_RESERVE` -- meant to be the stack's FLOOR (the boundary
405	  `mm.c`'s mmap arena must not cross) -- instead of at `mem_size` (the
406	  true top, with the reserved 8 MiB as growth headroom below it). The
407	  build's own content therefore immediately spilled below the floor, and
408	  the very first substantial `mmap()` call (malloc's 1 MiB request)
409	  landed exactly on top of the app's own already-in-use stack and
410	  zeroed it (mmap returns zeroed pages), corrupting a saved return
411	  address a few calls later. Fixed by starting the build at `mem_size`
412	  instead. Caught because the crash was a "return to a garbage stack
413	  address" pattern immediately downstream of the first big `mmap` call,
414	  not an obvious out-of-bounds fault -- the value that got zeroed was a
415	  legitimate stack slot the app hadn't returned through yet.
