758	  run (`pause()` also needed a matching guard, since it unconditionally
759	  `thrd.join()`s otherwise). This is llama.cpp SOURCE, not vlinux -
760	  applied directly to the `/home/nick/work/llama.cpp` checkout (untracked
761	  by this repo); anyone rebuilding llama-completion from a fresh
762	  checkout needs to re-apply it (documented in USER_GUIDE.md, not just
763	  here).
764	
765	  **Memory sizing: the roadmap's own "1G covers it" estimate was wrong,
766	  found by direct measurement.** The model's file-backed mmap (572 MB)
767	  plus its KV cache buffer (576 MB at `-c 512`, llama.cpp's
768	  `common_fit_params` computes this from context size) together exceed
769	  the `--runtime linux` default of 1G - confirmed by an actual failure
770	  (`ggml_aligned_malloc: insufficient memory`), not assumed. `--mem-size
771	  2G` plus an explicit `-c 512` (bounding the KV cache; the model's own
772	  default context, 32768, would need much more memory for no benefit on
773	  a short prompt) is the verified-working configuration.
774	
775	  Real generation quality/performance data point (this host, `ax45mpv_premium`-
776	  synced QEMU, functional not cycle-accurate): model load ~93s, prompt
777	  eval ~165s (5 tokens), generation ~36.6s/token. `-n 32` takes on the
778	  order of 20+ minutes total - QEMU's functional RVV emulation of a real
779	  4B-parameter model's matrix math is slow by design (fast mode trades
780	  throughput for cycle-independent functional correctness); this is
781	  exactly why U9's hybrid ROI measures ONE kernel iteration, not a whole
782	  token, let alone 32.
783	
784	  Same documented, non-blocking gap as every U4+ glibc fixture: `exit()`
785	  may crash in its handler-list walk AFTER all real work (generation,
786	  perf stats) is already complete and printed.
787	  `test_vlinux_llama_smoke.sh` accepts either outcome, matching every
788	  other U4+ test's acceptance pattern.
789	
790	  Full regression (14 driver C++ unit tests including the manifest
791	  extra-argv encoding tests, 43 tests/andes_sim + tests/vplat scripts
792	  with test_andes_sim_runtime_linux.sh's assertion flipped for the new
793	  argv-threading contract, all 6 tests/vlinux/*.sh) stayed green
794	  throughout; test_vlinux_llama_smoke.sh itself is manual-tier (needs
795	  LINUX_TOOLCHAIN + a pre-built llama-completion + the GGUF model, none
796	  of which the automated sweep provides) but was run manually to
797	  completion during this session, twice (`-n 4` and `-n 32`).
798	
799	## U9. Hybrid: one-kernel-iteration ROI
800	
801	- Description: the actual goal. Two supported ways to delimit ONE
802	  iteration: (a) marker build - a 5-line llama.cpp patch snippet
803	  (documented, kept in docs/) adds `<andesim/ROI.h>` markers around the
804	  target op guarded by an iteration counter (`if (++n == K)`), markers
805	  are HINT NOPs so the same binary still runs everywhere; (b) no-source
806	  route - `andesim profile` finds the hot loop, then `--trigger pc
807	  --pc-start/--pc-end` with symbols resolved from the app ELF (U2).
808	  Results print INSIDE the ROI (nothing after ROI-end executes - the
809	  existing contract). Expectation note for the guide: one Bonsai-4B-shape
810	  (2560 embed) q1_0 matvec is smaller than the original 27B estimate
811	  (~10-100 M cycles there) -> likely faster than minutes-to-~1h at
812	  vsim's 9-50 kHz, confirm actual figure once measured; a full token
813	  would still be far too slow - that is why we measure one iteration.
814	- Input/Output: hybrid run of a marker'd glibc matvec fixture (and then
815	  llama-completion with the counter patch) prints in-ROI checksum +
816	  `[andesim] N cycles`, N stable across two runs (deterministic single hart).
817	- Key files: docs/USER_GUIDE.md, docs/llama_roi_howto.md (new, with the
818	  counter-marker snippet), tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_hybrid_roi.sh
819	- Depends on: U4 (fixture), U8 (llama-completion variant)
820	- State: PLANNED
821	
822	## U10. Platform track: DRAM window >= 6 GB (full Bonsai-27B) [stretch, off critical path]
823	
824	- Description: lift the 2 GiB ceiling so the untouched 3.8 GB GGUF +
825	  arenas (~4.5 GB) fit. Three coordinated changes: (1) qemu_andesim
826	  andes_ae350 machine model DRAM window (currently "Cannot model more
827	  than 2GB RAM"); (2) vsim RTL platform address decode for the same
828	  window (external hybrid_vsim/RTL config - needs its own
829	  investigation: is the testbench memory size parameterizable per
830	  engine build?); (3) driver `max_program_mem_bytes()` (driver/
831	  shm.cpp:91), memmap print, and the vlinux arena bounds (already
832	  mem_size-driven). ABI is u64 addresses throughout - no wire change.
833	  First step is a spike: confirm the RTL decode location and cost; if
834	  the RTL cannot grow, evaluate a high-DRAM alias window instead.
835	- Input/Output: `--mem-size 6G` accepted; U8 smoke passes with the full
836	  Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf resident; U9 measures its layer-0 kernel.
837	- Key files: qemu_andesim (hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c), hybrid_vsim repo,
838	  driver/shm.cpp, driver/cmd_run.cpp, docs/USER_GUIDE.md
839	- Depends on: independent of U0-U9 (parallel track). NOT needed for the
840	  primary Bonsai-4B goal (fits 2 GiB directly) - only for a 27B revisit.
841	- State: PLANNED
842	
843	## U11. Bridge tool: GGUF layer-slice script (host side) [stretch, off critical path]
844	
845	- Description: `scripts/gguf_slice.py` (gguf-py): keep the first K
846	  transformer blocks + embeddings + output head, rewrite
847	  `block_count`/tensor list, so Bonsai-27B becomes a <= 1.5 GB model
848	  whose per-layer kernel SHAPES are identical to the real one. This is
849	  the U8/U9 workload until U10 lands. Sliced-model quality is garbage
850	  (fine - we measure kernels, not perplexity).
851	- Input/Output: `python scripts/gguf_slice.py Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf 12`
852	  -> `Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.k12.gguf`, loads in stock llama.cpp on the host,
853	  `llama-completion` runs on it.
854	- Key files: scripts/gguf_slice.py (new)
855	- Test: host-side pytest-style check of tensor count + metadata.
856	- Depends on: nothing (host tool). NOT needed for the primary Bonsai-4B
857	  goal - only for a 27B revisit (see U10).
858	- State: PLANNED
859	
860	---
861	
862	Rollout: one feature per session, TDD-first - every feature's contract
863	above is a grep-able stdout/exit-code check, so its RED test goes in
864	tests/vlinux/ (or tests/andes_sim/ for U2) before the implementation.
865	Update docs/USER_GUIDE.md as each lands.
866	
867	Order: U0 -> U1 -> U2 -> U3 -> U4 -> U5 -> {U6, U7} -> U8 -> U9. That is
868	the full path to the primary goal (llama-completion + Bonsai-4B,
869	fast leg then hybrid ROI). U10 and U11 are an optional 27B stretch
870	track, off the critical path entirely (U11 any time; U10 is the only
871	cross-repo item) - only worth picking up if/when Bonsai-27B specifically
872	is requested.
873	
874	Compound effect: U0-U7 give andesim a general "run Linux userspace
875	binaries" capability - every future glibc workload (SPEC kernels,
876	libnn perf tests, any vendor benchmark) reuses vlinux with zero
877	per-app porting, and U9's counter-marker recipe becomes the standard
878	way to cycle-measure ONE iteration of any hot kernel inside a large
879	application. When FR-109 (real Linux, S/U+paging) eventually lands,
880	its acceptance workloads and test fixtures are already here.

# Linux-Runtime Roadmap: run static glibc binaries (llama.cpp) on andesim

Goal: a prebuilt RISC-V **static glibc** binary (built with the Andes
`nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d` toolchain) runs on every andesim mode
(fast / cycle / hybrid) **unmodified**, with real argv, and hybrid
measures ONE kernel iteration (marker or PC trigger) on vsim. Primary
target: `llama-completion` (llama.cpp's text-generation CLI, `tools/completion/`
in `/home/nick/work/llama.cpp`) generating text from `Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf`.

How: a small M-mode **proxy kernel** (`vlinux.elf`, new `runtime/linux/`
component, pattern: riscv-pk) that loads the app ELF, builds the Linux
initial stack (argc/argv/envp/auxv), and answers the app's `ecall`s by
emulating ~30 Linux syscalls on top of the existing HTIF syscall window.
The hybrid transport, triggers, plugin, resume driver, and engines need
NO changes: the guest stays bare-metal, M-mode, paging-off, single-hart,
exactly the current ROI envelope.

Non-goals (explicitly out of scope here)
- No real Linux kernel boot, no S/U-mode, no paging, no interrupts
  (that is FRS FR-109, a separate track).
- No threads: `clone` returns -ENOSYS; llama.cpp runs with `-t 1`
  (verified: at n_threads=1 ggml never calls pthread_create, and
  uncontended glibc mutexes never reach futex).
- No dynamic linking: the app must be `-static` (the toolchain ships
  `libc.a`; a static hello links at vaddr 0x50000, inside DRAM).
- Full 3.8 GB Bonsai-27B residency is blocked by the 2 GiB DRAM window;
  that lift is feature U10 (platform track). Until then use a
  layer-sliced GGUF (U11) - per-layer kernel shapes are identical.
  NOT on the critical path: the primary target Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf
  (572 MB) fits the 2 GiB window directly, no slicing needed. U10/U11
  stay documented as the 27B stretch-goal track, unblocked but optional.

Verified facts this design stands on (probed 2026-07-15)
- HTIF window file I/O works on QEMU + all 3 vsim engines, 26 MB/s,
  1984 B/chunk; `_gettimeofday` works.
- C++ exceptions/ctors work bare-metal; printf INSIDE the ROI works on
  the vsim leg; a 3.6 MB image crossing the DLM window (0x200000)
  survives the handoff bit-exact.
- Hybrid QEMU leg is engine-synced (`-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512`), no
  zfh/zvfh; RTL is ELEN=32. llama.cpp must be built with
  `GGML_RV_ZFH=OFF GGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF -mext-zvlsseg`.
- Standalone fast mode pins `-cpu andes-ax46mpv` (Zce, no Zcd): FP code
  from the default multilib traps there. vlinux runs are engine-synced
  or must pass `-- -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` until U2 fixes the
  default for `--runtime linux`.
- Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf is architecture `qwen3` (2560 embed, 36 layers,
  32 heads, 32768 ctx, 398 tensors) - a standard llama.cpp arch, no
  custom model code needed. Confirmed end-to-end OUTSIDE andesim
  (2026-07-15): `/home/nick/work/llama.cpp/run-rv64-qemu.sh` runs the
  cross-compiled `llama-completion` under Andes's linux-user QEMU
  (`qemu-riscv64`, syscall translation, no system emulation - a
  functional-only sanity check, unrelated to andesim's hybrid pipeline)
  and it generates correct text at `-t 1` ("The capital of France is
  Paris."), proving the model loads and every ggml op it needs already
  runs on RVV. That build (`build-rv64/`, `build-rv64-noomp/`) is
  **dynamic** (`BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON`) with `GGML_RV_ZFH/ZVFH/CPU_REPACK=ON`
  - the opposite link mode and feature set vlinux needs (static,
  those three OFF per the line above), so U8 still needs its own build;
  this only de-risks the syscall/threading/model-format assumptions.
- `build-rv64-baremetal/` (a prior newlib-baremetal attempt via
  `cmake/riscv64-andes-elf-newlib-gcc.cmake`) is abandoned: the
  toolchain file no longer exists and it produced zero binaries. Not a
  usable shortcut around vlinux; ignore that directory.

## Guest memory map (vlinux contract, DRAM base 0x0)

| Region                  | Range                          | Owner |
|-------------------------|--------------------------------|-------|
| ILM aperture            | 0x0000_0000 .. 0x0000_FFFF     | platform (apps link at >= 0x10000, no overlap) |
| App image (PT_LOADs)    | link base (0x10000/0x50000) .. | app ELF; loader rejects overlap with vlinux |
| brk arena               | app image end .. 0x0200_0000   | `brk` grows up; when full glibc malloc falls back to mmap |
| vlinux                  | 0x0200_0000 .. 0x0220_0000     | proxy text/data/bss + its own stack (2 MB) |
| mmap arena              | 0x0220_0000 .. initial stack   | grows DOWN from just below the app stack |
| App initial stack       | top 8 MB below `mem_size`      | built by loader (argc/argv/envp/auxv) |
| V-scratch               | `mem_size` .. +4 KB            | hybrid V transport (existing, untouched) |

DLM aperture 0x200000..0x207fff sits inside the app-image range; content
across it is transported by the existing LM sidecars (probe-verified).
Every arena bound is checked: exhaustion returns -ENOMEM / fails loudly
(no silent vplat-style `_sbrk` corruption).

---

## U0. Extract shared HTIF window client (structural)

- Description: move the window protocol client (`win_syscall`, slot
  staging, chunk loop) and `uart_putc` out of `runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`
  into `runtime/htif_client.{c,h}` so vplat and vlinux share one
  implementation. No behavior change.
- Input/Output: existing vplat fixtures before == after.
- Key files: runtime/htif_client.c (new), runtime/htif_client.h (new),
  runtime/vplat_syscalls.c, runtime/Makefile
- Test: existing tests/vplat/*.sh all stay green (that IS the test).
- Depends on: nothing
- State: DONE (2026-07-15) - htif_uart_putc/htif_syscall/htif_win_*/
  htif_call_str*/htif_write/htif_read now live in runtime/htif_client.{c,h};
  vplat_syscalls.c is a thin newlib adapter over them. All 12
  tests/vplat/*.sh green before and after (byte-identical output).

## U1. vlinux skeleton: boot, banner, manifest reader

- Description: new `runtime/linux/` payload with its own crt.S + linker
  script at 0x0200_0000 (built with HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN, freestanding +
  newlib for internal printf). Boots via `-bios vlinux.elf` on fast and
  cycle, enables caches/FS/VS/UNA (the crt0 duties, so the existing
  mcache_ctl/write-mask transport keeps working), prints a banner, reads
  the `.manifest` section (magic+version, mem_size, app path, argv,
  envp; "empty manifest" default = banner + exit 0), exits via
  SimControl.
- Input/Output: `vlinux.elf` with default manifest -> stdout contains
  `vlinux: boot ok mem=<N>M` and exit code 0 on BOTH fast and cycle.
- Key files: runtime/linux/{crt.S,vlinux.ld,main.c,manifest.h},
  runtime/linux/Makefile, scripts/build_all.sh
- Test: tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_boot.sh (fast leg + sim_ax45mpv_premium)
- Depends on: U0
- State: DONE (2026-07-15) - runtime/linux/{manifest.h,main.c,vlinux.ld,
  Makefile} + tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_boot.sh + scripts/build_all.sh
  `vlinux` target. No new crt.S: ../crt0.S (shared with vplat) enables
  icache/dcache/mstatus.FS+VS/mmisc_ctl.UNA using only PC-relative
  addressing and a linker-provided `_stack` symbol, so it is already
  link-address-agnostic and vlinux.ld's `PROVIDE(_stack = 0x02200000)` +
  `. = 0x02000000` base retarget it with zero new code (CLAUDE.md: don't
  duplicate code). vlinux.elf links main.c straight against
  build/runtime/{crt0.o,libandesim_runtime.a} (no -specs=andesim.specs -
  vlinux is a kernel image, not a user program built with the two-flag
  command). Confirmed via research (QEMU andes_ae350.c +
  riscv_setup_rom_reset_vec, and the external vsim's load_elf) that
  `-bios` on both engines boots from the ELF's own e_entry with no reset
  stub needed at any fixed low address - 0x0200_0000 "just works". Test
  runs vlinux.elf as a plain standalone ELF (no --runtime flag yet -
  that's U2): `./andesim run --mode fast` + `sim_ax45mpv_premium` direct,
  same pattern as tests/vplat/test_vplat_f1.sh + f2.sh. All 12
  tests/vplat/*.sh + the build_all.sh/release_surface driver contract
  tests stay green.

## U2. Driver: `--runtime linux` plumbing

- Description: new run flag. The driver copies vlinux.elf per run and
  `objcopy --update-section .manifest=<blob>` (toolchain objcopy from
  config.env) with: absolute app ELF path, `mem_size`, argv[0..n] (from
  `-- <args...>`, now ALLOWED in hybrid for the linux runtime - they are
  app argv, not engine argv), minimal envp. The manifested vlinux.elf is
  what every leg loads, so fast/cycle/hybrid stay uniform. Linux runtime
  defaults: `--mem-size 1G`; standalone fast leg uses the engine-synced
  CPU (`andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512`), not the ax46 default. `--pc-start/end`
  symbols resolve against the APP ELF in this mode.
- Input/Output: `./andesim run --mode fast --runtime linux app.elf -- -m x.gguf -t 1`
  -> dry-run prints the objcopy step + `-bios <workdir>/vlinux-run.elf`;
  manifest blob round-trips (dump tool or readelf grep).
- Key files: driver/cli.cpp, driver/cmd_run.cpp, driver/run_plan.cpp,
  driver/manifest.cpp (new), docs/USER_GUIDE.md
- Test: tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_runtime_linux.sh (dry-run
  contract + manifest content grep)
- Depends on: U1
- State: DONE (2026-07-15) - driver/{manifest.hpp,manifest.cpp,tempdir.hpp,
  tempdir.cpp} (new) + `--runtime` on Cli (cli.hpp/cli.cpp) +
  run_fast/run_standalone wiring in cmd_run.cpp +
  tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_runtime_linux.sh + docs/USER_GUIDE.md 5.12.
  Three deliberate scope cuts from the paragraph above, each documented at
  its call site:
  1. **`--mode fast` only.** `driver/run_plan.cpp` (hybrid's multi-leg
     executor) turned out NOT to need touching: cycle/hybrid go through a
     different code path than fast/cycle's `run_standalone`, and the
     roadmap's own Order line (U0->...->U8 all run on the fast leg; hybrid
     wiring is explicitly U9) means nothing downstream needs cycle/hybrid
     support yet. `cmd_run()` REJECTS `--runtime` with anything but
     `--mode fast` (a clear error naming U9), rather than silently
     ignoring it -- an untested silent accept would be worse than a loud
     not-yet-supported.
  2. **argv/envp deferred to U3.** `runtime/linux/manifest.h`'s own U1-era
     comment already called this: "argv/envp arrive in a later manifest
     version once U3 needs them." Building a wire format for them now, with
     no consumer (vlinux's loader, U3) to validate the design against, is
     exactly the untested-speculative-format risk TDD guards against -- a
     wrong guess would just be redone at U3. `-- <args...>` still PARSES
     (matches the roadmap's own example invocation) but `cmd_run.cpp` warns
     and drops it rather than forwarding it into QEMU's own CLI, where it
     would be misparsed as engine flags (`-m x.gguf` is not a memory size).
  3. **Staged `vlinux-run.elf` is not cleaned up.** `fast`'s exec_passthrough
     execve()s and never returns, so nothing can rm the per-run temp workdir
     afterward; this mirrors run_plan.cpp's own qemu.cfg staging (real
     prep-work file, spawned unconditionally including under --dry-run) but
     deliberately differs on cleanup -- run_plan deletes its workdir even on
     a dry run (its qemu.cfg is disposable/re-derivable), whereas
     vlinux-run.elf is the actual `-bios` target if `--dry-run` is dropped
     and the run repeats for real, and the U2 contract itself
     ("manifest blob round-trips... readelf grep") only works if the file
     is still on disk after the command returns. Net effect: both dry-run
     and a real run leave one small workdir under the system temp dir per
     invocation -- a known, documented, low-severity leak (a few MB each),
     not pruned (no test demands it; a future session can add the same
     `prune_repro_bundles`-style cap run_plan.cpp already has for repro
     bundles, if it becomes a problem).

  `--runtime linux` also defaults `--mem-size` to `1G` and pins the
  standalone fast leg's CPU to `andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` (engine-synced,
  not the ax46 vplat default), exactly as specified above. `stage_linux_runtime`
  needs `build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf` (U1's artifact) and `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN`
  (for `objcopy`); both are checked with a clear error, not a crash.

## U3. ELF loader + Linux initial stack + auxv

- Description: vlinux HTIF-reads the app ELF (26 MB/s -> ~0.5 s for a
  10 MB binary), maps PT_LOADs (reject overlap with vlinux/V-scratch/
  window), zeroes BSS tails, builds the initial stack at the top of the
  app arena: argc/argv/envp then auxv (AT_PHDR/PHENT/PHNUM from the
  loaded headers, AT_ENTRY, AT_PAGESZ=4096, AT_RANDOM 16 bytes,
  AT_HWCAP=IMAFDCV bits, AT_UID/GID/EUID/EGID=0, AT_SECURE=0,
  AT_EXECFN), sets sp, jumps to the app entry in M-mode.
- Input/Output: a -nostdlib linux-ABI asm/C fixture (reads argc/argv
  from sp, calls raw `write(1,...)` + `exit_group`) prints its argv and
  auxv AT_PAGESZ. Proves loader+stack with only 2 syscalls, before glibc.
- Key files: runtime/linux/{loader.c,stack.c}, tests/fixtures Makefile
  (new LINUX_TOOLCHAIN fixtures; config.env.example gains
  LINUX_TOOLCHAIN=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast542/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d)
- Test: tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_loader.sh (fast + cycle, argv echo)
- Depends on: U1, U2
- State: DONE (2026-07-15) - runtime/linux/{loader.h,loader.c,stack.h,
  stack.c,syscall.c} (new) + runtime/ecall_hook.h (new, shared) +
  runtime/handler.c (extended) + runtime/linux/{main.c,Makefile,vlinux.ld}
  (extended) + tests/fixtures/{rt_linux_argv.c,Makefile} (new fixture) +
  tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_loader.sh. `andesim run --mode fast --runtime
  linux app.elf` now loads `app.elf`'s PT_LOADs, builds the Linux initial
  stack + auxv, and jumps to its entry in M-mode; verified on BOTH fast
  (QEMU) and cycle (the same staged vlinux-run.elf run directly on
  sim_ax45mpv_premium, U1's dual-engine pattern).

  Scope cuts (each also inline-commented at its call site):
  1. **No LINUX_TOOLCHAIN dependency yet.** The roadmap's own fixture is
     `-nostdlib` (no libc at all -- a naked `_start` reads argc/argv/auxv off
     sp and issues raw `ecall`s), so it needs no glibc: built with the
     ordinary bare-metal HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN, same as every other asm fixture.
     LINUX_TOOLCHAIN is deferred to U4, the first feature with an actual
     glibc-linked fixture ("Proves loader+stack ... before glibc" was the
     roadmap's own phrase for this).
  2. **argv stays `[app_path]`.** No manifest format change: real multi-arg
     argv (the eventual `-m model.gguf -t 1`) is deferred to whenever U8
     actually needs it, consistent with U2's own argv/envp deferral -
     inventing a wire format now, with no consumer to validate it against,
     risks getting redone anyway.
  3. **V-scratch/window overlap checks deferred to U9.** loader.c rejects
     PT_LOAD overlap with vlinux's own region (0x0200_0000..0x0220_0000, via
     a `_vlinux_base`/`_stack` linker-symbol pair - one source of truth, not
     a duplicated magic address) but not yet the V-scratch page or the HTIF
     window MMIO range, since standalone fast/cycle (the only wired modes)
     never reserve V-scratch at all - that only matters once U9 wires
     `--runtime linux` under hybrid.
  4. **`_sbrk`'s brk arena is not app-arena-aware.** vplat_syscalls.c's
     `_sbrk` still grows from vlinux's OWN `_end`, not the app's. Harmless
     today (the U3 fixture never calls malloc/brk) but a real gap for U4+,
     when a glibc app's malloc will need the app's own brk arena
     (roadmap: "app image end .. 0x0200_0000"), not vlinux's leftover space.

  Two real bugs found and fixed via the fixture, worth remembering:
  1. **`const` on `g_manifest` silently broke the loader.** U1 declared
     `g_manifest` plain `const` for section placement; at -O1 GCC constant-
     folded every read back to the empty-string initializer, since nothing
     in the visible program ever writes it - U2's post-link `objcopy
     --update-section` patch is invisible to the compiler. vlinux booted
     the "empty manifest" banner path even with a fully-correct staged
     app_path on disk. Fixed with `const volatile` (never written by this
     program, but its value changes through means outside the compiler's
     view) + a one-time snapshot into plain locals in `main()` so
     loader.c/stack.c see ordinary unqualified types.
  2. **Missing `fence.i` before jumping to freshly-loaded code.** The app's
     code is written via ordinary guest stores (through the D-cache crt0.S

  `_dl_fini` registration made during `__libc_start_main`, since it is the
  FIRST handler registered (LIFO: last one `__run_exit_handlers` runs) and

  cleanup, ...) already ran successfully -- has a function-pointer field
  that is not a valid code address (a stack-range value) and faults
  (illegal instruction) when called. This happens identically for a
  completely empty `int main(){return 0;}` static binary, so it is
  unconditional, environment-level glibc startup behavior, not anything
  about THIS fixture.

  session does not repeat the work): live-compared against a native
  x86-64 static glibc build of the identical trivial program (same GCC,
  host GDB). CONFIRMED via GDB there that x86-64 stores this exact field
  MANGLED (an equally nonsensical raw value) and its `__run_exit_handlers`
  demangles it right before the call: `ror rax,0x11` then
  `xor rax, fs:0x30` (a TLS-relative per-process pointer guard,
  `__pointer_chk_guard`) -- x86-64's copy of this same trivial binary
  exits 0 cleanly. The riscv64 vendor toolchain's disassembly of the
  IDENTICAL code path (confirmed via objdump, both the `ef_on`/flavor-2
  and `ef_cxa`/flavor-4 branches of `__run_exit_handlers`) has NO
  demangle step at all between loading the field and calling through it.

  something upstream computes the wrong raw address at registration --
  most likely a weak-symbol/GOT resolution issue specific to `_dl_fini`
  on a static non-PIE riscv64 binary) or (b) mangles at registration but
  the riscv64 `__run_exit_handlers` was miscompiled without its demangle

  test, so this acceptance does not mask a future, different regression.

  and break on the actual `__cxa_atexit`/`_dl_fini` registration site

  there, before deciding whether the fix belongs in vlinux (unlikely,
  nothing here controls this) or requires a toolchain report/rebuild.

  One more real bug found and fixed via this fixture (same class as U3's
  two): **`gp` not reloaded on trap entry** -- `trap.S`'s `m_trap_entry`
  saved/restored `gp` (x3) around a trap but never reloaded it to
  vlinux's OWN `__global_pointer$` before running `handle_trap`'s C code,
  so any C code in the trap handler that used gp-relative addressing (any
  static/global variable) ran with WHATEVER gp was active at the moment
  of the trap -- the APP's own gp, a different linked image's value, once
  the app is running. Silent in U3 (syscall.c had zero global variables,
  so nothing was gp-relative yet); U4's `mm.c` globals (`g_brk_cur` etc.)
  hit it immediately: `mm_init()` (running before the app starts, with
  vlinux's own correct gp) set them correctly, but `sys_brk()` (running
  later, from the trap handler, with the APP's gp) computed a completely
  different address for "the same" variable and read back zero every
  time. Fixed with the same `.option norelax` / `lla gp,
  __global_pointer$` sequence crt0.S already uses at boot, inserted into
  `m_trap_entry` right before `call handle_trap` -- a no-op for every
  trap that already shares one image with its handler (every existing
  vplat fixture, and U3's own fixture, which is why this was never
  visible before).

  A second, separate real bug (arena-boundary arithmetic, not gp-related):
  **the mmap arena's start point overlapped the app's own live stack.**
  `stack.c`'s initial-stack builder started writing AT `mem_size -
  STACK_RESERVE` -- meant to be the stack's FLOOR (the boundary
  `mm.c`'s mmap arena must not cross) -- instead of at `mem_size` (the
  true top, with the reserved 8 MiB as growth headroom below it). The
  build's own content therefore immediately spilled below the floor, and
  the very first substantial `mmap()` call (malloc's 1 MiB request)
  landed exactly on top of the app's own already-in-use stack and
  zeroed it (mmap returns zeroed pages), corrupting a saved return
  address a few calls later. Fixed by starting the build at `mem_size`
  instead. Caught because the crash was a "return to a garbage stack
  address" pattern immediately downstream of the first big `mmap` call,
  not an obvious out-of-bounds fault -- the value that got zeroed was a
  legitimate stack slot the app hadn't returned through yet.

  Two ABI-translation facts this feature stands on, verified against
  LINUX_TOOLCHAIN's own sysroot headers rather than assumed (asm-generic/
  unistd.h for every syscall number, asm-generic/stat.h and bits/types/
  struct_statx.h for the struct layouts, bits/fcntl-linux.h for the O_*
  bit values):
  1. **The HTIF host's open/openat handlers speak newlib's (BSD-derived)
     O_* flag bits, not Linux's.** vplat (newlib) already matched this
     convention; a static-glibc app's `flags` argument uses the Linux
     bit layout instead (only the low 2 access-mode bits agree -- O_CREAT
     is 0x40 in Linux vs 0x200 in newlib, etc.). `linux_to_newlib_open_flags()`
     translates at the syscall boundary -- exactly a proxy kernel's job,
     not a workaround. Missing this would silently drop O_CREAT
     (`andes_ae350.c`'s own comment documents this exact failure mode for
     the untranslated case) and `fopen(path, "w")` would fail ENOENT.
  2. **The HTIF host's fstat/fstatat handlers fill exactly two fixed
     byte offsets in whatever buffer address they are given -- st_mode
     (u32 @ +4) and st_size (u64 @ +16) -- not a whole-struct bounce**
     (`andes_ae350.c andesim_store_guest_stat`, matching vsim's mirror).
     Those offsets happen to line up with newlib's own `struct stat`
     (which is what the existing vplat client relies on), but Linux's
     riscv64 `struct stat` puts st_mode at +16 and st_size at +48 --
     completely different layout. `fill_stat_from_host()`/`sys_statx()`
     read the host's two fields into a small scratch buffer, then
     construct a real Linux-shaped `struct stat`/`struct statx` at the
     correct offsets (zeroing everything not known; `statx`'s `stx_mask`
     correctly reports only the fields actually filled, per the statx(2)
     contract -- not a shortcut). Also verified: `faccessat` (syscall 48)
     takes exactly 3 arguments at the raw-syscall ABI level (dirfd, path,
     mode) -- no flags, unlike the `faccessat()` library wrapper, which
     implements `AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW`/`AT_EACCESS` itself in userspace --
     so the 4th register is never forwarded as flags (would be garbage).
     `getcwd`'s host op returns a buffer ADDRESS-or-0 (a `char*`-returning
     convention, shared with vplat's own `_getcwd`), translated to the
     real `getcwd(2)` syscall's "bytes written including NUL" return by
     measuring the string vlinux just read back.

  One real bug found and fixed (same class as U3/U4's: fast tolerates it,
  the cycle-accurate RTL correctly rejects it): **`htif_win_load` is
  documented (`htif_client.h`) as u64-load-only with an 8-aligned `woff`
  requirement** (its own implementation dereferences a `uint64_t*` at
  `WIN_DATA_VA+woff`). The first cut of the mode/size extraction called
  `htif_win_load(&m, woff+4, 4)` -- a 4-byte read at a non-8-aligned
  offset. QEMU's byte-addressable MMIO model silently tolerated it and
  returned the right bytes anyway, so the fast leg passed outright; the
  cycle-accurate engine's real uncached-device bus logic correctly
  faulted (load access fault, mcause=5, mtval pointing exactly at the
  misaligned window address) on the illegal access pattern. Fixed by
  loading the whole 24-byte aligned block in one compliant call and
  extracting st_mode/st_size locally via little-endian shifts -- the
  third occurrence of this exact "fast is permissive, cycle enforces the
  real hardware contract" pattern in this roadmap (U3: `fence.i`; U4: `gp`

  class of bug whenever new HTIF/DMI-adjacent code is added.

    trusting the math): test_vlinux_loader.sh now passes 3 extra args
    (argc==4) instead of U3's original 2, specifically to exercise the
    new padding branch, not just re-test the old argc==1 coincidence -
    matches the by-now-established pattern of never trusting an
    alignment-sensitive change on fast alone.

    needed updating: its old assertion ("should warn argv is not
    threaded yet") became a real regression once this landed - flipped
    to assert the OPPOSITE (no such warning) plus that the staged
    manifest's `.manifest` section actually contains the extra argv
    bytes (readelf -p grep for `x.gguf`).

  binary against `--help` then the real model** (the same closed-loop

  riscv_hwprobe): `futex`(98), `sysinfo`(179), `fadvise64`(223),
  `madvise`(233).
  - **`futex`**: even at `-t 1`, glibc's OWN internal locking (malloc
    arena locks, static-init guards, ...) uses futex-based mutexes
    pervasively, not just for explicit application threading - this was
    NOT anticipated by the roadmap's own "-t 1 verified: uncontended
    glibc mutexes never reach futex" note, which turned out to be true

    contract explicitly requires callers to tolerate - spec-legal, not
    a shortcut), FUTEX_WAKE(_BITSET) "0 waiters woken" (there never are
    any), FUTEX_LOCK_PI/TRYLOCK_PI/UNLOCK_PI "success" (0 is their
    success code too) - all correct because a single-hart, single-thread
    system can never have real contention to get wrong.
  - **`sysinfo`/`fadvise64`/`madvise`**: straightforward. sysinfo reports

    sizing heuristic, not a correctness-critical value) and zero/absent

    shared/buffer/highmem, process count). fadvise64/madvise are pure
    access-pattern hints with no readahead/cache policy to tune, so both
    are accepted no-ops - the same "HINT is safe as a no-op" philosophy
    the ROI markers themselves rely on.

  the roadmap's own text**: `sys_mmap`'s file-backed path (U7) only
  accepted `MAP_PRIVATE`, matching the roadmap's own U7 description

  description was a guess that turned out wrong, caught immediately by
  running the real binary (`mmap failed: Function not implemented`), not
  discovered by re-reading the roadmap text more carefully. Fixed by
  accepting `MAP_SHARED` whenever `PROT_WRITE` is not requested: for a
  read-only mapping there is no OBSERVABLE difference between
  `MAP_PRIVATE` and `MAP_SHARED` (the distinction is entirely about
  write visibility, which never applies to a read-only mapping) - a
  genuinely correct fix, not a permissive relaxation. A writable
  `MAP_SHARED` request is still refused (`-ENOSYS`; no write-back path
  exists here).

  needed a small upstream patch.** llama.cpp's own status logger
  (`common/log.cpp`) unconditionally spawns a background `std::thread`
  on the FIRST log call, via `common_log_main()`'s lazily-constructed
  singleton - and the generated completion text ITSELF is printed
  through this same logger (`LOG("%s", token_str.c_str())` in
  `tools/completion/completion.cpp`), not a separate direct-stdout path,
  so this could not be worked around by simply accepting lost log output.

  roadmap's own deliberate non-goal - implementing it would mean a real
  cooperative context-switching scheduler, a vastly disproportionate
  scope expansion for one feature), `std::thread`'s constructor throws
  `std::system_error`, UNCAUGHT, crashing the whole process before

  GAP, not a vlinux issue: a background-logging PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION
  should never be able to crash an otherwise-working program on ANY
  platform where thread creation can fail, not just this one. Fixed with
  a small, targeted patch to `common/log.cpp` (full diff in
  docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 11): catch the `std::thread` construction
  failure in `resume()`, set a `synchronous` flag, and have `add()`
  print immediately instead of queueing for a worker that will never
  run (`pause()` also needed a matching guard, since it unconditionally
  `thrd.join()`s otherwise). This is llama.cpp SOURCE, not vlinux -

  default context, 32768, would need much more memory for no benefit on

     nor `__riscv_zvfbfwma` - GCC's auto-vectorizer lowers that plain
     scalar reduction into a widening e64 vector reduce anyway. Fixed with

     the `optimize` function attribute and `#pragma GCC push_options`,
     both tried and confirmed NOT to suppress the vectorization, objdump-

### Measuring one kernel iteration under hybrid mode

The fast leg above proves correctness; `--mode hybrid` measures real
cycles for one kernel iteration -- a full token would take hours at
vsim's cycle-accurate clock (~9 kHz) even for a model this size, which is
why hybrid mode exists: everything up to the marker runs on the fast
QEMU leg (negligible time), and only the marked region runs on the
cycle-accurate leg.

```sh

  --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
  build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion \
  -- -m models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
     --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
```

This needs `<andesim/ROI.h>` markers inside llama.cpp, bounding ONE
matvec-class operation (not a whole token) -- see `docs/llama_roi_howto.md`
for the exact patch and how the insertion point was chosen. Since ggml
builds its whole computation graph before executing it in one shot,
individual operations are not distinguishable at the application call-site
level (e.g. the per-layer forward-pass code) -- the markers go in ggml's
own generic per-node dispatch loop instead, gated by a counter so only
one specific node's execution is actually measured.

### Measuring one kernel iteration under hybrid mode

The fast leg above proves correctness; `--mode hybrid` measures real
cycles for one kernel iteration -- a full token would take hours at
vsim's cycle-accurate clock (~9 kHz) even for a model this size, which is
why hybrid mode exists: everything up to the marker runs on the fast
QEMU leg (negligible time), and only the marked region runs on the
cycle-accurate leg.

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux --mem-size 2000M \
  --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --step-timeout-ms 900000 \
  build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion \
  -- -m models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
     --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
```

(`--mem-size` stays under 2G -- the AE350 DRAM window's actual usable
ceiling is 2 GiB minus the V-scratch reservation, so `2000M` not `2G`.
`--step-timeout-ms` raises the per-leg spawn timeout past its 90s
default -- a real matmul on the cycle-accurate leg needs minutes; see the
`--step-timeout-ms` line in section 5.)

This needs `<andesim/ROI.h>` markers inside llama.cpp, bounding ONE
matvec-class operation (not a whole token) -- see `docs/llama_roi_howto.md`
for the exact patch and how the insertion point was chosen. Since ggml
builds its whole computation graph before executing it in one shot,
individual operations are not distinguishable at the application call-site
level (e.g. the per-layer forward-pass code) -- the markers go in ggml's
own generic per-node dispatch loop instead, gated by a counter so only
one specific node's execution is actually measured.

Confirmed end to end (2026-07-16): the command above, targeting layer 7's
V-projection matmul (the smallest matmul shape in this architecture --
see `docs/llama_roi_howto.md` for how the target node was chosen and why
the first, larger pick timed out even at 15 minutes), measured
**6528953 cycles**, identical across two independent runs (this hart is
deterministic single-hart, so a stable repeat cycle count is the
correctness signal, the same contract the small matvec fixture above it
already demonstrates). QEMU's hybrid leg enforces the real engine's
ELEN=32 vector-unit limit (unlike fast mode's own unconstrained CPU
string) -- getting a real llama.cpp build through it needed four small,
targeted upstream fixes to `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/{vec.cpp,arch/riscv/quants.c}`,
documented in `docs/llama_roi_howto.md` together with the exact
`ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K` value and the reasoning for picking it.

### 5.10 `--log-level <0-6>` (+ `--log-file`) -- how much andesim says

The same scale as the vsim engines' own `--log-level`, so you learn one
scheme: `0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off`.
Default is `2` (info): you see your program's output, the answer line
(`[andesim] N cycles`), and any warnings or errors -- nothing else.

`--log-level 1` (debug) adds the driver's chatter: the hybrid banner
(engine/VLEN/trigger), the decision lines (which engine and why; what
your `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` resolved to), the shared-mmap line (section
5.4), the window detail (`[andesim] window: trigger=... vsim mcycle=...
qemu mcycle=...`), and the closing PASS line. The level also rides into
both hybrid legs: the vsim engine gets the same `--log-level`, the QEMU
handoff plugin gets `log_level=`, and their stderr streams live to your
terminal (at info and above it is silenced), so one flag tunes the whole
pipeline.

`--log-level 0` (trace) additionally prints, just before each engine
spawns, its fully resolved command line -- the hybrid legs (`[andesim]
exec fast-leg [qemu64]: ...`) and the standalone fast/cycle runs
(`[andesim] exec standalone [qemu64]: ...`) alike. It is the same text
`--dry-run` shows, copy-pasteable to re-run one engine by hand, and it
is emitted BEFORE the spawn, so even a hung run leaves the command in
the log.

`--log-file <file>` appends EVERY level's messages -- timestamped and
level-tagged, regardless of the console `--log-level` -- to `<file>`.
Run once with `--log-file`, attach the file to a bug report, and nothing
needs re-running. Your program's own output is never filtered at any
level.

Related (always on, any level): when a hybrid leg fails, andesim keeps
the run's evidence -- the drained state files, LM sidecars, the staged
QEMU config, a copy of your ELF, and a `manifest.txt` with the error and
every leg's exact command -- under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/` (newest 20
kept) and prints where:

```
[andesim] repro: kept run artifacts at /home/u/.cache/andesim/repro/20260711T081500Z-my_prog (see manifest.txt)
```

### 5.11 `-- <args...>` -- engine passthrough

Everything after a bare `--` is forwarded verbatim to the engine.
`fast`/`cycle` only: those modes run one engine process, so there is an
unambiguous target (see the VLEN example in 5.2). `hybrid` builds both
legs' command lines itself and REJECTS `--` args rather than guessing
which leg you meant -- use the dedicated flags (`--kanata`, `--objdump`,
`--mem-size`, ...) instead.

# Measuring one llama.cpp kernel iteration under andesim hybrid mode

This is the companion doc USER_GUIDE.md section 11 points to: the exact
patch that puts ROI markers around ONE matmul inside llama.cpp, how the
target matmul was chosen, and the upstream `ggml` fixes a real build
needs before it survives the cycle-accurate leg's ELEN=32 vector unit.
Confirmed end to end 2026-07-16: **6528953 cycles**, stable across two
independent hybrid runs.

## 1. Why the marker goes in ggml's dispatch loop, not llama.cpp's model code

`ggml` builds its WHOLE computation graph first (`ggml_mul_mat()` just
appends a node), then executes it in one shot via a generic per-node
dispatch loop (`ggml_graph_compute_thread` -> `ggml_compute_forward`, in
`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c`). Individual ops are not distinguishable
at the call site (e.g. the per-layer forward-pass code in
`src/models/qwen3.cpp` or similar) -- by the time any one op actually
*runs*, you are inside this generic loop, looking at a `ggml_tensor*`
with no easy way to tell "this is layer 7's V projection" apart from any
other `GGML_OP_MUL_MAT` node without counting.

So the marker patch counts nodes and fires on the K-th one:

```c
// ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c, inside ggml_compute_forward's switch:
case GGML_OP_MUL_MAT:
    {
#if defined(__riscv) && defined(ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K)
        static int andesim_mul_mat_n = 0;
        const bool andesim_roi = (++andesim_mul_mat_n == ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K);
        if (andesim_roi) andesim_ROI_begin();
#endif
        ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat(params, tensor);
#if defined(__riscv) && defined(ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K)
        if (andesim_roi) andesim_ROI_end();
#endif
    } break;
```

Also add near the top of the file:

```c
#if defined(__riscv) && defined(ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K)
#include <andesim/ROI.h>
#endif
```

`ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K` is a build-time `-D`, not a source edit -- picking
a different node to measure is a reconfigure, not a patch change (see
section 3). Both markers are HINT NOPs (`andesim_ROI_begin()`/`_end()`),
so this same binary still runs correctly, unmeasured, on any engine or on
silicon when the counter never reaches K (or when `ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K`
is undefined -- the whole block compiles out).

## 2. Counting the nodes

Bonsai-4B (qwen3 architecture, 36 layers, 2560 embd) does 253 `MUL_MAT`
calls per token: 36 layers x 7 matmuls (Q, V, K, O-projection, FFN gate,
up, down -- confirmed via gdb breakpoint counting on a native x86 debug
build, not assumed from the layer count alone) + 1 final `lm_head`.

## 3. Picking K: smallest matmul, not the first one that compiles

The obvious first pick is any early node -- K=50 lands on layer 7's Q
projection (2560 -> 4096). It runs correctly (once the fixes in section 4
are applied) but is too large a computation for the cycle-accurate leg to
finish even inside a 900000ms (15 minute) `--step-timeout-ms` budget.

Rather than guess a smaller K blindly, dump every node's operand shapes
for one real forward pass on a **native x86 build** (fast, no simulator
needed) with a throwaway diagnostic:

```c
// temporary -- not committed; add right before ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat(...):
#if defined(ANDESIM_DUMP_MUL_MAT_SIZES)
{
    const struct ggml_tensor* s0 = tensor->src[0];
    const struct ggml_tensor* s1 = tensor->src[1];
    fprintf(stderr, "ANDESIM_MUL_MAT name=%s src0=%s[%lldx%lld] src1=[%lldx%lld]\n",
            tensor->name, ggml_type_name(s0->type),
            (long long) s0->ne[0], (long long) s0->ne[1],
            (long long) s1->ne[0], (long long) s1->ne[1]);
}
#endif
```

```sh
cmake -B build-host -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-DANDESIM_DUMP_MUL_MAT_SIZES"
cmake --build build-host -j --target llama-completion
./build-host/bin/llama-completion -m models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
  --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 1 -c 512 -t 1 2>&1 | grep ANDESIM_MUL_MAT
```

Result, per layer: Q/O-projection and the FFN gate/up/down matmuls are
all 2560x4096..2560x9728 (the FFN matmuls are actually ~2.4x LARGER than
Q, not smaller -- do not assume "later in the layer means smaller"). The
K/V-projection (2560x1024, this model's grouped-query attention uses
fewer KV heads than Q heads) is the smallest matmul shape anywhere in the
architecture, ~4x fewer MACs than Q, ~9.6x fewer than the FFN matmuls,
and there is nothing smaller available in a standard transformer layer
(the `lm_head` is larger still: `2560 x vocab_size`).

**Verified working value: `ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51`** -- layer 7's V
projection, the very next node after the original K=50 pick. Completes
comfortably inside a 900000ms budget.

If you retarget K, verify the object file actually recompiled with the
new value before spending 10+ minutes on a run that might still be
running the old K:

```sh
python3 -c "
import json
for e in json.load(open('build-rv64-static/compile_commands.json')):
    if e['file'].endswith('ggml-cpu.c'):
        print(e['command']); break
" | grep -o 'ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=[0-9]*'
```

(A stale-ccache-or-incomplete-incremental-rebuild gotcha cost real time
during this investigation: `compile_commands.json` showing the right flag
is necessary but was, once, not sufficient -- the `.o` had not actually
been regenerated. If a rebuild's *behavior* doesn't match what the
*compile command* implies, `rm -f` the exact `.o` path under
`build-rv64-static/ggml/src/CMakeFiles/ggml-cpu.dir/` and rebuild again
before doubting the fix itself.)

## 4. Four fixes a real build needs before the cycle-accurate leg accepts it

Hybrid's QEMU leg is engine-synced (`elen=32`, from the accurate
`-readconfig`) -- unlike fast mode's own hardcoded, unconstrained `-cpu
andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` string, it actually enforces the real engine's
32-bit vector-element limit. A stock `GGML_RVV` build of `ggml` was
written assuming `v` implies the RVV-spec-mandated ELEN>=64 minimum, so
several code paths emit illegal 64-bit-element vector instructions this
target cannot execute. All four were found the same way: run the real
binary, catch the illegal-instruction trap (mcause=2), disassemble at the
exact `mepc`, fix, repeat.

1. **`ggml_vec_dot_f16`/`ggml_vec_dot_bf16`** (`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/vec.cpp`):
   GCC auto-vectorizes their `double`-accumulated scalar fallback loop
   (taken because this build has neither `__riscv_zvfh` nor
   `__riscv_zvfbfwma`) into an illegal widening e64 reduce. Fix: add
   `__attribute__((target("arch=rv64gc")))` to just these two function
   definitions -- confirmed empirically that GCC's RISC-V port honors a
   function-level `target` attribute for suppressing this (the `optimize`
   attribute and `#pragma GCC push_options`/`optimize` do NOT work here --
   tried both, objdump showed no change either time).

2. **`ggml_vec_cvar_f32`/`ggml_vec_soft_max_f32`** (same file): use an
   explicit `vfloat64m1_t` accumulator (`vfwredusum_vs_f32m2_f64m1`,
   widening reduce). Every other architecture's branch in these same two
   functions reduces in native f32 precision with a plain SIMD op, then
   widens ONE scalar partial-sum per chunk to `double` in ordinary C --
   the RISC-V branch was the only outlier, not a hardware requirement.
   Fix: rewrite to match the sibling pattern (`vfredusum_vs_f32m2_f32m1`,
   non-widening, then `sum += (ggml_float) partial` in scalar C). Zero e64,
   same numerics every other build already computes.

3. **`quantize_row_q8_0`/`quantize_row_q8_1`**
   (`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c`): hardcode `vfloat32m8_t`
   (LMUL=8) for `vfabs`/`vfredmax`, unconditionally, unlike every other
   quant kernel in the same file (which dispatch across
   vl1024/vl512/vl256/vl128 variants). `ax45mpv_premium`'s vector FPU
   datapath does not extend to LMUL=8 for floating-point ops specifically
   (a plain integer `vle32.v` load at the same LMUL=8 executes fine
   immediately before the float op faults -- this is FP-datapath-specific,
   not a blanket LMUL cap; correlates with the engine's `isa-vl4` config
   bit, though only vsim's RTL enforces it -- QEMU does not, which is why
   this one surfaces on vsim rather than QEMU1, unlike fixes 1/2/4). Fix:
   both functions now call their existing portable `_ref` scalar
   implementations (`ggml/src/ggml-quants.c`, already used as the non-RVV
   fallback everywhere) unconditionally -- this is activation
   quantization, called once per token row before the (still fully
   vectorized) dot-product loop reuses it, a trivial fraction of total
   matmul cost.

4. **Diagnostic-path gap, not a ggml bug**: `runtime/handler.c`'s trap
   handler (shared by every andesim runtime, vplat and vlinux alike)
   calls `fprintf` then `_exit()`; `_exit()` never flushes stdio, so on a
   fully-buffered stderr (the vlinux syscall-backed stdio path) the whole
   diagnostic was silently lost on every trap. Fixed with an
   `fflush(stderr)` before `_exit()`, plus a raw `htif_uart_putc()`-based
   emergency print of `mcause`/`mepc`/`mtval` before even attempting
   `fprintf` (cheap insurance against a corrupted-state trap taking out
   `fprintf` itself). This is what made fix 3 possible to diagnose in the
   first place -- see `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md`'s U9 section for the full
   trail.

## 5. Reproducing the confirmed run

```sh
# in llama.cpp:
cmake -B build-rv64-static -UGGML_RV_ZVE32F \
  -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -I /path/to/andesim/build/runtime/include" \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -I /path/to/andesim/build/runtime/include"
cmake --build build-rv64-static -j --target llama-completion

# in andesim:

# Measuring one llama.cpp kernel iteration under andesim hybrid mode

This is the companion doc USER_GUIDE.md section 11 points to: the exact
patch that puts ROI markers around ONE matmul inside llama.cpp, how the
target matmul was chosen, and the upstream `ggml` fixes a real build
needs before it survives the cycle-accurate leg's ELEN=32 vector unit.
Confirmed end to end 2026-07-16: **6528953 cycles**, stable across two
independent hybrid runs.

## 1. Why the marker goes in ggml's dispatch loop, not llama.cpp's model code

`ggml` builds its WHOLE computation graph first (`ggml_mul_mat()` just
appends a node), then executes it in one shot via a generic per-node
dispatch loop (`ggml_graph_compute_thread` -> `ggml_compute_forward`, in
`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c`). Individual ops are not distinguishable
at the call site (e.g. the per-layer forward-pass code in
`src/models/qwen3.cpp` or similar) -- by the time any one op actually
*runs*, you are inside this generic loop, looking at a `ggml_tensor*`
with no easy way to tell "this is layer 7's V projection" apart from any
other `GGML_OP_MUL_MAT` node without counting.

So the marker patch counts nodes and fires on the K-th one:

```c
// ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c, inside ggml_compute_forward's switch:
case GGML_OP_MUL_MAT:
    {
#if defined(__riscv) && defined(ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K)
        static int andesim_mul_mat_n = 0;
        const bool andesim_roi = (++andesim_mul_mat_n == ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K);
        if (andesim_roi) andesim_ROI_begin();
#endif
        ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat(params, tensor);
#if defined(__riscv) && defined(ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K)
        if (andesim_roi) andesim_ROI_end();
#endif
    } break;
```

Also add near the top of the file:

```c
#if defined(__riscv) && defined(ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K)
#include <andesim/ROI.h>
#endif
```

`ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K` is a build-time `-D`, not a source edit -- picking
a different node to measure is a reconfigure, not a patch change (see
section 3). Both markers are HINT NOPs (`andesim_ROI_begin()`/`_end()`),
so this same binary still runs correctly, unmeasured, on any engine or on
silicon when the counter never reaches K (or when `ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K`
is undefined -- the whole block compiles out).

## 2. Counting the nodes

Bonsai-4B (qwen3 architecture, 36 layers, 2560 embd) does 253 `MUL_MAT`
calls per token: 36 layers x 7 matmuls (Q, V, K, O-projection, FFN gate,
up, down -- confirmed via gdb breakpoint counting on a native x86 debug
build, not assumed from the layer count alone) + 1 final `lm_head`.

## 3. Picking K: smallest matmul, not the first one that compiles

The obvious first pick is any early node -- K=50 lands on layer 7's Q
projection (2560 -> 4096). It runs correctly (once the fixes in section 4
are applied) but is too large a computation for the cycle-accurate leg to
finish even inside a 900000ms (15 minute) `--step-timeout-ms` budget.

Rather than guess a smaller K blindly, dump every node's operand shapes
for one real forward pass on a **native x86 build** (fast, no simulator
needed) with a throwaway diagnostic:

```c
// temporary -- not committed; add right before ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat(...):
#if defined(ANDESIM_DUMP_MUL_MAT_SIZES)
{
    const struct ggml_tensor* s0 = tensor->src[0];
    const struct ggml_tensor* s1 = tensor->src[1];
    fprintf(stderr, "ANDESIM_MUL_MAT name=%s src0=%s[%lldx%lld] src1=[%lldx%lld]\n",
            tensor->name, ggml_type_name(s0->type),
            (long long) s0->ne[0], (long long) s0->ne[1],
            (long long) s1->ne[0], (long long) s1->ne[1]);
}
#endif
```

```sh
cmake -B build-host -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-DANDESIM_DUMP_MUL_MAT_SIZES"
cmake --build build-host -j --target llama-completion
./build-host/bin/llama-completion -m models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
  --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 1 -c 512 -t 1 2>&1 | grep ANDESIM_MUL_MAT
```

Result, per layer: Q/O-projection and the FFN gate/up/down matmuls are
all 2560x4096..2560x9728 (the FFN matmuls are actually ~2.4x LARGER than
Q, not smaller -- do not assume "later in the layer means smaller"). The
K/V-projection (2560x1024, this model's grouped-query attention uses
fewer KV heads than Q heads) is the smallest matmul shape anywhere in the
architecture, ~4x fewer MACs than Q, ~9.6x fewer than the FFN matmuls,
and there is nothing smaller available in a standard transformer layer
(the `lm_head` is larger still: `2560 x vocab_size`).

**Verified working value: `ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51`** -- layer 7's V
projection, the very next node after the original K=50 pick. Completes
comfortably inside a 900000ms budget.

If you retarget K, verify the object file actually recompiled with the
new value before spending 10+ minutes on a run that might still be
running the old K:

```sh
python3 -c "
import json
for e in json.load(open('build-rv64-static/compile_commands.json')):
    if e['file'].endswith('ggml-cpu.c'):
        print(e['command']); break
" | grep -o 'ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=[0-9]*'
```

(A stale-ccache-or-incomplete-incremental-rebuild gotcha cost real time
during this investigation: `compile_commands.json` showing the right flag
is necessary but was, once, not sufficient -- the `.o` had not actually
been regenerated. If a rebuild's *behavior* doesn't match what the
*compile command* implies, `rm -f` the exact `.o` path under
`build-rv64-static/ggml/src/CMakeFiles/ggml-cpu.dir/` and rebuild again
before doubting the fix itself.)

## 4. Four fixes a real build needs before the cycle-accurate leg accepts it

Hybrid's QEMU leg is engine-synced (`elen=32`, from the accurate
`-readconfig`) -- unlike fast mode's own hardcoded, unconstrained `-cpu
andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` string, it actually enforces the real engine's
32-bit vector-element limit. A stock `GGML_RVV` build of `ggml` was
written assuming `v` implies the RVV-spec-mandated ELEN>=64 minimum, so
several code paths emit illegal 64-bit-element vector instructions this
target cannot execute. All four were found the same way: run the real
binary, catch the illegal-instruction trap (mcause=2), disassemble at the
exact `mepc`, fix, repeat.

1. **`ggml_vec_dot_f16`/`ggml_vec_dot_bf16`** (`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/vec.cpp`):
   GCC auto-vectorizes their `double`-accumulated scalar fallback loop
   (taken because this build has neither `__riscv_zvfh` nor
   `__riscv_zvfbfwma`) into an illegal widening e64 reduce. Fix: add
   `__attribute__((target("arch=rv64gc")))` to just these two function
   definitions -- confirmed empirically that GCC's RISC-V port honors a
   function-level `target` attribute for suppressing this (the `optimize`
   attribute and `#pragma GCC push_options`/`optimize` do NOT work here --
   tried both, objdump showed no change either time).

2. **`ggml_vec_cvar_f32`/`ggml_vec_soft_max_f32`** (same file): use an
   explicit `vfloat64m1_t` accumulator (`vfwredusum_vs_f32m2_f64m1`,
   widening reduce). Every other architecture's branch in these same two
   functions reduces in native f32 precision with a plain SIMD op, then
   widens ONE scalar partial-sum per chunk to `double` in ordinary C --
   the RISC-V branch was the only outlier, not a hardware requirement.
   Fix: rewrite to match the sibling pattern (`vfredusum_vs_f32m2_f32m1`,
   non-widening, then `sum += (ggml_float) partial` in scalar C). Zero e64,
   same numerics every other build already computes.

3. **`quantize_row_q8_0`/`quantize_row_q8_1`**
   (`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c`): hardcode `vfloat32m8_t`
   (LMUL=8) for `vfabs`/`vfredmax`, unconditionally, unlike every other
   quant kernel in the same file (which dispatch across
   vl1024/vl512/vl256/vl128 variants). `ax45mpv_premium`'s vector FPU
   datapath does not extend to LMUL=8 for floating-point ops specifically
   (a plain integer `vle32.v` load at the same LMUL=8 executes fine
   immediately before the float op faults -- this is FP-datapath-specific,
   not a blanket LMUL cap; correlates with the engine's `isa-vl4` config
   bit, though only vsim's RTL enforces it -- QEMU does not, which is why
   this one surfaces on vsim rather than QEMU1, unlike fixes 1/2/4). Fix:
   both functions now call their existing portable `_ref` scalar
   implementations (`ggml/src/ggml-quants.c`, already used as the non-RVV
   fallback everywhere) unconditionally -- this is activation
   quantization, called once per token row before the (still fully
   vectorized) dot-product loop reuses it, a trivial fraction of total
   matmul cost.

4. **Diagnostic-path gap, not a ggml bug**: `runtime/handler.c`'s trap
   handler (shared by every andesim runtime, vplat and vlinux alike)
   calls `fprintf` then `_exit()`; `_exit()` never flushes stdio, so on a
   fully-buffered stderr (the vlinux syscall-backed stdio path) the whole
   diagnostic was silently lost on every trap. Fixed with an
   `fflush(stderr)` before `_exit()`, plus a raw `htif_uart_putc()`-based
   emergency print of `mcause`/`mepc`/`mtval` before even attempting
   `fprintf` (cheap insurance against a corrupted-state trap taking out
   `fprintf` itself). This is what made fix 3 possible to diagnose in the
   first place -- see `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md`'s U9 section for the full
   trail.

## 5. Reproducing the confirmed run

```sh
# in llama.cpp:
cmake -B build-rv64-static -UGGML_RV_ZVE32F \
  -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -I /path/to/andesim/build/runtime/include" \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -I /path/to/andesim/build/runtime/include"
cmake --build build-rv64-static -j --target llama-completion

# in andesim:
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux --mem-size 2000M \
  --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --step-timeout-ms 900000 \
  /path/to/llama.cpp/build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion \
  -- -m /path/to/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
     --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
```

Expected: `[andesim] 6528953 cycles`, identical across repeat runs.

142	  `__global_pointer$` before running the C handler, so any gp-relative

`/home/nick/work/andesim/ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md` tracks building `vlinux`
(a new M-mode proxy kernel, `runtime/linux/`, pattern: riscv-pk) so a static
glibc RISC-V binary can run unmodified on all 3 andesim modes (fast/cycle/hybrid),
with hybrid producing a cycle-accurate measurement of ONE kernel iteration.

Primary target as of 2026-07-15: `llama-completion` (llama.cpp's text-gen CLI)
generating text from `Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf` (572 MB, fits the 2 GiB DRAM window
directly). This replaced the original target (`llama-bench` + `Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf`,
3.8 GB) per the user's explicit pivot ("goal revised to run llama-completion
Bonsai-4B model"). See [[llama-cpp-riscv-checkout]] for the supporting
cross-build/model facts this pivot is grounded in.

**Why the pivot**: llama-completion produces visible, checkable generated text
(a real demo) instead of a benchmark table, and Bonsai-4B sidesteps the 2 GiB
DRAM ceiling entirely, so the two features that existed only to work around
that ceiling for 27B (U10: DRAM window >= 6 GB, U11: GGUF layer-slice script)
are no longer on the critical path - they're kept in the roadmap as an
explicitly optional 27B stretch-goal track, not deleted.

## Feature state (one feature per session, per CLAUDE.md)
- U0 (extract `runtime/htif_client.{c,h}` out of `vplat_syscalls.c`, structural
  no-behavior-change refactor so vplat and vlinux share the HTIF window client):
  **DONE** 2026-07-15. All 12 `tests/vplat/*.sh` green before and after.
- U1 (vlinux skeleton: boot, banner, manifest reader): **DONE** 2026-07-15.
  `runtime/linux/{manifest.h,main.c,vlinux.ld,Makefile}` +
  `tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_boot.sh` + `scripts/build_all.sh` `vlinux` target.
  Key design call: no new crt.S - `runtime/crt0.S` (shared with vplat) is
  link-address-agnostic (PC-relative + linker-provided `_stack` symbol), so
  vlinux.ld just retargets it to base 0x0200_0000 with zero new asm. Confirmed
  by research that QEMU's `-bios` (MROM trampoline) and vsim's direct
  `reset_vector` pin both boot from the ELF's own e_entry - no boot stub
  needed. Test runs vlinux.elf as a plain standalone ELF (no --runtime flag
  yet, that's U2).
- U2 (driver `--runtime linux` plumbing): **DONE** 2026-07-15.
  `driver/{manifest.hpp,manifest.cpp,tempdir.hpp,tempdir.cpp}` (new),
  `--runtime` added to `Cli` (cli.hpp/cli.cpp), `run_fast`/`run_standalone`
  wiring in cmd_run.cpp, `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_runtime_linux.sh`,
  docs/USER_GUIDE.md 5.12. `andesim run --mode fast --runtime linux app.elf`
  stages a private `vlinux-run.elf` copy (objcopy --update-section .manifest=
  with app path + mem_size) and boots THAT via -bios instead of the app
  directly. Three scope cuts, each documented in the roadmap's U2 DONE note:

  (hybrid wiring is U9; nothing on the critical path before U9 needs it, per
  the roadmap's own Order line); (2) **argv/envp deferred to U3** - `--
  <args...>` parses (matches the roadmap's example invocation) but is
  warned-and-dropped, not forwarded to QEMU's CLI (would be misparsed as
  engine flags) and not yet written into the manifest - no wire format was
  invented without U3's loader to validate it against; (3) **staged
  vlinux-run.elf is not cleaned up** - fast's exec_passthrough execve()s and

  demands it yet). Also: `--mem-size` defaults to 1G under `--runtime linux`;

  initializer, since nothing in the visible program ever writes it (the
  objcopy patch is invisible to the compiler). This will bite again if a
  future manifest field is added without the same qualifier. (2) code

  load backdoor) needs an explicit `fence.i` before being executed, on any
  cache-modeling engine (the real RTL) - QEMU's cacheless functional model
  silently masks a missing fence.i, so this class of bug ONLY surfaces on
  the cycle leg, never fast. Both bugs were caught by running the SAME test

  cycle didn't, and the diff was the tell.

  `libpython3.10.so.1.0`/`PYTHONHOME` point at a workspace that's gone),
  which is what would be needed to inspect the actual riscv64
  registration site live. This is a vendor-toolchain-internals question,
  not a vlinux bug - full details and next steps are in the roadmap's U4
  DONE note. `test_vlinux_glibc_hello.sh` accepts a clean exit 42 OR this
  EXACT crash signature (stdout already fully correct at that point) -
  any other outcome still fails the test.

  Decision point: I asked the user how to proceed (keep digging / try to
  fix the target gdb / accept the documented gap and move on) and got no
  response within the session: proceeded with the recommended default
  (document thoroughly, mark U4 done, let U5+ continue since none of them
  depend on exit() working). Revisit if the user wants this pursued
  further - the next concrete step is a working riscv64 gdb (repair the
  toolchain's python linkage or build/find an alternate one) to break on
  the actual `__cxa_atexit`/`_dl_fini` registration site.

  the SAME fast-passes/cycle-differs-or-both-differ-from-expected
  pattern): (1) **`gp` not reloaded on trap entry** - `trap.S` saved/
  restored gp around a trap but never reloaded it to vlinux's OWN
  `__global_pointer$` before running the C handler, so any gp-relative

  with the same `.option norelax`/`lla gp,__global_pointer$` sequence
  crt0.S already uses, inserted into `m_trap_entry` before `call
  handle_trap`. (2) **mmap arena start overlapped the live app stack** -
  `stack.c` started building the initial stack AT `mem_size -
  STACK_RESERVE` (meant to be the arena's FLOOR) instead of AT `mem_size`
  (the true top, with 8 MiB as headroom below) - the build's own content
  immediately spilled below the intended floor, so the first big `mmap()`
  (malloc's 1 MiB request) zeroed part of the app's own already-live
  stack. Fixed by starting the build at `mem_size`.
- U5 (File I/O syscall set): **DONE** 2026-07-15. `syscall.c` grown with
  openat/close/read/pread64/lseek/fstat/fstatat/statx/faccessat/getcwd
  (readlinkat/getdents64 are deliberate silent stubs, -EINVAL/-ENOSYS) +
  `tests/fixtures/rt_linux_file.c` + `tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_file.sh`.
  Verified fast+cycle: real glibc fopen/fread/fseek/ftell plus direct
  syscall() probes for the rest of the set all correct.

  Two ABI-translation facts, verified against LINUX_TOOLCHAIN's own
  sysroot headers (not assumed): (1) the HTIF host's open/openat handlers
  speak NEWLIB's O_* flag bits, not Linux's (only the low 2 access-mode
  bits agree - O_CREAT is 0x40 in Linux vs 0x200 in newlib) - a static
  glibc app's flags need translating at the syscall boundary

  handlers fill exactly 2 fixed byte offsets (st_mode u32@+4, st_size
  u64@+16) in whatever buffer they're given - NOT a whole-struct bounce,
  and those offsets match newlib's struct stat (what vplat relies on) but
  NOT Linux riscv64's struct stat (mode@+16, size@+48) or struct statx at
  all - vlinux must construct the real Linux-shaped struct from those 2
  host-given fields, zeroing/reasonable-defaulting the rest.

  HW contract" bug class** (see U3's fence.i, U4's gp-reload): the first
  cut read st_mode via `htif_win_load(&m, woff+4, 4)` - htif_client.h
  documents this primitive as u64-load-only with an 8-ALIGNED woff
  requirement (it dereferences a `uint64_t*`); QEMU's byte-addressable
  MMIO silently tolerated the misaligned 4-byte read and returned the
  right bytes anyway (fast passed outright), but the cycle-accurate
  engine's real uncached-device bus logic faulted (mcause=5 load access
  fault, mtval pointing exactly at the misaligned window address). Fixed
  by loading a whole 8-aligned 24-byte block and extracting fields
  locally via little-endian shifts. Worth watching for again: any new
  HTIF/DMI-adjacent code that reads/writes sub-8-byte or misaligned
  chunks of a window/register interface will pass on fast and fault only
  on cycle - always test both legs, never trust fast alone for this class
  of code.

  clock_gettime/clock_getres (backed by the existing VH_SYS_GETTIMEOFDAY
  host clock)/nanosleep/clock_nanosleep (immediate 0, no timer exists) +
  `tests/fixtures/rt_linux_time.c` + `tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_time.sh`.
  CLOCK_MONOTONIC is synthesized (no dedicated host primitive) as elapsed
  time since the process's first monotonic query, a lazily-captured
  static baseline - never goes backward, the guarantee that matters.
  Non-bug lesson: the roadmap's own "10M-loop" test figure assumed the
  fast leg; on cycle (~8.7kHz, -O0) that hung past the 600s timeout with
  zero output (not a crash - just never finished) on top of the ~7min
  glibc-startup baseline. Shrunk to 10K iterations with zero loss of
  verification power (the real contract is "delta >= 0", independent of
  loop size). Worth remembering for any future fixture sized for fast
  that also runs on cycle.
- U7 (File-backed private mmap): **DONE** 2026-07-15. `mm.c` grew a
  MAP_PRIVATE file-backed branch of `sys_mmap` (arena-allocate + eager
  `htif_pread` into it - a private owned copy) + `sys_mremap` (always
  -ENOMEM) + `tests/fixtures/rt_linux_mmap.c` + `test_vlinux_mmap.sh`.

  unmapping any range including a partial/tail one (llama.cpp's own
  pattern), so the existing U4-era always-succeeds no-op already answers
  it correctly; a "region table" turned out to be unneeded once that was
  checked, not a shortcut.

  seek-read-restore logic out of syscall.c into a new shared
  `htif_pread()` primitive in `htif_client.{h,c}` (parallel to the
  existing htif_read/htif_write) - both pread64 and the new mmap path
  need it, and reaching across files for a `static` function would have
  been the wrong alternative to sharing it properly.

  also runs on, not just fast" lesson (U6 was first): a 256 KB test file
  (~258 window round trips) hung past 600s with zero output; rather than
  guess, ran a direct 4 KB diagnostic first - it completed in 435s,
  matching the established ~7min baseline almost exactly, confirming the
  mmap code itself was correct and this was purely a timeout-budget
  question. Settled on 16 KB (~9 round trips each way) + 900s timeout.
  General lesson solidifying across U6/U7: when a new cycle-leg fixture
  times out with NO crash trace and NO output at all (unlike the U3/U4/U5
  bug class, which always produces a distinct fault signature), suspect
  a data-size/timeout budget problem first, and confirm it FAST with a
  much-smaller diagnostic input before assuming a real bug or blindly
  bumping the timeout.

  goal itself. Real static-glibc `llama-completion` correctly generates
  "The capital of France is Paris." from Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf under
  `--runtime linux` fast, verified at both `-n 4` and the roadmap's own
  `-n 32`. Full details in the roadmap's U8 DONE note (long - covers 5
  distinct sub-findings). Highlights:
  - **Argv threading** (U2/U3's deferred prerequisite, implemented as
    direct U8 scope, not a separate feature): manifest v2 adds a flat
    NUL-separated `argv_extra_buf`+count (64 args / 4096 bytes max);

    into stage_linux_runtime"; stack.c builds a real multi-entry argv[].

    16-aligned only for ODD argc - true by COINCIDENCE for U1-U7's
    argc==1 only. Fixed by computing block size from real argc + an
    8-byte pad word when needed. Verified DIRECTLY with an even argc on
    BOTH fast and cycle (not trusted from the math alone) - the
    established "never trust an alignment change from fast alone" habit
    ([[fast-leg-permissive-cycle-enforces-hw-contract]]) paid off again.
  - **New syscalls, all found via the real binary** (`--help` then real
    model), same closed-loop process as U4's riscv_hwprobe: `futex`(98)
    - even at `-t 1`, glibc's OWN internal locking (malloc arena,
    static-init guards) uses it pervasively, not just explicit
    threading, contradicting the roadmap's own too-optimistic "-t 1:
    uncontended mutexes never reach futex" note; answered `0`
    unconditionally (spec-legal spurious-wake tolerance, safe because a
    single-hart system can never have real contention). `sysinfo`(179),
    `fadvise64`(223), `madvise`(233): straightforward, hint/no-op style.
  - **A real bug from an unverified roadmap assumption**: U7's own
    description said llama.cpp uses `MAP_PRIVATE` for its GGUF mmap;
    the REAL source (`llama-mmap.cpp`) uses `MAP_SHARED`. Caught
    immediately by running the real binary, not by re-reading roadmap
    text more carefully - a concrete instance of "verify against source,
    not against a prior design note." Fixed correctly (not permissively):
    MAP_SHARED without PROT_WRITE is OBSERVABLY IDENTICAL to MAP_PRIVATE
    for a mapping nothing ever writes through.
  - **A genuine cross-repo change**: llama.cpp's async status logger
    (`common/log.cpp`) unconditionally spawns a `std::thread` on the
    FIRST log call - and the GENERATED COMPLETION TEXT ITSELF prints
    through this same logger, not a separate path, so losing it was not
    an option. Since `clone` is `ENOSYS` (real threading is the
    roadmap's deliberate non-goal - a full cooperative scheduler would
    be a wildly disproportionate scope expansion), the thread
    constructor throws uncaught, crashing before main() runs. Root-caused
    as a genuine llama.cpp robustness gap (crashing on a failed
    PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION is bad on any platform), not a vlinux
    issue - fixed with a small patch (full diff in
    docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 11) making the logger fall back to
    synchronous printing when thread creation fails. This patch lives in
    `/home/nick/work/llama.cpp` (untracked by the andesim repo) -
    anyone rebuilding from a fresh checkout must re-apply it.
  - **Memory sizing**: the roadmap's own "1G covers it" estimate was
    wrong (didn't account for the KV cache buffer, 576 MB at `-c 512`,
    on top of the 572 MB model mmap) - found by an actual OOM failure,
    not assumed. `--mem-size 2G -c 512` is the verified-working config.
  - Perf data point (this host, functional QEMU, not cycle-accurate):
    load ~93s, prompt eval ~165s/5 tokens, generation ~36.6s/token - a

    emulation by design, which is exactly why U9 measures ONE kernel
    iteration, not a whole token.
